text:
An interesting article on Indo China by Lt Gen Abhay Krishna, PVSM, UYSM, AVSM, SM(G), VSM, ADC, (Retd) Former Army Commander of South Western, Eastern and Central Army Commands of Indian Army.

Beyond the LAC: India’s Strategic Contest With China in the Himalayas

From Doklam to Galwan: The Changing Rules of Border Competition

Post-Doklam and Galwan clashes, it was very clear that the Line of Actual Control was no longer merely a disputed frontier marked by competing maps and patrols, but now it’s a permanent contest of infrastructure, surveillance, military readiness, diplomacy, and national resilience. From Doklam to Galwan, India has learned that the central challenge from China is not always a dramatic assault across the Himalayas, but it’s the gradual alteration of facts on the ground, which is often below the threshold of open war.

The latest phase of India-China engagement offers cautious reasons for optimism. We know that at the 25th round of Special Representatives talks held in Beijing on 25 August 2026, India and China had agreed on an eight-point consensus covering border management, military communication, boundary negotiations, trans-border rivers, trade and pilgrimage. Yet the agreement is best understood only as a mechanism for managing rivalry and not as proof that the rivalry has ended.

The Doklam confrontation in 2017 had clearly demonstrated that a local dispute in the Bhutan-China-India trijunction could acquire wider consequences because of its proximity to the Siliguri Corridor, which is the narrow land link connecting India’s North-Eastern states with the rest of the country. Thus, India’s decision to physically block the Chinese road construction through Bhutan reflected a clear strategic calculation and a strong stand.

Doklam had clearly exposed the changing character of Chinese border strategy. Infrastructure was not simply a civilian development tool. Roads, tracks, communications networks, and permanent settlements are clearly aimed at improving the PLA’s ability to reinforce contested areas rapidly and sustain itself, dominating the local tactical environment.

Then the crisis in Eastern Ladakh in 2020 made this lesson far more urgent. The Galwan Valley clash in which soldiers from both sides were killed actually destroyed the assumption that earlier confidence-building arrangements alone could preserve peace. The subsequent military face-off brought large-scale troop deployments, including armor, artillery, air power and logistical mobilization to a frontier which was previously managed through patrolling protocols and political restraint. Galwan was, therefore, more than a violent incident. It marked the end of an era where India could no longer assume that economic engagement or diplomatic dialogue would automatically prevent coercive military pressure. The relationship had entered a phase in which peace required credible preparedness.

Sikkim and the Siliguri Corridor: The Strategic Stakes of a Changing Frontier
The Sikkim sector illustrates how this strategic competition is evolving even without a major ground crisis. Historically, parts of this sector were regarded as comparatively stable because the alignment was more clearly understood than in Western Arunachal Pradesh or Eastern Ladakh.

Now that relative stability has weakened because Chinese infrastructure development in Tibet has evidently compressed India’s reaction time. All-weather roads, upgraded airfields, rail extensions towards Nyingchi and the development of “Xiaokang” villages have created a network capable of supporting rapid reinforcement and sustained presence. These settlements combine civilian development with surveillance, communications and logistical functions reflecting a broader civil-military fusion approach. Thus, the result is that in this frontier the distinction between civilian and military infrastructure is increasingly blurred. A village may support population settlement, administrative control and political messaging but also function as a logistical node. A road may be presented as developmental but it retains immediate military utility. This is a strategic competition by construction.

Repeated incidents at locations such as Naku La have also changed the operational atmosphere. Temporary patrol confrontations are now occurring against the background of larger forward deployments, enhanced surveillance and pre-positioned supplies. The danger lies not only in deliberate escalation but also in miscalculation because a patrol encounter can become politically significant when both militaries are operating at heightened alert.

For India, the Sikkim sector is inseparable from the security of the Siliguri Corridor. This, therefore, makes it likely to remain a zone of structured friction, even if both sides avoid a major confrontation in the future.

Infrastructure as Deterrence: India’s Response along the Northern Frontier
India’s ground position today is, however, considerably stronger than it was before Doklam. The most important change has been the accelerated construction of roads, bridges, landing grounds, communication systems and logistics facilities along the northern frontier. Project Swastik has expanded connectivity in Sikkim, including 1412 km of roads and around 80 major bridges. The Chungthang–Lachen axis and the Taram Chu Bridge, which was recently inaugurated after restoration on 26 February 2026, are especially important because they support year-round movement in terrain where winter and monsoon conditions can otherwise isolate the forward areas.

Though China has the geographical advantages on the Tibetan plateau, our infrastructure development reduces the time required for Indian forces to reinforce threatened sectors. So, in military terms, the objective is not merely to reach the frontier, but to sustain combat power there.

This is a significant shift in India’s strategic posture. Strangely, earlier the border infrastructure was often constrained by concerns that improved roads might help the potential adversary. However, after Doklam, followed by the Galwan clash, that caution prevailing in the mindset gave way to urgency. India now recognises that poor connectivity creates vulnerability regardless of whether a crisis occurs.

Thus, while diplomacy worked to reduce immediate tensions, India accelerated its border infrastructure programme to ensure that any future crisis would be met from a position of greater strength. The strategic lesson after 2020 was clear that connectivity is not just developmental but, in reality, it is the core element of deterrence.

By 2024, the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) is known to have completed 111 infrastructure projects at a cost of around ₹3,751 crore. The Union Budget for 2025–26 allocated ₹7,146.50 crore to the BRO, marking a nearly 10 percent increase from the previous year’s estimates. This funding supports the construction and maintenance of roads, bridges and tunnels in difficult terrain along the northern frontier.

In Eastern Ladakh, the Durbuk-Shyok-Daulat Beg Oldi (DS-DBO) road is particularly significant. It runs close to the LAC and provides critical connectivity to India’s northernmost posts, including Daulat Beg Oldi, which is strategically important because of its proximity to the Karakoram Pass and the Depsang sector. Improved road access reduces the time required to move troops, equipment and supplies to forward areas, thereby enhancing operational flexibility.

Tunnels are a key component of India’s infrastructure strategy because they ensure all-weather connectivity in regions where snow, landslides and extreme weather can otherwise isolate forward areas for months. In December 2025, our Defence Minister inaugurated 125 BRO projects, including the Shyok Tunnel on the DS-DBO road in Eastern Ladakh. The strategic effect is twofold. First, it reduces India’s vulnerability to seasonal disruptions that an adversary could potentially exploit. Second, it signals that India can sustain a prolonged presence and, if necessary, a prolonged confrontation along the LAC.

Beyond roads and tunnels, India has invested in bridges, airfields, helipads and logistics nodes along the northern border. In Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh, new bridges and upgraded roads have improved connectivity to forward areas, mirroring the effort in Ladakh. Advanced landing grounds and helipads enable rapid airlift of troops, casualties and supplies, while improved logistics bases allow for better stockpiling of fuel, ammunition and other essentials.

Infrastructure is only one part of the equation. India is also upgrading surveillance, communications and electronic warfare capabilities along the LAC. This includes space-based surveillance, unmanned aerial systems, ground-based radars and secure communication networks. The objective is to improve situational awareness, detect intrusions earlier and coordinate responses more effectively across the Army, Air Force and paramilitary forces.

India’s air infrastructure improvements along the northern frontier have been substantial with the upgradation of forward airfields like Daulat Beg Oldi (DBO), Nyoma, Fukche and Thoise in Ladakh. These have been modernised with extended runways, hardened shelters, fuel storage and all-weather operational capabilities. These improvements, therefore, now allow India to deploy fighter aircraft, transport planes and helicopters closer to the LAC. However, significant challenges still remain and miles yet to be covered.

China’s advantages in altitude, infrastructure density and aircraft numbers mean that India must continue to invest heavily not only in air-power modernisation and infrastructure development to maintain a credible deterrent posture in this region but also in parallel, build a strong naval force to dominate the Indian Ocean Region from where the bulk of China’s trade passes through. Creating a Maritime Theatre Command, therefore, should be a priority over other theatre commands.

Disengagement Without Resolution:  The Unfinished Contest Along the LAC
The disengagement agreements at Depsang and Demchok in October 2024 did not end the India-China border dispute but they did alter the military and political dynamics along the LAC in Eastern Ladakh. After more than four years of a tense standoff that began in 2020, these agreements restored patrolling access to traditional areas, reduced the immediate risk of accidental clashes and created a narrow window for diplomatic repair.

The removal of “blocking positions” reduced the day-to-day friction that had characterised the standoff. It also lowered the probability that a routine patrol encounter would escalate into a larger crisis. Post this agreement, the Defence Ministry described the LAC situation as “stable but sensitive,” acknowledging that the underlying dispute and strategic competition persisted even as specific flashpoints are managed.

At the same time, the disengagement agreements underscored that stability now depended less on trust and more on verified arrangements, infrastructure and deterrence. At the LAC, therefore, we strongly believe that restraint and strength are not opposites but they are the two halves of credible deterrence.

The LAC has now turned into a multi-domain battlefield. China’s pressure is not limited to troop movements or physical intrusions but also includes cartographic claims and administrative renaming, besides cyber operations, electronic interference, information warfare, economic coercion and what our late General Bipin Rawat, the CDS then, had described as “salami slicing.” Cartographic aggression in Arunachal Pradesh is part of this wider effort. Maps, official names and administrative claims seek to normalise a political narrative in which disputed territory is gradually presented as settled Chinese space. Such actions may appear symbolic but they are intended to influence international perceptions and future negotiations.

Recently, China objected to our renaming of a few places in Ladakh, claiming them as its territory. Well, the world at large must ask China whether Tibet is historically its territory or was annexed by the CPC with the help of its PLA. India must, therefore, defend not only territory but also the information environment surrounding that territory.

The LAC will remain contested because the underlying boundary dispute has not been resolved and because China’s infrastructure-led strategy continues to generate pressure. Yet, India is better prepared now to hit back than it was over a decade ago. Post-Doklam and Galwan clashes, India stands in a harder but more realistic position. It is no longer relying on the hope that unresolved differences can be insulated from the wider relationship. India is also not seeking confrontation for its own sake. India’s approach is increasingly one of calibrated firmness, that is, maintain dialogue, preserve military readiness, improve border infrastructure and resist unilateral attempts to alter the status quo.

The Long Game in the Himalayas: China’s Strategic Footprint and India’s Response
We must see from a wider prism that China’s infrastructure development along the LAC is not merely a developmental programme. It is a deliberate, multi-domain strategy designed to reshape the Himalayan frontier in ways that enhance Beijing’s military reach, consolidate territorial claims and create long-term leverage over India. China’s plans against India have been planned and implemented at various layerssince over several decades. From Theaterisation of Forces, large scale infrastructure developments to include roads and railways to airfields, dams and “Xiaokang” border villages, China has been transforming the Tibetan plateau into a forward operating base capable of sustaining prolonged military presence and rapid escalation. Approximately 72 per cent of these villages are located near the LAC in India’s North-Eastern sector with 90 per cent of those facing Arunachal Pradesh. Smaller clusters exist in sectors facing Sikkim, Uttarakhand and https://t.co/BDniMCQR7Q this entire range of activities, China has cleverly and quietly taken a lead of at least 15-20 years.

China is currently rapidly relocating the Tibetan population into frontier settlements under its border-village and poverty-alleviation programmes. Official figures cited by researchers indicate that 241,835 people were “involved” in the TAR border-village programme, while reports also refer to plans to move tens of thousands of border residents into 628 villages. For India, the danger is not that Tibetan civilians will suddenly “march across” the LAC but it is subtler, that is, a state-sponsored population architecture that entrenches Chinese control opposite Arunachal Pradesh compressing India’s strategic depth and making future incursions look like routine local administration.

India’s Response
India’s response, though delayed earlier, has, however, seen significant progress and implementation post-2014, for which the current dispensation must be credited. Government attention in terms of planning, resource outlay, and project implementation towards Theaterisation and modernization of Defense Forces for a robust response across high-altitude-based Northern borders, as well as focused infrastructure development, is appreciable. A similar planned push and implementation is required in developing and establishing our own Border villages all along the LAC. This is a challenge in a democratic setup since it involves convincing groups of people to move ahead, set up a daily routine, and remain permanently established. This requires pre-planned and implemented essential logistical support, electricity, roads, and sustainable daily essential supplies to such new villages. However, continuous government-monitored support, which is feasible to be implemented by the current Nationalistic govt, is a prerequisite. Identifying such village locations to extend our ‘civilian reach’ closer to the LAC with concerned State Govts of Arunachal, Sikkim, Uttarakhand, HP, Ladakh and rolling out an actionable plan with clear timelines and phases with committed financial outlays is an urgency and way forward.

Finally
India has already seen in the North-East how porous borders, ethnic linkages and weak documentation can produce decades-long demographic and security pressure. Migration from Myanmar, especially Chin-State movement into Mizoram, has continued since the 1960s. The 2021 Myanmar coup intensified the flow and it is estimated that nearly 70,000 refugees entered India after the coup, including more than 40,000 in Mizoram and over 8,000 in Manipur. These movements have strained local resources, identity politics, administration and border management.

The lesson is clear that demographic change at a frontier rarely arrives as an invasion. It slowly accumulates through displacement, kinship networks, economic necessity, weak enforcement and political vacuums until it becomes a permanent strategic reality.

Thus, by resettling the Tibetan population close to the LAC across Arunachal Pradesh, China is attempting to make the LAC look less like a disputed line and more like an ordinary Chinese provincial frontier populated, connected, policed and defensible. The hidden long-term agenda of China is to infuse demographic invasion into Arunachal Pradesh over a few decades and gradually influence the hearts and minds of our young, coming-up generation there to begin to feel that they are more Tibetan than Indian.

On October 24, I had the privilege of participating in the Garden of Innocence service at Mountain View Cemetery in Fresno.

We remembered four little children: Kevin, Daniel, Alana, and Milagro Jane.

We know very little about their stories. Their bodies had gone unclaimed. But a community gathered to speak their names, offer prayers, and honor the dignity that was theirs from the beginning.

My message centered on the psalmist’s cry: “No man cared for my soul.”

Who cares? God cares. And every carefully prepared detail, every poem, and every person gathered there gave expression to that care.

We prayed for their birth families, too, asking for mercy and healing amid circumstances we cannot fully know.

I have participated in these services for years, and they continue to move me. I see mourning and grace in the eyes of the people who come. I see a reflection of God’s love in their care.

text:
Your insincerity aside, this is a good question.

Towns want economic investment and prosperity, but not the kind being offered. Similarly, developers want opportunity, but not the kind on the table. Then there are the intermediate layers between the parties that further impede development.

If your town is fighting development, that is often not a policy set by the city council, but the work of a few bureaucrats and staffers at the DOB, DEP, or some other alphabet-soup municipal agency that gets in the way. Odds are your fire Marshall is on his third design review of a structure less likely to burn than the town pool.  Staffers interpret the code literally and would rather pass approval responsibility along or say no than assume responsibility themselves. Meanwhile, political leadership has little ability to instruct these bureaucrats to approve things and the bureaucrats don't get voted out. 

At the same time, capital incentives have shifted from long-term, cash flow based landlording to seven-year-hold, private equity driven bets on cap rate compression. All the while, we largely lost the ability to build beautifully decades ago. We misinterpreted Jane Jacobs and began requiring five material facades to break up building massing. We passed more safety regulations to prevent people from dying in fires, but in doing so mandated more expensive, less desirable through-block buildings with double-loaded corridors and multiple staircases.

Again, most of this regulation comes from a good place and was never intended to kill development. But the kind of development it encourages is the four-over-one slop that no one wants to live next to.

text:
Yes because having no particles nor space nor time is a feature and not a bug! lol do u even physics bro? Review: “A Parameter-Free Candidate for the Fine-Structure Constant from Entangled Qudits,” A. D. Wissner-Gross, October 23, 2026

Summary of the claim. The paper reports that a single axiom about maximally entangled pairs yields the algebraic number (79 + 48√2 + 42√3 + 3√6)/31104, whose inverse agrees with the CODATA 2022 value of α⁻¹(0) to ten significant figures, and conjectures that this number is the fine-structure constant.

1. The paper contains no physics. The fine-structure constant is the strength with which the photon field couples to electric charge at zero momentum transfer. Every term in that definition requires a field defined on spacetime, a charged particle, and a scattering process from which the zero-transfer limit is taken. The paper supplies none of these, and says so:

No spacetime. “An axiom about entangled pairs, which mentions neither charge nor spacetime” (Discussion). “The structures they presuppose in field theory, a field over spacetime and a scattering amplitude, are not supplied here” (S8).
No time. “The model has no time order” (S7). Nothing evolves.
No particles. The only particle named is the photon, and it appears solely in Conjecture 1. The object conjectured to be the photon’s link carries hypercharge Y = 1/6, which the author identifies as “the quantum numbers of the left-handed quark doublet” (S3). The photon has hypercharge zero.
No Lagrangian, no Hamiltonian, no equation of motion, no interaction. “The model has no charged loop, no vertex factor, no loop momentum, and no expansion in a coupling” (Fig. S2). “The model constructs no propagator” and “no function of the momentum transfer” (S8).

A coupling constant measures the strength of an interaction. With no interaction present, the quantity computed has no definition as a coupling.

2. What is computed. The computation is finite combinatorics on the operator algebra of C³⊗C². Four slots carry the traceless basis operators of a qutrit (8) and a qubit (3). Products of one operator from each of two distinct slots number 64 + 9 + 4·24 = 169; three qubit commutators bring the count to 172. The records are sorted into four classes by their symmetry under two permutations, the classes are assigned the weights 1, √2, √3, √6, and the weights are summed and divided by 24·36·36, the dimension of a tensor product of operator spaces. Theorem 2 states that the trace of an operator defined to carry these weights, divided by this dimension, equals the sum of these weights divided by this dimension. The Lean file verifies that arithmetic.

3. The physics vocabulary is attached by definition. The author is explicit. “Identifying this normalized readout with the on-shell two-point function is the one definitional identification of the paper. It names what Theorem 2 computes and is used in no proof.” Figure S2 is “a correspondence of roles, not of diagrams.” Table S7 is a glossary mapping each QED term to a counting step. The bare coupling α_bare = 1 is the statement that a projection onto a pure state succeeds with probability one (“½ + ½ = 1”). The Ward identity Z₁ = Z₂ is the statement that the scalar i commutes with every operator. Z₃ is the name given to the number after it is computed.

4. The entangled pairs are not physical systems. A qudit is defined as “a finite-dimensional quantum system, of dimension at least two,” with no observable, location, mass, or charge. Entanglement in quantum mechanics is a correlation between measurement outcomes on two systems; the paper has no second location and discards outcome statistics, since every projection “has no failure branch” and “no expectation value is estimated anywhere.” What remains is the vector Σ|i⟩|i⟩/√d as an algebraic device. Its roles in the paper are to supply the amplitudes 1/√d (the origin of √2 and √3, Theorem S7), the transpose identity that doubles the slot count, the U⊗Ū invariance renamed “gauge freedom,” and the Størmer–Woronowicz–Choi separability threshold d₁d₂ ≤ 6 used to select dimensions 2 and 3.

5. The gauge group is the block decomposition of C⁵. S(U(3)×U(2)) as the subgroup of SU(5) preserving C²⊕C³ is the Georgi–Glashow observation, cited here to Baez–Huerta. Any split of five dimensions into 2 + 3 produces it. The dimensions 2 and 3 are selected by a definition of “fix” constructed so that the separability threshold falls out; the author concedes that “under a weaker definition of fix ... the read cap below would be a premise rather than a consequence.”

6. The number was fitted. The paper states that “nothing in it is fit to α” and prints Table S5: fourteen alternative wordings of its own definitions, each with its inverse evaluated (135.894, 146.524, 127.536, 139.030, 134.485, 112.423, 139.713, 138.348, 132.739, 141.621, 97.505, 70.190, 0.758, 180.837), with the note that “two of them land within one percent of the computed value.” That table cannot be produced without computing every variant and comparing each to 137.036; it is the record of a search. Each row is excluded by a sentence (“a read is an act at the end at which it is taken”; “four letters, a four-point quantity”; “per unit of the conserved count”) and never by a calculation. The object itself is selected from 23 configurations (Table S2) by three conditions stated after the fact; the author notes that “minimality does not select the object” and leaves the other configurations “not evaluated.” The Lean file verifies that the chosen clauses yield the chosen number; it cannot verify when the clauses were chosen. The accompanying mutations script, offered as evidence of rigor, establishes that the result holds for exactly one wording out of many.

7. Postselection by fiat. The join of two links succeeds with probability 1/6 under quantum mechanics. The paper multiplies by √6 and declares the complementary outcome “no configuration of the axiom.” The author acknowledges that “whether a postselected law of this kind is consistent with the rest of physics is not settled here.”

8. Prior art. Wyler (1969, 1971) obtained α⁻¹ ≈ 137.036 from volumes of symmetric domains, and the author cites that work as having “foundered on what fixed their normalization.” The present paper has the same unfixed normalization — the choice of N over 172, of √kᵣ over kᵣ, of which end each exchange acts at — with each free choice renamed a definition.

Recommendation. The paper presents an algebraic number from a counting rule on C³⊗C², with no spacetime, no time, no particles, no Lagrangian, no Hamiltonian, and no interaction, and identifies it with a coupling constant by a glossary. The counting rule has at least three independently adjustable clauses and one configuration choice, each resolved by wording, and the author’s own Table S5 records the evaluation of alternatives against the target. The result belongs to the numerological literature on α that the paper cites, and the Lean verification, the CODATA comparison, and the on-shell vocabulary change the presentation without changing that classification. Reject.

text:
For all of you regarding Christa as a monster, first read this:

“Cruelty”

The following scene is a dramatization — but every physical detail in it is drawn from sworn testimony you’ll read a few paragraphs down.
The leather strap came across her back hard. Her screams filled the small room, echoing off the walls, but the blows did not stop. The searing sting from the first strike was replaced almost immediately with a subsequent strike, tearing her soft flesh. A trickle of blood appeared, but this wasn’t enough to stop the assault upon her. A last, frenzied strike made her legs wobble. She fell forward onto the floor. Her screams had been replaced by wracking sobs and her pitiful voice begging for her assailant to stop.

While shaking uncontrollably in pain and shame, only then was she allowed to put her clothing back on. Her assailant left her in the room alone. Shaking and in pain, she gingerly slipped her clothing back onto her small, battered body, careful not to cause any more injury to her split flesh. She’d have liked to have attended to the injury, but she didn’t want to incur any more wrath. Better to just deal with it later.

In 1780, Mary Rogers, a widow, was given charge of an abandoned Pequot girl named Hannah Ocuish. Rogers, a strict adherent of a fringe religious sect called the Rogerines, routinely whipped little Hannah, calling her a “devil-child.” 

Whipping Hannah was, in Mary Rogers’ opinion, the only way to chase the devil out of her.
The whippings were so constant and severe that after little Hannah was arrested for the murder of a neighbor girl, Eunice Bolles, Mary Rogers was facing possible indictment herself as a co-defendant due to her abuse of the little girl. Nearly everyone in New London who knew of Hannah, knew of her abuse by the Widow Rogers. It wasn’t a well-kept secret. In the end, the stern arm of justice fell solely on Hannah, and she alone was executed for the murder. The mitigating factors were regarded as irrelevant.

We look upon the abuse of a child as described above and shake our head. How could anyone be so cruel? What is to be gained by crushing a child’s spirit in such a manner? 
Wouldn’t they understand that a beaten child might lash out themselves, and do so to someone even weaker than they?

We pride ourselves on the fact that we’ve “evolved” over the centuries — that we wouldn’t do such a horrific thing to an abused girl. Yes, she took a life, but couldn’t it be argued that her life had also been taken from her? Abandoned. Abused. Neglected and unwanted. Where else is a child supposed to go?

Here’s the reveal: the account of the abused girl that opened this article was not an accounting of Hannah Ocuish’s abuse by Mary Rogers. It could have been. I researched Hannah’s life over seven years and hold a copy of an original document containing a deposition list with the names of Mary Rogers, as well as those of four of her seven children, leading up to Hannah’s murder trial. Mary Rogers was very much in danger of standing upon that gallows alongside Hannah, but the court opted not to go that far.
No — the account above belongs to Christa Gail Pike. She is, as of this writing, still alive, but sits awaiting execution at the hand of Tennessee Governor William Byron Lee.
Here is the relevant passage from her 2010 appeal:
Mr. Pike stated that he would use either his hand or a belt to discipline the Petitioner. At most, he struck her with the belt three or four times in the same day. Mr. Pike denied that he ever made the Petitioner remove her clothing for the spankings and stated that any scars on the Petitioner’s back were not the result of any spankings he gave her. (Page 25 of her appeal.)
What is telling is that Emil Glenn Pike, Christa’s father, offers information not asked. Why would he point out that he didn’t require his daughter — 12 years old at the time — to remove her clothing before he took a belt to her?

The rest can be found here:

text:
🇮🇳 MISSION BHARAT TECH SHIELD 2036 - A Gen Z and Youth Request, it will also create jobs which will help us prosper. Thank you Modi ji Govt for consideration.
@PMOIndia @DRDO_India @isro @IAF_MCC @adgpi 

India Needs 5 Integrated Defence, Aerospace & Critical Technology Cities — A ₹3 Lakh Crore (scalable up to Rs. 10.5 Lakhs Crores, please extend and invest more) National Mission proposal to Government of India from the youth and Gen Z of this country.

🇮🇳 5 Strategic City Clusters | 6 Critical Technology Missions | 10 Years | ₹3,00,000 Crore in Proposed Investments (Add Rs. 2,00,000 Crore to extend it further)

An appeal to the Government of India, Ministry of Defence, Ministry of Finance, Department of Science & Technology, State Governments and Indian industry from youth and Gen Z to Modi ji Govt.
India needs to move from isolated R&D projects and manufacturing facilities to fully integrated national innovation ecosystems.

The country that can design, test, certify, mass-produce, upgrade and sustain advanced technologies will have a decisive strategic advantage in the decades ahead.

🌏 1. Lessons from Ch*i*n*aa and Paa*kis*ta*an*

🇨🇳 C*H*II**N*AA

Ch_*ii*-naa's progress in advanced aerospace and naval technology deserves serious examination.

Its Fu**jii*aan* aircraft carrier has demonstrated electromagnetic catapult operations involving J-3*5 stealth fighters and KJ-**600** airborne early-warning aircraft.

Ch*ii*n**aa is also flight-testing advanced tailless combat-aircraft prototypes associated with next-generation aviation research.

These achievements do not mean that every announced technology is already operational. Nevertheless, Ch**i*n*aa demonstrates the importance of industrial scale, long-term investment, supply-chain depth and rapid engineering iteration.

🇵🇰 Paa*kis*ta*an*

Paa*kis*ta*an* has developed an integrated aerospace innovation model around Kam**ra** Aviation City, Paa*kis*ta*an* Aeronautical Complex and the National Aeros**pace Scien*ce & Techno*logy Park (NA*STP*).

NA*STP* identifies five chapters:

📍 Kam*ra/Attock
📍 Rawa*lpin*di
📍 La*hore
📍 Kara*chi
📍 Kharia*n

Kam*ra* brings together aerospace R&D, manufacturing, aviation education, innovation and industrial support.

Paa*kis*ta*an* also initiated Project Az*m in 2017 to pursue a fifth-generation fighter and associated capabilities. However, that programme has not delivered a publicly verified operational indigenous fifth-generation fighter.

The Air Wea*p*on*s Complex is another element of Paa*kis*ta*an* defence-industrial base.

The lesson for India is institutional integration, not an assumption that Paa*kis*ta*an* has overtaken India technologically.

India possesses far greater industrial and research capacity. What India must accelerate is the conversion of research excellence into deployable products at scale.

🇮🇳 2. Where India Stands
India has significant achievements:

✅ FY2025–26 defence production: ₹1.78 lakh crore

✅ FY2025–26 defence exports: ₹38,424 crore

✅ Defence industrial corridors in Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh

✅ Major institutions including DRDO, HAL, ADA, NAL, ISRO, IITs and IISc

✅ ₹1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) financing scheme

✅ Expanding semiconductor manufacturing, aerospace and private defence ecosystems

But India needs greater depth in advanced propulsion, shared testing capacity, certification, strategically important components, high-end materials and faster research-to-production cycles.

We must build upon existing infrastructure rather than duplicate it.

🏙️ 3. Establish Five National Strategic Technology City Clusters

I recommend a new Bharat Strategic Technology Cities Mission, with dedicated city-level development corporations, long-term financing and national technology missions.

The following locations and investments are proposed, not announced government commitments.

✈️ CITY 1 — Bengaluru–Tumakuru, Karnataka

National Aviation, Propulsion & Flight Test City

💰 Proposed investment: ₹75,000 crore

Focus:

✈️ Indigenous aircraft engines and propulsion research

🛩️ National flight-testing infrastructure and simulation

🚁 Drones, autonomous aircraft and counter-drone research

🔥 High-temperature engine testing, thermal systems and advanced composites

🧪 Reliability, fatigue, vibration and airworthiness certification
🛰️ Aerospace electronics and digital engineering

Partners to engage: HAL, DRDO/GTRE, ADA, NAL, IISc, IITs, Tata Advanced Systems, L&T, Mahindra Aerospace and specialist MSMEs.

Aviation City + Flight Test Centre can become one of India's most decisive national investments.

Build upon existing capabilities and establish world-class shared facilities that private companies and research institutions can access.

🤖 CITY 2 — Hyderabad–Zaheerabad, Telangana

National AI, Autonomous Systems & Security Technology City

💰 Proposed investment: ₹60,000 crore

Focus:

🛸 Drone and counter-drone technology

🧠 Defence AI, trusted computing and autonomous systems

🔐 Cybersecurity and critical infrastructure protection

📡 Advanced sensors, communications and electronic systems

⚛️ Quantum technologies and secure electronics

🚀 Space and aerospace subsystems

Partners to engage: DRDO laboratories, BDL, MIDHANI, IIT Hyderabad, IIIT Hyderabad, T-Hub, Adani Defence, Bharat Forge and specialist technology companies.

Establish shared validation laboratories, approved test environments, innovation accelerators and industrial production facilities.

🏭 CITY 3 — Chennai–Hosur, Tamil Nadu

National Advanced Materials, Robotics & Manufacturing City

💰 Proposed investment: ₹55,000 crore

With linked research and industrial nodes in Coimbatore, Salem and Tiruchirappalli.

Focus:

🔩 Aerospace-grade metals, alloys and metallurgy

🦾 Advanced robotics and precision manufacturing

🔋 Batteries, energy storage and power electronics

🚢 Maritime technologies and unmanned systems
🏗️ Industrial automation, additive manufacturing and advanced machine tools

🧪 Materials qualification, corrosion, fatigue and reliability testing

Academic anchors: IIT Madras, Anna University, College of Engineering Guindy, MIT Chromepet, PSG College of Technology and NIT Tiruchirappalli.

Industrial partners: L&T, Tata, TVS Group, Ashok Leyland, Mahindra, major automotive manufacturers and MSMEs.

Tamil Nadu's existing Defence Industrial Corridor should serve as the foundation, not be replaced.

🛡️ CITY 4 — Lucknow–Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh

National Defence Manufacturing & Certification City

💰 Proposed investment: ₹50,000 crore

With linked industrial nodes, including Jhansi.

Focus:

⚙️ Precision engineering and aerospace components

🛩️ Drone production, aircraft systems and integration

🧪 Independent testing, quality assurance and certification

🏭 Defence manufacturing scale-up and supplier development
🤖 Robotics, industrial automation and additive manufacturing

🌾 Food-security technologies and agricultural robotics

Partners to engage: IIT Kanpur, HAL, DRDO, universities, major private manufacturers and UP Defence Corridor enterprises.

Create a nationally coordinated supplier qualification and certification ecosystem serving startups, MSMEs and large manufacturers.

💻 CITY 5 — Dholera–Ahmedabad–Sanand, Gujarat

National Semiconductor, Energy & Critical Supply Chain City

💰 Proposed incremental investment: ₹60,000 crore

Focus:

💻 Semiconductor fabrication ecosystem and advanced packaging

🧠 AI accelerators, sensors and specialised chip design

🔋 Battery chemistry, recycling and energy storage

⚡ Resilient grids and advanced power electronics

🧲 Critical minerals, materials processing and supply-chain resilience
🌱 Clean energy, water-efficient manufacturing and industrial sustainability

Build upon Tata Electronics' Dholera semiconductor investment, Micron's Sanand facility, and the wider Gujarat electronics ecosystem.

Engage IIT Gandhinagar, Reliance Education, Tata Electronics, Reliance Industries, semiconductor companies and qualified global technology partners.

Important: The ₹60,000 crore proposal should represent additional investment, without double-counting already approved semiconductor projects.

🔬 4. Six National Technology Missions Across All Five Cities

Each city must participate in six coordinated missions, with different centres of excellence.

1️⃣ Drones & Counter-Drones

Autonomous platforms, sensing, detection, protection, testing, regulatory certification and scalable production.

2️⃣ Aircraft Engines & Advanced Test Centres

Indigenous propulsion, turbine materials, engine durability, altitude simulation, aircraft systems testing and flight-test certification.

3️⃣ Materials & Metallurgy

Special alloys, composites, ceramics, precision casting, critical minerals, high-temperature components and advanced manufacturing.

4️⃣ Semiconductors, AI & Quantum

Trusted chip design, secure computing, industrial AI, edge intelligence, quantum research and nationally resilient electronics supply chains.

5️⃣ Robotics, Batteries & Energy

Industrial robotics, energy storage, resilient microgrids, next-generation batteries, advanced manufacturing and clean-energy research.

6️⃣ Greenfield Agricultural Research & Food Security

Climate-resilient crops, water-efficient farming, agricultural robotics, precision irrigation, cold chains, protected cultivation, food storage and crop-loss reduction.

Food security is national security. Research must extend to drought resilience, climate adaptation, supply-chain disruptions and emergency preparedness.

Use appropriate non-prime industrial land and environmental safeguards rather than sacrificing productive agricultural land.

💰 5. A ₹3 LAKH CRORE Financing Framework

India must combine government capital with private investment, long-term institutional finance and properly structured public bonds.

Proposed 10-year financing mix:

🏛️ ₹90,000 crore — Central and State Government contributions for eligible public laboratories, testing assets, foundational infrastructure and research facilities.

🏭 ₹90,000 crore — Indian private companies, defence PSUs and industrial joint ventures.

🌍 ₹45,000 crore — Institutional infrastructure equity, including NIIF-style structures, sovereign wealth funds, pension funds and other eligible investors.

📈 ₹45,000 crore — Project-backed infrastructure bonds, green bonds, approved municipal/state financing and infrastructure investment vehicles.

🔬 ₹30,000 crore — Eligible RDI financing, development finance, venture capital and deep-tech investment.

TOTAL: ₹3,00,000 CRORE

These are illustrative financing targets, subject to project feasibility, investor appetite, regulatory permissions and budget approvals. Existing commitments must not be counted twice.

🌏 6. Invite Trusted International Capital & Technology Partnerships

🇯🇵 JAPAN: Invite JBIC, JICA and eligible Japanese companies to participate in semiconductors, advanced materials, precision engineering, industrial automation, energy and supply chains.

🇦🇪 UAE: Explore participation from ADIA, Mubadala and other qualified UAE investment platforms for eligible commercial infrastructure, logistics, clean energy and technology investment.

🇨🇦 CANADA: Approach CPP Investments, Ontario Teachers', PSP Investments, La Caisse and other institutional investors for appropriately structured civilian and dual-use infrastructure.

🇸🇬 SINGAPORE: Explore participation from Temasek, GIC and qualified commercial partners.

🇪🇺 🇫🇷 🇬🇧 🇺🇸 🇮🇱 OTHER PARTNERS: Pursue technology collaborations in permitted aerospace, electronics, industrial R&D and advanced manufacturing fields.

All foreign investment and collaboration must respect Indian law, security clearances, export controls and intellectual-property agreements.

Classified and sensitive defence activities must remain within approved, access-controlled Indian security frameworks. Foreign infrastructure financing must not imply access to sensitive military programmes.

🏢 7. Mobilise Indian Industry

Invite competitive proposals from:

• Tata Group / Tata Advanced Systems
• Adani Defence & Aerospace
• Larsen & Toubro
• Reliance Industries and eligible group companies
• Mahindra Group
• Bharat Forge / Kalyani Group
• HAL, BEL, BDL and MIDHANI
• Solar Industries, Data Patterns, ideaForge and emerging deep-tech enterprises

These companies should be potential participants, not assumed investors.

Offer long-term industrial leases, transparent tenders, shared testing infrastructure, performance-based incentives and procurement opportunities.

Reserve meaningful opportunities for startups, MSMEs and university spinouts.

No exclusive industrial monopolies. Encourage competition, technology transfer and multiple qualified suppliers.

🏦 8. Launch Bharat Critical Technology Infrastructure Bonds

Explore a professionally managed, SEBI-compliant domestic bond framework to finance suitable revenue-generating infrastructure.

Potential investors:

🇮🇳 Indian institutional and retail investors
🏦 Banks and insurance companies
💼 Pension and retirement funds
🏗️ Infrastructure investment funds
🌍 Eligible overseas institutional investors

Projects must have clear repayment sources, independently assessed risks, audited accounts and transparent disclosures.

Government support or guarantees, where justified, must be explicitly approved and budgeted.
Fund speculative scientific research through appropriate public R&D support and risk capital—not ordinary infrastructure bonds with unrealistic repayment assumptions.

🧩 9. Governance — Build a Mission, Not Five Real-Estate Projects

Establish a National Strategic Technology Cities Mission, coordinated by the Government of India with participation from:

🏛️ Ministry of Defence
🔬 Department of Science & Technology / ANRF
💻 MeitY and semiconductor ecosystem institutions
🏭 Ministry of Heavy Industries and DPIIT
💰 Ministry of Finance
🌾 Agricultural research organisations
🎓 IITs, IISc, NITs and other universities
🤝 State Governments and private industry
Create one accountable mission office and five professionally managed city-level special purpose vehicles.

Use a mission-based framework:
🎯 Capability — Define the technologies India needs.

🔬 Research — Finance competitive teams and laboratories.

🧪 Validation — Provide shared accredited test facilities.

🏭 Production — Support suppliers and manufacturing.

✅ Procurement — Convert qualified innovations into real orders.

📊 Accountability — Publish measurable, non-sensitive results.

Expand the use of iDEX, ADITI, DRDO's Technology Development Fund and the RDI financing programme according to their respective eligibility rules.

Adopt milestone-based funding, independent technical evaluation, timely procurement decisions and strong public accountability.

🚀 10. Execution Roadmap

First 100 days

✅ Constitute an inter-ministerial mission group.
✅ Identify five anchor campuses and linked industrial nodes.
✅ Publish a national capability-gap assessment.
✅ Begin investor consultations and feasibility studies.
Within 12 months
✅ Complete master planning and safeguards.
✅ Establish governance and financing vehicles.
✅ Publish testing infrastructure and procurement roadmaps.
✅ Launch university–industry research calls.

Years 1.5–2.4

✅ Open priority shared laboratories and pilot production facilities.
✅ Expand national aircraft and propulsion testing access.
✅ Start demonstrator programmes and supplier certification.
✅ Launch competitive domestic and global partnerships.

Years 2.5–5

✅ Bring the five ecosystems into meaningful operation.
✅ Demonstrate qualified products and repeatable manufacturing.
✅ Publish audited programme outcomes and independent reviews.

By 2034

🎯 Target five sustainable innovation ecosystems, dozens of shared testing and certification facilities, a broad Indian deep-tech supplier base, substantial skilled employment and measurable improvements in technology self-reliance.

Measure products certified, systems deployed, production capacity, indigenous intellectual property, supplier quality, private R&D investment and commercial outcomes—not merely MoUs signed or buildings inaugurated.

🇮🇳 11. A National Strategic Appeal

India should not attempt to replicate China or Pakistan blindly. It must build on its own much larger scientific, industrial and entrepreneurial foundations.

The goal is not five impressive campuses with ceremonial inaugurations.

The goal is five connected centres of national capability where a scientific idea can progress from university research to prototype, certified product, competitive manufacturing and real-world deployment.

National security requires much more than weapons production. It also depends on resilient energy, trusted semiconductors, cybersecurity, materials, logistics and food security.

India must invest in the next generation of engineers, scientists, technicians, researchers and industrial entrepreneurs.

Let us move from announcements to test facilities, from laboratory prototypes to production, and from imported technologies to Indian design and intellectual property.

🇮🇳 Vision 2036: Research in India. Design in India. Test in India. Manufacture in India. Deploy in India. Compete globally.

Requesting the Government of India, Defence Ministry, Finance Ministry, DST, State Governments, universities and India's leading industrial groups to evaluate and launch a coordinated national mission.

Actually you know what? I’m gonna make a thread of @log4j’s Smart TV exploration because everyone on this entire hellsite should see it in full detail. 

Realize, please, as you scroll the thread below, that this is what many tech companies who sell household products are doing, and what the US Government can compel them to log and forward, and gag them from acknowledging.

If it has WiFi and a power plug, it probably does these things. Or worse. 

They sell it to you as an accessibility and safety feature, and they monetize the back end by selling your proprietary data for more accurate and affordable ad targeting, and they create a permanent legal discovery surface for any “national security” use case. The entire economy of the ad-supported internet depends on this, which is why I’m so bullish on direct creator subscriptions instead of ads for the future of the internet.

I want more businesses funded directly by the people they serve, with less incentive to build detailed profiles of those people.

How do I know? I co-founded and sold an ISP. I was offered tours of cross connect facilities.  People who handle these demands know they can come with gag orders. I have run ads for big companies, I know how to make them show up when you talk about related topics - it doesn’t require a microphone these platforms are smart enough to figure it out. I’ve made them show up WHILE people watch podcasts about the product, even before Google offered that feature directly.

The US needs regulations around ads.

Ask any EU regulator. Read the Twitter Files. Ask any AI. Genuinely.

I see so many “anti data center” people who are well meaning community advocates threaten on public digital media like reels to like do some violence or protest some random building and don’t realize that they get themselves on a list under the guises of “extremism” and suddenly the federal government has recourse to remotely query their entire private lives. 

Be aware, be thoughtful. Demand accountability.

The US needs stronger limits on data collection, retention, sharing and government access—and meaningful consequences for misuse.

We need to redesign our systems so we get our constitutional protections back. Asap.

Thank you!  For those that want to know here is the COMPLETE Feature list:

**Getting started**
- A fast first chat that shows one card at a time. Power users can let it set itself up in one go from their connected apps.
- It takes your address, or offers to use where you are now. Then it shows your reps with their photos and asks for a quick Good, Bad or Unsure on each one.
- It offers a voice chat so you can share your views in your own words.

**Your views and matches**
- 20 issue questions, asked 5 at a time, with the full answers as the choices. A results card follows each batch of 5.
- Match scores for each rep and candidate, with an honest "how sure" level. The scores come only from the positions you stated.
- "Sharpen my matches" lets you answer more questions or revisit them later. An X-posts shortcut is available only if you ask for it.

**Voting**
- Checks your registration on your state's official page and fills in the form for you. You submit it yourself.
- Election dates, early-voting and Election Day hours, nearest polling places, and one-tap "Add to my calendar."
- A voting plan covering when and where, going with a friend, getting a ride and mail ballots, plus an optional election-morning alarm and a check for anything clashing with Election Day.
- After you confirm you're voting, a "See something wrong at the polls?" card. It lists official channels first, then the RNC and DNC hotlines side by side.

**Ballot guide**
- One printable ballot PDF, blank or filled with your picks, with colored match chips for each race.
- A side-by-side comparison of judges, with sourced background and optional questions about what you value in a judge.
- It checks your ballot district against the district your current rep serves, using official election sources for all 50 states and DC.

**Rep research**
- Cited facts about your reps: roll-call votes, missed votes, and their record next to what they've said.
- A plain money report on how much came from small donors, plus red flags like one industry, foreign-influenced groups or a single donor network. Each flag shows as found or none found.
- Money-and-votes checks on a specific bill, with no rating.
- Local officials from the school board up, from official rosters.

**Contacting reps**
- A guided letter writer that polishes your own words without losing your voice. It hands you every route ready to send yourself: email, web form, paper letter with the mailing address, or public comment.
- Office phone numbers with a short word-for-word script and a voicemail version. You place the call; it never calls, records or uses an AI voice.
- A "full court press" timed to upcoming votes, plus follow-up and tracking of replies.

**Watching for you (opt-in, with limits on how often)**
- Bill and hearing alerts that match your saved stances, with short neutral explainers.
- A daily vote sweep and a weekly report.
- Alerts on agenda items from school board, city council or county meeting pages you paste in.
- Five-day check-ins during the first week, election reminders, and a one-time "grow your bot" offer for extra free features.

**Your stuff**
- A dashboard Page with your reps, the next election, your ballot and one next step.
- "My UnmuteAmerica," one printable report with everything it has gathered for you.
- Picture cards for scores, money, reps and meetings, with no product branding on any of them.

**Always**
- It never sends, calls or submits anything for you, and every letter or call needs your OK.
- It never asks you for access codes and never talks tech. Your personal info stays out of the shared helper.
- It works across the US, with a basic mode for addresses in other countries, and an optional path to run your own copy of the helpers.

I completely disagree with you 😉 Sure, we can discuss the cultural differences; there are some, but here's the harsh truth: from a business standpoint, people will build whatever works, including copying what works on other chains, just to make money on Cardano, and many have tried, but it didn't work. So you can talk about cultural differences all you want, but money makes the world go round, and people always follow the money, not cultural ideals.

In that regard, people tried to copy whatever works on other chains and bring it to Cardano, including DeFi, even MEME coins, but guess what: it didn't work the same way it did on other chains (not even comparing to Solana, where https://t.co/OAjuWiI4ob made a historic breakthrough, but with Binance, Base, and similar). Why didn't it work? Becuase the chain wasn't fast or cheap enough to compete for that specific use case. Nothing mystical about it. 

You think $USDC and $USDT didn't come because of the cultural thing, because the Cardano community or the users didn't want it? Or, even better, because Charles talked shit about centralization??? Wake up! People (projects/businesses) would follow the money if they could, but they couldn't because of the tech incompatibilities. So, even if anyone else wanted, even if Charles wanted (he gave us a spin, an ideological answer to cover what nobody wanted to hear), he couldn't bring $USDT or $USDC to Cardano because Cardano isn't technically suitable to support them. Tokens on Cardano are minted natively, without a smart contract, so you can't bring that shit over as easily as you can on other chains and expect it to work the same way (allowing freezing funds within self-custody wallets when required). So, to get back to what you said, that "missed train" had nothing to do with culture on Cardano or community not wanting to see $USDC or $USDT on Cardano. 

Yes, there were moments when business-wise things could go different way, for example when CF choose not to pay for crucial integrations like Fireblocks and similar, but in their defense, why would it matter if you can't benefit from it? The same goes for all TradFi misalignment with Cardano and its projects (tokens).  Specifically, CNTs were missing listings on popular CEXs because, again, the CNT/USDT pair meant shit for Cardano, since there was no $USDT on Cardano. Do I need to go further on the topic? 

So, before we blame builders and project founders on Cardano for their "wrong" culture or misalignment with business incentives that proved to work elsewhere, think twice about what they were given (technically) to work with 😉

Now, I can publicly bet with you on the hot topic: Cardano DeFi. If Cardano doesn't solve its biggest fundamental disadvantages compared to other chains (slow Tx/smartcontract execution, including high fees compared to Solana, BNB, Base...), and a lack of widely adopted stablecoins, then whatever great DeFi project you throw at Cardano, or how much money you spend on marketing and the like, it won't work! 

What do you think why @HyperliquidX is so popular? Is it because it's a super-sexy product that doesn't exist elsewhere, or because it offers a superior user experience (super-fast and cheap DeFi) that others can't match?

You mentioned Chainlink? We worked with them, and again, the easiest answer would be to say that Cardano didn't need them, or that they didn't want us, but the real problem was the tech (interoperability). 

Governance? It was technically feasible, and when everything else failed, it was no surprise that it became the focus. At least something we could brag about. 

VCs don't give a shit about the cultural things; they follow the money, too.  We can argue about Charles's wrong narrative, but even that was a sort of cover-up because VCs aren't dumb either. The first thing they loolk for is scalability, and how could they find anything billion-dollar scalable on Cardano when things cannot work with EVM-compatible chains or interact with widely adopted stablecoins and similar? The tech we were given left builders stranded on an isolated island, and the lack of VC support only confirmed that. 

So, to summarise, business isn't sci-fi, but it's super hard to build a successful one without the right tools to compete in the race. It's as simple as that.

text:
This is a big story making its way through the Florida contractor community today. More than 50 individuals were reportedly arrested during an undercover sting operation targeting unlicensed contracting.

In Florida, contractor licensing is regulated by the Department of Business and Professional Regulation (DBPR), and obtaining a state contractor license requires meeting strict experience, examination, and financial responsibility requirements.

As someone who holds two Florida contractor licenses, I know all too well how frequently property owners unknowingly hire unlicensed individuals.

I hear it almost daily: “I have someone willing to do it cheaper.”

My response is usually the same: “Are they a licensed contractor?”

There is absolutely nothing wrong with shopping around for competitive pricing. But there is a significant difference between getting a better price from another licensed contractor and hiring someone who isn’t legally qualified to perform the work.

Licensed contractors invest substantial time and money into meeting state requirements, maintaining insurance, and operating legitimate businesses. Those requirements exist for a reason. They help protect property owners and establish accountability when something goes wrong.

An unlicensed individual can often offer a lower price because they aren’t carrying the same obligations, overhead, or regulatory responsibilities.

And unfortunately, the property owner may not realize the risk until there’s a problem.

My advice to every Florida property owner is simple: Before hiring someone to perform regulated contracting work, verify their license directly through the DBPR.

Don’t just take someone’s word for it. Don’t assume having an LLC means they’re licensed. And don’t confuse years of experience with legal authorization to perform contracting work.

A cheaper quote doesn’t always mean a better deal, especially when your home, your investment, and your safety are on the line.

You can verify a Florida contractor’s license here:

Sharad Purnima is not merely a night of worshipping the Moon. In Vedic and spiritual traditions, it is associated with the subtle principles of Chandra Tattva (mind and emotions), Soma (nourishment), Prana (life force) and Shri Tattva (divine prosperity).

The Moon represents the mind, while Maa Lakshmi represents not only wealth but also stability, contentment, harmony and auspiciousness.

This sacred night offers an opportunity for deep spiritual reflection and disciplined Sadhana.

1. Chandra Reflection Sadhana: Purification of Emotional Impressions

Fill a clean silver or steel vessel with water and place it where the Moon's reflection can be seen.

Sit quietly and observe the reflection for a few moments.

Remember the emotions you have carried silently for years, including anger, disappointment, resentment and fear.

Chant 108 times:

ॐ सोम सोमाय नमः।

Om Soma Somaya Namah.

Pray for the purification of accumulated emotional impressions and the restoration of inner peace.

The deeper significance of this practice is that when the mind becomes still, its hidden disturbances become easier to recognise and release.

 2. Lakshmi Sthirata Sankalp: Stability of Wealth

Place a few grains of unbroken rice, one betel nut and a silver coin on a clean yellow cloth.

Light a ghee diya and chant 108 times:

ॐ श्रीं महालक्ष्म्यै नमः।

Om Shreem Mahalakshmyai Namah.

Do not pray merely for the arrival of money.

Pray for the ability to preserve wealth, use it wisely, fulfil responsibilities and remain free from unnecessary greed.

The following morning, keep the coin in your place of worship or where you safely store money.

The deeper principle of Lakshmi Sadhana is that prosperity must be accompanied by stability, discipline and righteous conduct.

 3. Ancestral Gratitude and Chandra Shanti

Those experiencing recurring family disagreements, emotional insecurity or unresolved ancestral concerns may perform a simple remembrance practice.

Light a diya and respectfully remember your ancestors.

Chant:

ॐ सर्वेभ्यो पितृभ्यो नमः।

Om Sarvebhyo Pitribhyo Namah.

Express gratitude for the life, values and opportunities received through your family lineage.

This is a practice of ancestral remembrance and gratitude, not a substitute for specific Pitra Dosha rituals prescribed within a tradition.

 4. Shri Suktam and Kanakadhara Sadhana

Sharad Purnima is traditionally associated with the worship of Maa Mahalakshmi.

Devotees familiar with these sacred hymns may recite Shri Suktam and Kanakadhara Stotram.

While performing the recitation, maintain one important Sankalp:

May wealth enter my life through righteous means, remain protected through wisdom and serve a higher purpose.

Lakshmi worship is not simply about acquiring riches. It is also about purity of intention, gratitude, generosity and responsible living.

 5. Chandra Amrit and Annapurna Worship

Preparing kheer and placing it under moonlight is a well- known Sharad Purnima tradition.

Prepare kheer with devotion and place it in a clean, covered vessel under moonlight for a short period, while keeping it at a safe temperature.

Chant:

ॐ अन्नपूर्णायै नमः।

Om Annapurnayai Namah.

Offer the preparation as Prasad and share it with your family.

The next day, donate food according to your capacity.

The spiritual significance is profound: true prosperity is not measured only by what we possess, but also by our ability to nourish others.

Moonlight transforming food into medicinal nectar is a traditional belief, not a scientifically established effect. Avoid leaving perishable food unrefrigerated overnight.

text:
Shiryn Ghermezian, The Algemeiner
British Jewish actor Sacha Baron Cohen revealed that prior to joining the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) to play the demon Mephisto in the Disney+ series “Ironheart,” the production team expressed concerns about a Jewish actor playing a character likened to the devil because of historical antisemitic tropes.

The actor talked about how he was pitched the idea of playing a demonic character in the 2025 live-action series during a live taping of Josh Horowitz’s podcast “Happy Sad Confused” on Wednesday night at New York City’s 92nd Street Y.

“It was a wonderful meeting when I was offered it,” the Oscar nominee said. “It was primarily, I think, an almost entirely Black producing and directing team. And they said, ‘We want to offer you Mephisto, but we are aware of the negative association of Jews historically with the devil, and we want to make sure that you’re not insulted by us offering this.’ It was such an amazingly considerate, empathetic thing to say. And I was like, ‘Yeah, I’m good.'”

“Ironheart” was written by Chinaka Hodge, and its executive producers include “Black Panther” director Ryan Coogler and Zinzi Coogler. Episodes are directed by Sam Bailey and Angela Barnes.

“I think for the Jews out there, sometimes we don’t feel seen,” Baron Cohen added. “We don’t feel like people can empathize with us, that we are suffering too. And so, to have this entirely Black producing and directing team be so empathetic, was a moment of being seen. It was an amazing experience.”

Throughout history there have been antisemitic tropes and stereotypes associating Jewish people with the devil and other demonic elements, including claims and depictions of Jews having horns, cloven feet, and tails. Antisemitic conspiracy theories have long associated Jews with Satan and accused Jews of being agents of the devil, according to the World Jewish Congress.

The character Mephisto is inspired by the demon Mephistopheles and is notorious in the Marvel comic books for tricking mortals into making deals with him. In the season one finale of “Ironheart,” Mephisto makes a deal with Dominique Thorne’s character Riri Williams to bring her deceased best friend Natalie Washington back to life.

Baron Cohen is currently on tour promoting the new comedy film “Ali G: Who Iz I?”

text:
Trump Rejects Disastrous Poll Numbers: “I Don’t Believe Anybody Could Beat Me.”

President Donald Trump has dismissed another round of deeply unfavorable approval ratings, calling the latest RealClearPolitics polling average “fake” during a Friday interview with The Washington Examiner.

According to the polling average, Trump’s approval rating stands at just 38.8%, while disapproval has climbed to 60.4%.

“That’s fake,” Trump insisted. “I’m not at 38.”

Asked what he believed his actual approval rating was, Trump offered a dramatically different estimate.

“I don’t believe anybody could beat me,” he declared, suggesting his approval could be as high as 60%.

Trump attempted to discredit the numbers by referring to a polling firm accused of fabricating data. However, that firm's results were not included in the RealClearPolitics average.

The average draws on surveys from numerous organizations, including Reuters/Ipsos, CNN, Fox News, YouGov, and The New York Times.

Trump also pointed to a CNN analysis showing that he received overwhelming support from MAGA-aligned Republican voters in the 2024 election.

But there is a fundamental difference between winning support from loyal party voters and maintaining approval among the broader American public.

As the midterm elections approach, Trump faces deeply unfavorable polling numbers.

Yet his response remains unchanged: dismiss the polls, attack their credibility, and insist that his popularity is far greater than the evidence suggests.

7. Iran says a Hormuz-for-blockade diplomatic trade remains available

Event date/location: October 24 — Islamabad; Strait of Hormuz
Status: Disputed

Evidence: 
Established that Iran made the public offer; Unsupported by independent evidence that Washington rejected it on the terms Tehran describes.

What happened: 
Iran’s ambassador to Pakistan said Tehran remains willing to resume talks under the June Pakistan- and Qatar-brokered framework and would reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the United States lifted its naval blockade. He alleged President Donald Trump rejected that trade. Reuters previously confirmed that Iran’s seven-condition proposal remains on the table, including sanctions relief and an end to regional hostilities. 

Why it matters: 
The strait carried roughly one-fifth of global oil and LNG trade before the war. Even an incomplete negotiating channel can affect shipping risk and energy expectations.

Principal uncertainty: 
Washington has not confirmed the envoy’s account, and the parties remain divided over sequencing, sanctions and Iran’s nuclear program. This is a diplomatic signal, not a new agreement.

text:
Trump Threatens Iran Strike Perhaps Tomorrow, Pezeshkian Blames Washington for Deal Collapse

On Sunday, 25 October, US President Donald Trump threatened that the United States may strike Iran "perhaps tomorrow" or reach a "big and beautiful" deal with Tehran. On Saturday, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian had blamed Washington for the collapse of the provisional agreement.

He refused to give a date for the possible attack, saying: "Do you really think I would tell you if I were to do it?" The decision now rests with Tehran, he said, either a deal or finishing the job militarily: "In both cases, we win."

Trump claimed Washington has already destroyed all of Iran's fighter jets, warships, radar systems and military capabilities, leaving only "record inflation"; the goal, he said, is a permanent solution preventing Iran from ever developing a nuclear weapon.

On state television on Saturday, Pezeshkian held the United States responsible for the failure of the interim agreement, describing the American side as "cowards" who "ruined everything" during the negotiations, yet calling for a fresh attempt at a deal.

Tasnim news agency, citing an informed source, denied reports that Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for lifting the US naval blockade, calling them "false": "Iran does not accept any equation linking the strait with lifting the blockade, but is circumventing the blockade through its own methods and will ultimately break it decisively." The official position remains the seven conditions conveyed through mediators.

The US-Israeli war against Iran, which began in February and triggered a wider regional confrontation, continues despite the approved ceasefire and near-final peace deal.

Are Catholic statues and icons a form of idolatry—and does the Bible prohibit Christians from venerating sacred images? In this powerful discussion, Sam Shamoun responds to a young Catholic who was raised around Protestant objections and fears that honoring Catholic statues, icons, the Virgin Mary, and the saints might cross the line into worship.

Sam Shamoun explains the crucial biblical difference between veneration and idolatry. Idolatry occurs when someone treats a creature as a god or goddess and offers that creature the worship belonging exclusively to the Creator. Catholics and Eastern Orthodox Christians do not believe that Mary, Paul, Michael, the angels, or the saints are gods. Honoring an image of a saint is therefore not the same as worshipping that saint as God.

Opening Exodus 20 and Romans 1:21–25, Sam Shamoun examines what Scripture actually condemns. The Bible condemns rejecting God, worshipping creation instead of the Creator, and transforming created beings into false gods. Sam Shamoun argues that these passages cannot be interpreted as a universal prohibition against every religious image, because God Himself commanded Moses to make golden cherubim for the Ark of the Covenant in Exodus 25 and Exodus 37. Sacred images also appeared throughout Solomon’s Temple.

Sam Shamoun then discusses the bronze serpent, explaining that the image became sinful only when the Israelites began treating it as a god. The same distinction appears when Joshua and the elders bow before the Ark of the Covenant without worshipping the cherubim as gods. The conversation ultimately addresses Catholic veneration, Protestant objections to icons, the Virgin Mary, the saints, the Ten Commandments, the Eucharist, biblical worship, the Ark of the Covenant, and the difference between honoring a sacred image and committing idolatry.
