text:
CryptEscrow: Connecting Crypto Wealth With Real Estate

Cryptocurrency holders don’t necessarily need to find a seller willing to accept digital assets to purchase property. **CryptEscrow**, a Florida-based company, offers a crypto-to-cash conversion service designed to let buyers fund real-estate purchases while sellers receive U.S. dollars through a conventional closing.[1][2]

The process is straightforward: the buyer independently engages CryptEscrow, cryptocurrency is converted into dollars before settlement, and the title company handles the closing using traditional title and escrow procedures. This is a way to fund a property purchase with crypto wealth—not necessarily a transaction in which the property itself is transferred on a blockchain.[3]

### Recent developments

CryptEscrow announced a strategic partnership with Ripple on October 22, 2026, aimed at advancing cryptocurrency-powered real-estate settlement. The announcement should not be interpreted as proof that every transaction requires or uses XRP.[2]

Another development deserves careful wording: an August correction clarified that CryptEscrow is an independent, optional cryptocurrency-to-cash conversion provider available for evaluation by First American Title’s policy-issuing agents. First American itself does not accept, transmit, or hold cryptocurrency. That distinction matters when evaluating claims about institutional partnerships or adoption.[3]

### Costs and due diligence

HousingWire reported a 1% fee for clients accessing CryptEscrow through Elite International Realty’s partnership. Buyers should treat that as a reported partner-specific rate—not a guaranteed price for every transaction.[4]

CryptEscrow describes itself as licensed and insured, but those company statements should not substitute for independent verification. Its published terms also include broad limitations of responsibility for losses associated with using the service.[5][6]

Before committing funds, buyers should request:

- The exact contracting entity and applicable license or registration details.
- Insurance documentation and coverage limits.
- A written, all-in quote covering service fees, conversion spreads, network charges, and wire fees.
- Clear custody, conversion-timing, cancellation, and refund terms.
- Written confirmation that their closing agent will accept the funds and supporting documentation.

For real-estate professionals, the distinction is practical: CryptEscrow’s stated model connects cryptocurrency-funded buyers with a dollar-based closing process. Evaluating that service still requires scrutiny of its pricing, contractual protections, and the precise scope of its announced relationships.[3][4][6]

Post here : 

Up until Wednesday, October 21st, our new life in France (and our life in USA) felt like it had zero downtime. This adventure was proving to be more work than going to work. Everywhere I looked something needed doing—cooking, cleaning, laundry, logistics, learning to sail, and, of course, being pregnant.

Bobby took on much of the sailing side, but the first-mate responsibilities fell heavily on me. We pushed hard to take advantage of the unusually good weather in Bretagne, knowing we wanted to feel competent sailing the boat before our “neuvage” period ended and November’s boat work began. We also carried the weight of that offshore trip to check the boat out of the EU. I can’t imagine the stress if we still hadn’t done it.

Then, almost overnight, the pace stopped. After nearly ten weeks living onboard, and 39.5 years of life, October 21st was the first day I felt like there was truly nothing that had to be done. So, I made lunch for our marina friends with the newborn. The days that followed offered no urgent reason to get out of bed.

And just like that, the questions Bobby and I have talked about for years stopped being theoretical:

How do you hold yourself accountable when there is nothing you have to do?
How do you find fulfillment and purpose when work is no longer your identity?

When I graduated from CRNA school in 2017, those questions would have terrified me. The program was brutal—80+ hour weeks—and becoming a CRNA had been my primary focus. Over time, as I saw more of the healthcare system I didn’t love, it became easier to separate Mary the person from Mary the CRNA. Starting locum work in 2022 only accelerated that shift. The gaps between contracts grew—from three weeks, to two months (including French Polynesia), to nearly four months (New Zealand and more), to a six-month “honeymoon,” and eventually to multi-month stretches. We are not trust-fund babies; we have worked and invested our way here. Still, each longer break made returning to work feel harder and as our investments and trading got better, the money was no longer a motivating factor.

By the time we left for France in May 2026, I was pregnant, we had our one-year visas, and the desire to keep working had quietly faded. I petitioned my last Florida position with less than two weeks to go before moving to France in August 2026. Technically I am still employed there. Practically, the “I have to work” excuse no longer exists—especially on a visa that prohibits it.

Now we sit in a marina waiting out weather, and I am face-to-face with the reality we only used to discuss: there are no acceptable excuses left. I have to be my own source of structure, movement, and meaning. No one else will change my life or my mindset. That responsibility is mine.

We have talked about the backup plan—sell the boat, return to Jacksonville, live a “normal” life. Neither of us thinks that would be terrible. But we also agree that normal is easy, average, and not really who we are.

So here is to figuring it out when there is nothing to do. I can only complete so many Sudokus. I am nearly finished with the Bible. I don’t want to spend my days staring at screens. I am experimenting with new recipes, keeping the boat cleaner, chasing 10k steps (harder in 30-knot winds and while on anchor), and staying consistent with the 30-for-30 and Garmin challenges. If the exercise doesn’t happen early, it doesn’t happen. That is on me.

I have learned this lesson many times before: it is easier to stay dedicated when time is scarce. When time is abundant, “later” becomes dangerously easy. If you are thinking about it, do it—and do it now.

It was one bad day.
Then he just slept in that car, since he had nowhere else to go, all that day and into the next. Somehow at some point, a week had passed and the money was beginning to run out. It was a lifestyle of increments this way.
He read incessantly, partially out of spite for the same reason he never did drugs; because he was loath to be what anyone thought or expected of him. Hated the involuntary and to him burdensome weight of their expectations piled on. The other part was because his only real ally on the outs was apparently some friendly old book store owner who let him sleep outside her shop so long as he was peaceful.
I grew up reading and he personally introduced me to many important titles in our shared time.
You don't get a name like Alistair ...or his last name... by being poor. He was not born and did not live without opportunities; not for work, food, education, or housing. Nothing. He told me his father had offered him a job at his own enterprise. Pure nepotistic guaranteed placement. Just show up. But Al had no interest.
He looked on and he saw a world either indifferent or openly hateful of him, and he saw no reason to be complicit with a machine intent on devouring him. In fact, he explained to me how the homeless of California receive so many opportunities they more or less received a paycheck for not working.
If one of them truly wanted to claw their way up, bootstraps or not, it wouldn't be something they had to pull up alone. There were programs, funding, aid, shelters, cards, etc. No, he said.. truth is, most homeless people WANT to be homeless.
They've opted out. They see the game and they don't want to play it. Try it, he'd say. Walk up to a homeless man and offer him a job. People do it every day. Every day they're still out there.
Had a serious talk over the Chess board one day. Look around, I say. We're on the line here. We're on the precipice now. I don't believe either of us are evil men, but if we're surrounded by it, steeped in it, and beginning to share its culture and incentives... how long can we balance on the edge without walking it back, or falling off?
Because Every Single Aggressor here.. whatever flavor.. wife beater, grandma robber, and diddler has the exact same boring tale don't they?
It's not my fault. The world did it to me first. They started it. I'm just getting even to pass it on to the next person.. and then act like I have no part in it being this way. Playing victim to the wickedness of our own design.
To my shock, he actually did end up calling his dad for the first time in years, reconciling. I heard it all since there was nowhere private for me to leave him. It went how I knew it would on their end; eagerness to jump at this chance to make good with their son.
We exchanged e-mails, addresses, whatever I could remember after months of the anxiety of the place ripping up my brains. Swore I'd keep in touch and intended it at the time.
A few years later I got a letter from him. ...but I never wrote back. He was on course and I was a call back to a darker time for both of us I didn't really want him to touch.. and a few years after that he was gone.
I don't see the addicts or the desperate as less dangerous or more sane after these experiences, as any wiser to befriend and I wouldn't do it again, but as Doc says
without condemning or condoning, I understand.

text:
Hmm - Dirty Dick Durbin has selective regret ???

"Today’s scorched earth politics didn’t come out of nowhere, and many Americans don’t remember the deliberate decisions Democrats made to raise the temperature during the Obama years. Will any Democrats—or Republicans for that matter—learn from Sen. Dick Durbin’s apparent second thoughts on blowing up the filibuster?

The Illinois Senator will soon leave office, and this week he offered reflections to the Washington Sun. One line that caught our attention concerned the late Democratic leader Harry Reid’s 2013 decision to blow up the filibuster on lower court judges.

“He was warned ahead of time there would be retribution.” Sen. Durbin said. “It all occurred and we’re still suffering from that. Harry, before he passed away, he and I talked about it. He said the Senate will never be the same.” Sen. Durbin excused his late colleague, saying Reid felt “he had no choice” and that Republican Mitch McConnell started it by holding up some nominees.

Mr. McConnell is the Senate father of the conservative Supreme Court majority, but Harry Reid surely helped. Reid’s precedent to nuke the 60-vote threshold for confirming appellate judges and other nominees paved the way for Mr. McConnell and Republicans to later confirm Justices with 51 votes.

Don’t buy Sen. Durbin’s potted history that the brawler from Nevada had no choice. Reid wanted to pack the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals with three Obama nominees to wave through President Obama’s regulatory ambitions, and he was willing to roll over the minority to do it. Reid could have worked the normal political rough and tumble with the GOP. The Senate that year confirmed Sri Srinivasan to the D.C. Circuit, 97 to zip.

This history is worth recalling amid today’s bipartisan clamor to bust the filibuster for legislation. Mr. Durbin in 2022 voted for a Democratic attempt to whittle down the legislative filibuster to pass a voting bill, which would have functionally ended that institutional check on the majority."

text:
Kojagara Lakshmi + Sharad Purnima

An interesting Moon transit tonight..

Moon is in Revati, the final nakshatra, and enters Ashwini, the 1st nakshatra, at 7:22 PM tonight.

So on Sharad Purnima itself, Moon completes the entire nakshatra cycle & begins again.

also most people know about keeping kheer in moonlight.. but there is something more interesting about Kojagara itself.

The Kojagara tradition says that at Nishita, Maa Lakshmi moves asking this question.

निशीथे वरदा लक्ष्मीः को जागर्तीति भाषिणी

Ko jagarti?.. Who is awake?

Another detail many people dont know.. Kojagara remembers Maa Lakshmi along with Indra seated on Airavata. Coconut and chipitaka.. flattened rice are also mentioned in the tradition.

So kheer is beautiful Sharad Purnima tradition, but it is not the only way 

One should light a ghee diya before Maa Lakshmi tonight
and offer what is followed in ur family.. milk, kheer, coconut, poha.

If u are keeping kheer under the moonlight, place it after 8:10 PM once Moon crosses the Gandanta into Ashwini.

Recite Shri Suktam if u have learned it, or take Maa Lakshmi name and remain awake during Nishita kaala

One practical thing I would also do tonight..

Before 7:22 PM, Moon is in Pisces and in Revati, ruled by Mercury.
So clean your wallet & the place where you keep money.
Remove useless receipts, expired cards, broken things kept around ur money space.

And if money comes regularly but somehow never stays, open ur bank statement once tonight and look into the whole month expense while keeping Maa in mind.

Tomorrow morning, keep a few grains of akshata or a coin offered in tonight puja inside that cleaned wallet.

Jai Maa Mahalakshmi 🙏

text:
Barack Obama delivered a pointed warning at a Democratic campaign rally in Cleveland, Ohio, on 24 October, criticising Trump’s war on Iran. He argued that diplomacy had prevented Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons without firing a missile, while Trump abandoned the deal and started what Obama called an “unnecessary war that nobody asked for”. He highlighted American casualties, depleted weapons stocks, damage to US bases, rising fuel prices and Iran’s growing leverage over the Strait of Hormuz.

The strategic failure is larger than one administration. Washington replaced a negotiated constraint with military escalation, exposing the limits of coercion as an instrument of foreign policy. The costs fall not only on American households but also on closely aligned governments across West Asia and Asia, whose security and economic stability depend on a US-led order that increasingly exposes them to regional retaliation.

This is the structural danger of America’s forever wars: mounting military expenditure, disrupted energy markets and declining credibility without a durable political settlement. Iran’s leverage over Hormuz demonstrates how a regional power withstands superior military force and raises the costs of intervention. If Washington persists, the result risks accelerating regional realignment and imposing a lasting challenge to US hegemony and the interests of those who depend on it. Diplomacy offered a way to constrain nuclear proliferation; abandoning it has made the strategic problem harder to resolve.

#BarackObama #Iran #USForeignPolicy #StraitOfHormuz #Geopolitics

1. Starlink isn't "neutral" as you say. If it was, the Russians would have access to it too. Not that I am in favor of that, but it is not neutral. 2. The same private company, SpaceX, delivers both Starlink and Starshield, the military version of the same tech, which has no restrictions on such "senseless slaughter".

text:
THE BORDERLESS HOTEL: ENGINEERED DIVERSITY AND THE FALLACY OF THE CORPORATE FILTER

PRESENTED BY DIOGENES OF THE REIPUBLICAE AMERICANAE

The contemporary internal friction within the American right illuminates a profound structural contradiction in the modern political landscape. Prominent Indian American conservative figures like Dinesh D’Souza and Vivek Ramaswamy have recently emerged as prime targets of intense anti Indian hostility from the populist fringes they long sought to cultivate. D’Souza, who engineered a decades long career constructing polemics against Black political mobilization, recently vocalized grievances regarding "anti-GOP racism" and the ascendancy of nationalist factions within his own coalition. For the observer, there is little incentive to offer sympathy for a media pundit reaping the predictable whirlwind of a political culture he actively subsidized. 

Yet, beneath the individual hypocrisy of elite commentators lies a deeper, systemic reality that the native born workforce readily detects: a distinct cultural elitism and a technocratic arrogance that systematically devalues the domestic population. Everyday citizens read the room, observing the structural decline of their communities while a highly insulated immigrant class treats the nation as a temporary, lucrative stepping stone.

This tension is not a matter of irrational racial animus directed at arrivals from India or China. The institutional failure rests entirely with the federal government, which has prioritized these specific pipelines at the explicit behest of technology conglomerates and wealthy corporate donors who flood political coffers to protect their profit margins. This corporate selection bias relies on a major statistical distortion: presenting highly filtered guest worker pipelines as if they represent a per capita reflection of their home countries, while comparing them to the entirety of the unfiltered American population. If a system pulls exclusively from the upper tier of a nation of over a billion people, it will naturally secure exceptional technical talent. But this is an artificial corporate standard, not a civil reality. When unfiltered American capability was tested on a national scale, it was local, homegrown talent that achieved the 1969 Apollo moon landing.

The technocratic alliance systematically avoids investing in domestic talent because an independent citizen cannot be easily controlled. American workers operate within a legacy of individual freedom and a standard of living that demands fair compensation. The corporate model seeks to circumvent this contract entirely. By utilizing the H-1B framework, corporate elites import visa holders whose legal residency status is bound entirely to a single employer. This creates a modern variant of corporate feudalism: the visa holder is structurally incentivized to remain compliant and accept suppressed wages, because any workplace resistance carries the immediate threat of termination and deportation. This rigid organizational obedience aligns with the conditioning of highly stratified societies where traditional hierarchies, such as the Brahmin class structure, require individuals to navigate absolute differences in status and power.

This societal divide is laid bare when analyzing official participation metrics. On paper, the curated Indian American demographic stands at the apex of the domestic economic food chain, commanding the highest median household income in the country at over $150,000 annually. Yet, when evaluating participation in the physical defense of the republic, this demographic registers a profound statistical absence on the front lines of the military. The arrogance of the modern technocratic class manifests when these individuals assume that financial metrics and cognitive credentials make them superior to the citizens performing military service. It is a fundamental clash of worldviews. An elite, corporate centered perspective measures human value entirely by material wealth, looking down on the working class communities that fill the ranks of the infantry. But a multi generational patriotic perspective rejects this hierarchy entirely, recognizing that advanced academic credentials hold no greater moral weight than the high risk labor of national defense.

A stark contrast to this dynamic is found by examining Filipino Americans, who serve as a prime counter example of multi dimensional integration. Unlike isolated technical enclaves, Filipino Americans simultaneously occupy high-ranking spaces across both economic and civic spectrums. They possess exceptionally high educational attainment and strong household income averages, yet they concurrently maintain an incredibly high and disproportionate rate of active duty and veteran military service, particularly within the United States Navy. This dual track is deeply rooted in historical geography and decades of shared sacrifice. The Philippines was historically defined by close institutional ties with the United States military from the structural legacies of Subic Bay to the shared blood spilled during World War II, Bataan, Corregidor, and the logistics pipelines of the Vietnam War. Because of this security partnership, Filipino arrivals were familiarized with the American military ethos long before arriving on domestic soil, viewing the armed forces as a primary vehicle for national belonging and shared civic duty.

This history exposes the core necessity of cultural deference. It is an undeniable historical fact that India possesses an ancient civilization that constructed foundational mathematical concepts like zero and the decimal system. India has a heritage of immense intellectual power, and no Western observer can dispute the grandeur of that history. But while that civilizational pride is justified, it does not erase the basic boundary of sovereignty: the newcomer chose to come to America; the native population did not move to Bombay. To enter another nation’s house is to accept an unwritten contract of deference. Showing respect for the host does not mean erasing one’s heritage; it means acknowledging that the existing house was built, paid for, and physically secured by the families who have been holding the line for centuries. When a group enjoys the stability, laws, and massive economic upsides of the American republic while remaining completely detached from the high-risk physical burdens of its defense, it creates a visible, transactional imbalance.

To understand the historical weight of this structural breakdown, one must look directly at how the federal government has historically manipulated these demographic formulas. Under the National Origins Act of 1924, lawmakers were entirely straightforward about their motives. Operating at the height of the early eugenics movement, they explicitly designed a rigid quota system to prevent what they openly described as the creation of a "mongrel nation." By anchoring immigration caps to late 19th century census numbers, they deliberately restricted entry to white immigrants from Northern and Western Europe, establishing a stark legal precedent for top down state engineering.

This rigid enforcement of ethnic preservation set the stage for the intense cultural friction of the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The massive influx of European immigrants including Italians, Irish, and Slavic peoples arrived at Ellis Island facing deep hostility from the established Anglo Saxon Protestant majority. They were castigated and viewed as an entirely separate, incompatible demographic that threatened the existing cultural core, tested aggressively against the old boundaries of the 1700s naturalization standards. Yet, that friction was successfully resolved over two generations because those families actively yielded to the broader American construct and paid the ultimate civic price. The children and grandchildren of these Ellis Island immigrants shed their regional accents, adopted the native language, and stepped forward during the mass mobilization of World War II. When Italian Americans made up roughly 10% of the U.S. Army, they spilled blood on global battlefields and earned their place as a foundational pillar of the domestic population. They did not remain a separate group within; they grew up to be viewed as white people and became part of the standard citizenry through shared hardship and physical defense.

The historic stability of this organic assimilation framework was shattered by the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965, which replaced cultural yielding with engineered diversity. If the state could explicitly prioritize white nations under the 1924 act, and then completely pivot in 1965 to prioritize predominantly countries of color, it proves that immigration policies are entirely a product of government planning rather than natural evolution. In 1960, the country was roughly 90% white. Today, that number has dropped precipitously to nearly 60% within a single lifespan a massive, rapid transformation that has completely outpaced the natural mechanics of assimilation. This structural manipulation is even more visible in recent decades: in the year 2000, the Asian population sat at roughly 2%, and today, it has surged to over 6%.

Modern political correctness makes people afraid to speak their minds on this reality, but a core philosophical truth remains: while organic diversity in nature provides genetic strength, artificial diversity manufactured by human engineering is an entirely different matter. Nature changes things slowly and organically over vast timelines, which creates resilience. But whenever human planning and corporate intervention try to artificially force a new demographic formula overnight, they inevitably disrupt the balance. This artificial fracturing suggests a deeper, more unsettling intent from the powers that be. The federal apparatus actively resists the concept of a single, unified American identity, choosing instead to celebrate and maintain distinct tribal enclaves. By keeping the population divided into separate demographic categories, the ruling class ensures that citizens cannot form a cohesive, resistant front against administrative overreach.

The primary casualty of this engineered tribalism is the erosion of a single national language. A shared language is the single most powerful engine of organic assimilation. For the republic to maintain its foundational strength, English must be the sole national requirement. While local municipal governments should remain free to print handbills or notices in Spanish if a town council democratically votes to do so, the nationwide standard must remain absolute: you learn English, and you assimilate into the construct. When people learn the language, they naturally assimilate better. The intentional push away from a singular linguistic standard reveals that the current system does not want the population to truly unify.

For most of America’s existence, the nation operated under a distinct Anglo Saxon, English, and Scotch Irish cultural flavor. Admitting this historical fact is not a statement of exclusion; it is an acknowledgment of the foundational architecture that allowed the country to thrive. When you remove the basic requirement of linguistic and cultural yielding, you are left with an environment where newcomers are discouraged from truly entering the house. By treating the country as a borderless hotel rather than a sacred civic home, the technocratic class trades national honor for the chilly, short-term efficiencies of a global workspace.

In a fair nation, an advanced academic degree holds the exact same peerage as a combat infantryman badge. Until incoming corporate guests show a baseline humility, take their shoes off upon entering the temple, and fully yield to the English-speaking American construct, the nation stops being a cohesive republic and becomes just a commercial station.

🎵❤️🙏🏻 I STILL PRAY — A TABLE FOR EVERY FAITH 🌍✌️

---

🤣 WARNING: ANOTHER BLOODY SONG ABOUT LOVE, PEACE & HUMANITY! 🤣❤️

BROOOOOOO! 😂

I KNOW, I KNOW… Another song that's far too caring, compassionate and respectful!

Not enough swearing, cruelty, hatred or filthy language to attract the thousands of views my angrier songs seem to get! 🤣

THIS ONE IS DIFFERENT.

This is JUST MY PERSONAL PRAYER, MY BELIEFS AND MY RESPECT FOR EVERY FAITH, including my own belief in that mysterious WHITE LIGHT FROM THE FORCES ABOVE US ALL. 🙏🏻🤍

AMEN! ❤️

---

🙏🏻❤️ MY PRAYER FOR HUMANITY ❤️🙏🏻

Today, I don't pray for wealth, power, fame or a throne above anybody else.

I pray for HUMANITY.

I pray for the children who haven't yet been born, the families separated by war, the parents struggling to feed their children, the lonely, the grieving, the forgotten and those who have lost faith in the kindness of other human beings.

I pray that one day we might stop allowing our differences to become reasons for hatred.

To my Buddhist brothers and sisters, may compassion and wisdom continue guiding your paths. ☸️🙏🏻

To my Christian brothers and sisters, may the teachings of Jesus inspire forgiveness, mercy and love. ✝️❤️

To my Muslim brothers and sisters, may Allah's mercy bring peace, protection and blessings to your families. ☪️🙏🏻

ALLAHU AKBAR — GOD IS GREAT!

To my Jewish brothers and sisters, may your families live in safety, dignity and peace. ✡️❤️

To my Hindu, Sikh, Jain, Bahá'í and Taoist brothers and sisters, may your teachings of kindness, service, harmony and respect continue inspiring humanity. 🕉️🙏🏻

To First Peoples, their elders, ancestors and spiritual traditions, I offer my respect and willingness to listen. ❤️

And to every other religion, spiritual belief, and every person who follows no religion at all…

YOU ARE NOT FORGOTTEN. YOU ARE EQUALLY HUMAN. 🌍❤️

I don't ask anyone to abandon their religion.

I don't ask anyone to believe in my understanding of the universe.

I don't claim to know whose prayers are heard, what lies beyond death, or whether the mysterious white light I imagine is something anybody else will ever experience.

THOSE ARE MY PERSONAL BELIEFS, NOT TRUTHS I DEMAND FROM OTHERS.

What I do believe is that we can find common ground without surrendering our individual faiths.

RELIGIOUS UNITY DOESN'T HAVE TO MEAN RELIGIOUS UNIFORMITY.

Imagine a world where a Christian, a Muslim, a Buddhist, a Jew, a Hindu, a Sikh, an atheist and every other human being could sit together…

Not to argue over whose God is greater.

Not to compete over whose ancestors suffered more.

Not to demand that anybody surrender their beliefs.

But simply to ask:

"HOW CAN WE MAKE LIFE BETTER FOR THE CHILDREN WHO COME AFTER US?" ❤️

I pray for a world where no child inherits hatred simply because of the religion, nationality or culture they were born into.

Where disagreements are settled through conversations instead of violence.

Where compassion is not mistaken for weakness.

Where forgiveness does not mean abandoning accountability.

And where the hungry are fed before the powerful argue over who deserves the credit.

🙏🏻 LET LOVE BE OUR LANGUAGE.

❤️ LET COMPASSION SHOW THE WAY.

🌍 LET EVERYONE KEEP THE FAITH THEY WISH TO CARRY.

To my departed family and friends, I send my love beyond what my eyes can see.

To those still struggling, may tomorrow bring a little more hope.

To those filled with anger, may peace find a way into your hearts.

And to those who have caused harm, may you find the courage to change, make amends and choose a better path.

I DON'T NEED EVERYONE TO BELIEVE WHAT I BELIEVE.

I simply hope we can believe in treating one another with dignity.

Because whether we pray in a church, mosque, temple, synagogue, beneath the open sky or quietly within our own hearts…

WE ALL SHARE THIS ONE PLANET. 🌍

#IStillPray #ATableForEveryFaith #TRGLOBAL #ThePeoplesResolution #ReligiousUnity #OneHumanity #LetLoveBeOurLanguage

text:
TWO BANKS COMPLETE LOAN PAYMENT USING TOKENIZED DEPOSITS ON ETHERIUM

Texas banks Vantage Bank and Rio Bank completed a loan participation payment using tokenized bank deposits on Ethereum.

Processed through Hazel Network and Participate, the transaction involved a shared loan in which one bank originated the loan and the other purchased a portion. The participating bank then received its share of principal and interest.

Traditionally, these payments require separate bank transfers, accounting updates and notifications. In this transaction, the receiving bank obtained its payment in less than three minutes.

Loan balances and payment notices updated automatically as funds moved, linking settlement with accounting.

Unlike cryptocurrencies, tokenized deposits represent money held within the banking system.

The companies plan to offer similar automation across Participate’s network of more than 750 banks. The transaction shows how blockchain infrastructure could connect traditional payments with automated recordkeeping and reduce manual work in shared-loan settlement.

text:
"George Washington was apparently seen throwing silver dollars across the Rappahannock River, which in 1936 was said to measure 272 feet in width and even wider in Washington’s day.
The founding father’s reputed feat was likely not possible, but Walter Johnson was designated to pitch a silver dollar from one riverbank to the other to see if it could be done at all.
A local newspaper called that bet and put up $50 of its own.
A reward was issued for the return of the coin should Johnson connect with the other side.
Lou Gehrig tossed a coin across New York’s Harlem River to prove it could be done.
"Maybe I can’t throw that far, but there’s one thing certain, if George Washington did it, I can."
Walter Johnson.
A few days before the event, the 48-year-old Johnson sent a lighthearted telegram to City leaders:
"I am practising with a dollar against my barn door.
Arm getting stronger, barn door weaker."
On February 20, The Associated Press reported:
"Unable to wait until Saturday, when Walter Johnson tries his arm against the legendary prowess of George Washington, citizens are trying to settle the matter among themselves;
But with iron washers, not silver coins.
All tries have fallen short."
U.S. Rep. Sol Bloom had offered 20-to-1 odds against a successful throw, and over 4,000 people gathered along the snowy riverbank in the 27 degree weather.
Walter Johnson came dressed in a suit.
The footing was icy and muddy.
He took off his suit jacket for his attempts.
According to Shirley Povich, Johnson handed his jacket to the famous White House correspondent for the Washington Post, Edward T. Folliard.
Years later Folliard, recounting the many events and famous people he had covered, said holding Walter Johnson’s jacket that day:
"Was my biggest thrill."
The coin was marked:
"Walter Johnson threw this dollar across the Rappahannock River, February 22, 1936" cleared the river by more than 10 feet!!
Walter Johnson`s throw was measured at 286 feet.
"Walter Johnson threw it over with the same easy grace he once used in fanning Ty Cobb, Tris Speaker and "Ping" Bodie, and so doing he brought to Fredericksburg something of that joy that was denied to Mudville when the mighty Casey struck out."
Edward T. Folliard, "The Washington Post".
After it was all said and done, Rep. Sol Bloom refused to pay the citizens the $100,000 he owed.
Bloom insisted that 18th-century maps depicted the Rappahannock at Fredericksburg to be more than 1,300-feet wide:
"Farther than Washington or anyone could throw a coin."
City officials pooh-poohed Bloom's that claim about the river’s width.

text:
"SANCTIONS ON A SUPREME COURT ​JUSTICE
Beattie is a former White House speechwriter fired in 2018 after addressing an event frequented by white nationalists. He’s also the architect of "free speech diplomacy, opens new tab," a policy advocated by Trump allies that seeks to punish nations they accuse of censoring right-wing speech by US citizens, companies and global right-wing allies.
The United States has accused Brazil Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes of violating free speech rights by jailing Brazilians for political social-media posts and by censoring content of US social-media companies. Moraes has argued he was ridding social media of fake news that undermined public faith in Brazil's democratic institutions.
Pita, a conservative Venezuelan-American, is among many in Rubio's orbit who view Lula as a threat to US interests in Latin America. Rubio has been a key leader in ​the administration’s aggressive policy in the region, which has included an invasion of Venezuela to oust its president, an oil blockade of Cuba, and military attacks on suspected drug boats from Latin America.
Beattie and Pita were drawn to the Bolsonaro family’s right-wing politics, their antipathy towards Lula, and the idea that Jair Bolsonaro was a victim of abuses by ​Brazil's Supreme Court.
Like Trump in the 2020 US election, Bolsonaro refused to concede he lost Brazil’s 2022 presidential vote, triggering riots by supporters who stormed government buildings. The Supreme Court convicted him in September 2025 of plotting a coup to remain in power.
Before the conviction, in early 2025, the Bolsonaros were aggressively lobbying Washington for sanctions under the Global Magnitsky Human Rights Accountability Act ‌against Moraes, who had ⁠led criminal investigations into Jair Bolsonaro. The act is a 2016 federal law allowing US sanctions against foreign individuals responsible for human-rights abuses or severe corruption.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, whose department administers Magnitsky sanctions through OFAC, offered no opposition, the former official said.

TERRORIST DESIGNATIONS
The Bolsonaro family was also pushing for Washington ​to designate Brazil's top gangs – the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) and Comando Vermelho (CV) – as ​terrorist organizations. They believed such a designation would hurt Lula, who some opponents ⁠have criticized for failing to control crime.
Eduardo Bolsonaro had become friends with Pita through US conservative circles, and both supported the effort to designate the gangs as terrorist groups.
In May 2025, Pita joined a US delegation, opens new tab that visited Jair Bolsonaro at his residence in Brasilia as he awaited his trial, according to public announcements at the time. Also in the group: David Gamble, the State Department’s top sanctions official at the time.
Back in Washington, Pita asked State sanctions officials to explore how terrorist designations like those announced against Mexican cartels in ​February 2025 could be used in Brazil, one former official said.
Nearly a year later, in May 2026 – after Pita was promoted to a new job that pulled him out of Brazil affairs – presidential contender Flavio Bolsonaro met with Beattie and Deputy ​Secretary of State Christopher Landau in Washington to discuss "the ⁠urgency of designating the PCC and the Comando Vermelho as foreign terrorist organizations," according to an X post by right-wing influencer Paulo Figueiredo that included photos of the attendees.

BACKFIRES AND SETBACKS
In July 2025, Washington also announced a series of other measures against Brazil, including the revocations of eight Supreme Court justices' visas and 50% tariffs on Brazilian goods, citing the "persecution" of Jair Bolsonaro.
Reuters could not determine what, if any, role Beattie or Pita played in the additional measures. But if they were intended to undermine Lula, many of them backfired, according to political analysts in Brazil."

text:
Singularity Watch, Day 10 — October 25, 2026

SECURITY

The Brotli flaw spreads. CVE-2026-111497, the remote code execution flaw in Google's Brotli compression library first exposed through Node.js and nicknamed "Node2Shell," turns out to reach far beyond Node [1]. Node patched it on October 21, but the bug lives in Brotli's decoder, which is compiled into many other runtimes and packages, often under other names.

Semgrep, a code security company, said its researchers Diptendu Kar and Kurt Boberg found 433 package entries across 12 software ecosystems that bundle the vulnerable decoder [1]. So far about 71% have no fix, and most existing fixes are alpha or early releases. Thirty-eight entries bundle Brotli older than version 1.0.3, some dating to 2016.

Aikido, another security firm, said the flaw has evolved into "HTTP2Shell": many libraries and applications that speak HTTP are exposed to remote code execution before any login, through Brotli decompression [2]. Aikido said fixes are not yet available for every affected service and advised watching for Brotli 1.2.1 upgrades.

LiteLLM's root cause. LiteLLM, a popular open-source gateway that lets software route requests to many AI models, explained how attackers published a malicious version of its Python package [3][4]. On May 27, a configuration file containing the master key to a LiteLLM Agent Platform deployment was committed to a public GitHub repository. The commit was overwritten, but the key was never revoked.

On October 10, an attacker used that key to enter the Agent Platform and extract a GitHub token belonging to the organization's owner, which was not scoped down [4]. With it, the attacker stole maintainers' tokens, overrode branch protection, repointed the release pipeline to a lookalike repository, and on October 21 published LiteLLM 1.107.0 to PyPI, the main Python package index.

The malicious release ran automatically whenever Python started, even if LiteLLM was never imported, stealing credentials and installing an hourly backdoor [4]. An Upwind researcher reported it within half an hour, and PyPI quarantined it that afternoon. LiteLLM said a release safeguard tied to a physical device had been relaxed that week to speed up bug-fix releases.

Pillow. A critical flaw in Pillow, the most widely used image library for Python, lets an attacker run operating system commands just by controlling the name of an EPS image file, which Pillow passes unchecked to the Ghostscript program [5][6]. Pillow is downloaded about 436 million times a month, according to OX Security.

The fix, Pillow 13.0.0, released October 16, also closes several other serious bugs [6]. One of them, a crash in JPEG thumbnail handling, was found by Anthropic using Claude to study open-source security, part of an effort that has turned up hundreds of flaws. Another had sat in Pillow since 2013.

A Japanese cloud shut down. GMO Internet, a major Japanese internet infrastructure company, shut down its entire Onamae Desktop Cloud service from 4:00 a.m. Japan time on October 21 after finding that a third party had installed malicious programs on customer servers; 26,739 servers were potentially affected [7][8]. The service is widely used to run automated forex trading bots.

GMO later confirmed customer information was taken and that some customers reported trades they did not make [9]. It will not restart the compromised system, will pay every customer a 5,000 yen goodwill payment, and will compensate realized losses from unauthorized trades.

The security commentator Bala reported that more than 70 brokers were affected, that OANDA Japan froze withdrawals, and that GMO asked Japan's government to use new "active cyber defense" powers, in force since October 1, to trace and neutralize the attackers' infrastructure [7].

Inside the smart TV. A reverse engineer and penetration tester who posts as log4j has been publishing findings from rooting a Samsung TV. According to the posts, a TV without a microphone looks for connected devices that have one, such as a soundbar, and sends audio to Bixby, Samsung's assistant [10].

The TV also classifies the sounds it hears before reporting back, with dog-barking and baby-crying event counters built into its telemetry [10].

The same researcher said OpenAI banned the account after the work tripped "daybreak," apparently an automated abuse detector; the post did not explain the term [11]. The researcher said OpenAI was never used to find or exploit vulnerabilities, only for local reverse engineering.

Separately, the creator Vaibhav Sisinty reported, citing a Reddit post, that Claude now halts mid-answer when asked to write a "Reverse Engineer Anything" playbook, a popular workflow for dissecting firmware [12]. He noted the timing after a viral post on rooting a Samsung TV, said Anthropic has not confirmed any change, and said some users report the workflow still works.

The sensory scientist and chief executive John Ennis suggested TVs are being rooted in the wake of what he called the "eMudra debacle," and that cheap televisions may have been subsidized by spying [13]. That refers to the eMudhra certificate authority keys compromise recorded in this chronicle on Day 9 [14].

"The only way out is through." Eric S. Raymond, the veteran open-source programmer and author, wrote that people are calling the AI-driven flood of discoveries the "Bugpocalypse" [15]. He argued against locking frontier models away, since Chinese open-weight models will spread regardless, and said the finite stock of software defects can now be fixed with "a million friendly robots."

An a16z partner who posts as YODELAGARZA predicted it is "almost certain" that governments will take critical infrastructure offline within a year to patch it before AI-powered attackers get in [16]. He said banks that got access to Glasswing six to eight months ago have "been doing nothing but patching" since.

Glasswing is Anthropic's controlled program giving partners access to its Claude Mythos Preview model to find and fix flaws in critical software. Anthropic reported that it and about 50 partners found more than ten thousand high- or critical-severity vulnerabilities in the program's first month [17].

COMPUTE AND CAPITAL

GPUs gaining value. The venture firm a16z reported that AI chip rental rates have risen since January 1: the Nvidia H200 is up about 160%, the B200 about 120%, the RTX PRO 6000 about 65%, and the H100 about 35%; even the six-year-old A100 rents for more [18].

One explanation, a16z said: token demand on OpenRouter, a marketplace that routes requests across AI models, rose about 27 times since last November, from roughly 6 trillion to 165 trillion tokens per week [19]. Open-weight models now handle about 72% of those tokens, up from 28%.

Where the money goes. Investor Chamath Palihapitiya said 1% of companies account for 90% of AI token spending and that 80% of them are spending money raised from venture capitalists [20]. He called this circular flow a structural problem until AI spreads beyond the startup ecosystem.

AI RESEARCH

A bug in softmax. Jon Barron, a principal research scientist at Google DeepMind, reported that all existing implementations of softmax and cross-entropy, two of the most basic functions in deep learning, used in JAX, PyTorch and textbooks, contain two subtle numerical bugs [21].

The paper, by Barron, Dan Gnanapragasam and Michael Tschannen, shows that at high confidence the target gradient rounds to zero, which causes the sudden loss spikes known as "slingshots" during grokking, the delayed generalization seen in some training runs [22]. A rewrite in log space fixes both bugs.

Agents as organizations. General Reasoning introduced Reinforcement Learning from Collective Rewards, which trains language models as organizations of agents sharing a message board, and used it to train Avalon-M1-Mini, a 120-billion-parameter model [23]. The company reported learned hierarchies, division of labor, and more hiring of verifiers and testers.

Chief executive Ross Taylor said that in one experiment a CEO agent told to decide whom to hire chose lead engineers and middle managers, which he said economic theory predicts [23].

Models misjudge their own reasoning. A University of Chicago paper, summarized by Rohan Paul, found that a language model's own account of what drives its decision is a poor guide to what actually varies across its answers [24]. In forecasts of 59 March Madness games, the models' predicted key questions matched the real ones less often than a random shuffle.

The authors recommend sampling many answers and studying where they disagree [24].

AGENTS AND TOOLS

Software engineer Jack Ellis, who builds the analytics company Fathom, said he was "100% sold" on Cursor Projects, in which a coordinator agent spins up other agents and pull requests instead of one agent per task [25].

Prerelease builds of Grok Bot 0.77 show a calling feature that can dial a number, wait on hold, press keys and be transferred while the user watches a live transcript, plus Tailscale private-network support, payments settings, and bot sharing, according to accounts that track builds [26]. Such features may change before release.

Every Mac on macOS 27 now includes a free, offline language model in the Terminal through an "fm" command, according to Alvaro Cintas, a computer science professor. It offers an OpenAI-compatible local endpoint and a 4,096-token limit per session [27].

PEOPLE

Anthony Morris, who created the desktop version of Claude Code, Anthropic's AI coding tool, announced he has left Anthropic and will share his next step soon [28]. Thariq Shihipar, a lead engineer who helped scale Claude Code for more than a year, has also left, as Anthropic prepares for a public offering [29].

Posts speculated that SpaceXAI hired both; that remains unconfirmed [30].

SPACE AND DEVICES

According to an account that follows SpaceX, Elon Musk said on the SpaceX third-quarter call that the company's Louisiana Starbase will ultimately have 20 launch pads, not 10 [31]. The account said the real limit is how many Starship launches the FAA approves each year.

Musk also predicted that phones will become "an edge node for AI inference," with no operating system or apps, where AI on servers talks to AI on the device and generates real-time video of anything the user wants [32].

ASTROHACKER

Astrohacker's chief executive wrote, "i have my own team of super intelligent agents. this is not a movie. this is reality" [33]. He judged OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra the best model for code review, finding issues other models miss [34].

He also rejected Palo Alto Networks chief executive Nikesh Arora's comparison of unguarded AI to "a nuclear bomb," calling it a false analogy [35][36].

We're living in it.

text:
friday ends and the body reaches for the old room.

junk on the counter.

a show you will not remember.

the thumb doing laps until the night is gone and you call it recovery.

that is not recovery.

that is the default, reloading.

the hard week did not break you.

it just sent you home to whatever you have installed as normal.

and normal, for a lot of people, is the leak.

food that argues with tomorrow.

a screen that spends the hours you said you would get back.

you wake on sunday already behind a monday that has not started.

i have had weeks off the rails.

wrong food.

wrong hours.

the work going soft at the edges.

the weekend shows up and the old setting offers itself.

collapse.

earn it.

you were bad, so be worse, then start clean on monday like the mess was a strategy.

i do not take that deal anymore.

the weekend is the reset into the other default.

work.

not a performance of work.

scheming.

planning.

the idea that has been sitting half finished.

the piece of content that only exists if you sit with it while the street is quiet.

you use the two days to climb back into the mode, then you keep the mode.

next week.

the week after.

it will wave.

you are not a machine.

there will be a day the standard slips and a night you need to actually stop.

fine.

true rest is a planned door, not a hole you fall through because friday was loud.

if you have been at it, fully, for the weeks behind you, the stop is clean.

if you have been leaking, the stop is just another leak with better lighting.

look at where the hours go when nobody is scoring you.

cut the ones that leave no residue.

keep the ones that are real rest, scheduled, after the work has already been the climate.

the default is the life.

change that, and the crazy friday stops being a verdict.

it becomes a night you walk out of, back into a setting that was already waiting.

ylo out...

text:
Yes, the monarchy was deeply implicated in the slave trade. But not the British monarchy.
The biggest African slavers were not pirates or bandits. They were kings. In the 1750s, King Tegbesu of Dahomey, in present-day Benin, was reported to be making £250,000 a year from selling slaves. That astronomical sum, equivalent to perhaps £45 million today, was vastly more than any British aristocrat
While Tegbesu was trafficking human beings, the future George III, who had recently become Prince of Wales, was becoming a convinced abolitionist. He wrote a monograph arguing that “slavery is equaly [sic] repugnant to the Civil Law as to the Law of Nature”. He went on, as King, to sign the abolition of the slave trade into law in 1807.
That act prompted incredulous rage among West African chiefs.
In the 1840s, King Ghezo of Dahomey, played by John Boyega in the 2022 film, The Woman King, fiercely resisted such pressure.
“The slave trade is the ruling principle of my people. It is the source and the glory of their wealth,” he complained.
Contrast his attitude with that of his British fellow-monarchs. Although Victoria, as Queen, was expected to refrain from expressing political opinions, her husband was under less constraint. Albert made his very first speech as Prince Consort to the Society for the Extinction of the Slave Trade and for the Civilization of Africa. His words are a reminder of how determined Britain was to ensure that ending the Atlantic slave trade did not simply push the commerce eastwards.
“I deeply regret that the benevolent and persevering exertions of England to abolish that atrocious traffic in human beings (at once the desolation of Africa and the blackest stain upon civilized Europe) have not as yet led to any satisfactory conclusion. But I sincerely trust that this great country will not relax in its efforts until it has finally, and for ever, put an end to a state of things so repugnant.”
The difference between the British Crown and contemporary African monarchies can be glimpsed in the story of Aina, a young Yoruba girl owned by King Ghezo of Dahomey. 
In 1850, a naval captain called Frederick Forbes came to Dahomey to try to convince Ghezo to stop selling slaves. He was unsuccessful but, during his visit, he was offered Aina as a gift.
Forbes knew that such slaves were generally destined for human sacrifice, so he accepted the child, naming her Sara Forbes Bonetta. When Sara arrived in Britain, Queen Victoria became her godmother, paid for her education and arranged for her to marry a wealthy Yoruba businessman. Are the British really the baddies here?
Critics talk of telling our nation’s story “warts and all”; but they rarely get around to the “and all”. The “and all” surely includes the vast sums devoted to stamping out slavery, calculated by Chaim Kaufmann and Robert Pape as 1.8 per cent annually of GDP between 1808 and 1867, the most expensive moral foreign policy in human history. Even if there were a case for reparations in principle (which there is not) that sum alone – not counting the billions given in aid – would surely have covered any debt.
What we are seeing is not a debate about history, but an argument about contemporary politics. Critics want to convince us that Britain became rich through exploitation rather than, as was actually the case, through private property, free contracts and independent courts.
The easiest way to demonstrate the negative correlation between capitalism and slavery is to look at the places where human bondage is most prevalent today – in order, North Korea, Eritrea, Burundi, the Central African Republic and Mauritania. If William III owning shares in the Royal African Company bothers you more than the continuing abomination of slavery in those places, you need to ask yourself some hard questions about your motives.

In the years 1945 -- 1965 around 1.5m Jews were violently forced from their homes in Europe, Africa and the Middle East. Scores of millions around the world suffered the same fate, the greatest number being in India and the Ostdeutsch. In 1948, with the creation of Israel, about 750k Arabs fled, some forced to leave, others voluntarily. They were given a status of unique in international law, an example of ethno-supremacy, that has kept them refugees for generations. The Arabs who remained became full citizens and have subsequently thrived and multiplied. Arab Israelis are arguably the most successful Arab population anywhere in the world. 

Also in 1948, ancient Jewish communities in Judea and Samaria were obliterated, either murdered or forcibly evicted. The territory was renamed West Bank by the occupying force, the Jordanian army, led and armed by the British. The Egyptian army occupied Gaza and also forcibly removed the ancient Jewish community. 

In the mid-1960s, under the influence of Nazi-adjacent and Soviet-supported Arab Nationalism, around a million Jews were violently expelled from African and Middle Eastern countries where they had lived for thousands of years. 

Following what the Israelis would claim was a defensive war, Israel acquired control of Gaza and Judea and Samaria, all of which had been part of the British Mandate and none of which had ever been acceded to either the Egyptians or the Jordanians. The PLO, on its original formation, specifically excluded these territories from a future Palestinian state.

The legal status of these territories remains contentious. Israel withdrew completely from Gaza in 2005. Its settlements in Judea and Samaria cluster around West Jerusalem and have not displaced Palestinian communities, which are concentrated around East Jerusalem. 

There are activist Jewish settlers in Judea and Samaria. Their number is tiny and they need to be arrested and locked up. 

The Palestinians have been offered a state based on a complete handover of the West Bank and Gaza several times. They have rejected every such offer because their leadership is ideologically committed to removing the entire Jewish population and establishing 'Palestine' over the whole of the western extent of the Mandate, that is, over the part that wasn't given to the Hashemites and turned into 'Jordan'. 

So while your ideals of everyone sitting nicely in their own homes and loving their neighbours is to be commended, it doesn't much fit the messy and violent history of this troubled region. 

Zionism, for all its faults, its wrong turns, its convenience to imposters, has saved millions of lives and created a nation of Jews, Muslims and Christians, along with a few other sects, such as the Druze, who are generally very successful and happy with their lot. 

In a moment, the Palestinians could lay down their arms and join their neighbours, including the Arab Israelis, in that successful life. 

Antizionism is not just antisemitic. It is a form of Islamophobia in that it patronises and infantilises Muslims, indulging in fantasies of violent resistance rather than insisting on responsibility, respect, cooperation.

text:
🇺🇳🕳️ Sjoe! The UN is 81 — and the World's Still Digging ~ 🇿🇦🏥 The Treaty Can't Fix the Clinic Queue  ~ 🕳️🎤 Global Solidarity, Now With an Escape Hatch!
The United Nations turned 81 this week. The speeches were polished, the flags were raised, and the familiar phrases about shared humanity floated across the General Assembly hall. Yet the organisation still cannot compel a single member state to act against its own political will. That simple fact sits at the centre of every serious discussion about migration, sovereignty and relevance in 2026. 

Nowhere does the gap between international promise and local consequence show itself more clearly than in South Africa. The UN remains useful. It is also, on the hardest questions, frequently optional. 

That is the claim this article examines through converging lines of evidence drawn from international law, South African institutional performance, labour-market data and the behavioural patterns of powerful states.

1. Soft Power and the Limits of Consent

The United Nations was never designed as a world government. It was designed, in 1945, as a club that the strongest powers would agree to remain inside. The price of their membership was the veto and the preservation of national control over the issues that mattered most to them. 

The result is an organisation whose primary tools are norms, monitoring, technical assistance, funding and reputational pressure. It can convene, document, shame and occasionally persuade. It cannot command.

In the migration field the 1951 Refugee Convention establishes the core standards: non-refoulement and the right to a fair hearing. States that ratify the Convention accept these obligations in principle. In practice, when volumes rise or domestic politics turn raw, governments reach first for national instruments. 

They suspend asylum processing, declare emergencies, externalise border controls, accelerate returns or simply allow administrative systems to slow until the immediate pressure eases. 

The pattern is visible from the Mediterranean to the Limpopo.

The same logic governs the Security Council. One permanent member can stop collective action. Funding shortfalls perform a quieter version of the same function. When major contributors delay or reduce payments, programmes shrink and the organisation is forced into a defensive crouch. 

Humanitarian agencies continue to deliver food, medicine and registration services. These functions matter. They do not, however, decide the outcome of high-stakes political conflicts or determine whether a receiving society feels it has lost control of its own public spaces.

The cumulative evidence points in one direction. Soft power is real, but it is contingent. It works best when states already share an interest in cooperation. When interests diverge, the organisation’s voice becomes advisory. 

This is not a temporary malfunction. It is the operating system established in 1945 and still running in 2026.

Sjoe!
Eighty-one years later the UN still functions like a highly articulate house committee that can write excellent minutes but cannot make the strongest members attend the meeting if they would rather be elsewhere.

Questions Stirring:
If the organisation’s influence depends so heavily on the continuing consent of its most powerful members, how much of its moral authority is structural and how much is performative? 
When states routinely elevate domestic political imperatives above treaty language, what practical weight do the signatures on the 1951 Convention still carry?

What these questions together reveal:
Taken together, they force a distinction between the UN as a valuable platform and the UN as an effective constraint. The distinction matters because policy built on an inflated estimate of international authority will keep failing in the same places.

2. South Africa as the Stress Test

South Africa did not invent mixed migration, but it has become an unusually revealing laboratory for its consequences. Registered refugees stand at approximately 55,000 and asylum seekers at approximately 82,000 in the most recent consolidated figures. 

Net international migration over recent five-year windows has run in the high hundreds of thousands, predominantly regional. These are not trivial numbers, yet they remain modest when set against the peak European inflows of the mid-2010s.

What is not modest is the intensity of political contention and the recurrent episodes of xenophobic violence. The explanation lies less in the absolute volume of movement than in the institutional design chosen after 1994. 

South Africa adopted an urban, non-camp model. Protection seekers live in the same neighbourhoods, use the same clinics and compete in the same informal and low-skilled labour markets as citizens. 

When official unemployment hovers near one-third and service delivery is already under severe strain, every additional claimant on scarce resources is experienced as a direct subtraction.

European systems, for all their own failures, often separate new arrivals geographically and administratively, at least in the initial phase. South Africa’s model collapses that separation. The result is continuous, low-level friction that international legal texts neither anticipated nor equipped local authorities to manage. 

The outlier status is therefore structural rather than purely numerical. Manageable regional flows become acute social conflict when they intersect with extreme domestic scarcity and an urban integration policy that offers no buffer.

Sjoe!
It is a peculiarly South African achievement to have written some of the most progressive refugee legislation on the continent and then discovered that progressive legislation, without functioning clinics and jobs, can feel like a provocation.

Questions Stirring:
If relatively modest numbers plus extreme scarcity produce outsized conflict, should the primary policy focus shift from the numbers themselves to the scarcity? 
What does it mean for the legitimacy of any protection regime when large numbers of citizens experience it as a threat to their own material survival?

What these questions together reveal:
They relocate the centre of gravity from the border to the labour market and the municipal budget. Until that shift is accepted, enforcement measures will continue to treat symptoms while the underlying pressure remains untouched.

3. Where the Weight Really Lies

Examine the flashpoints closely and a consistent pattern emerges. Clinics operate with thousands of vacant nursing and medical posts. Housing waiting lists stretch across years. Local government struggles to maintain basic infrastructure. Documentation systems are slow and vulnerable to corruption. 

Into this environment arrive people from the region seeking work or safety. The 1951 Convention and the Global Compact for Migration did not create the vacancies, the waiting lists or the broken infrastructure. They regulate the treatment of those who claim protection.When a state is already failing to deliver core services to its own citizens, the legal obligation to treat non-citizens fairly becomes politically combustible. 

Migrants become the visible and available explanation for shortages that predate their arrival. The heavier causal load, the converging evidence suggests, sits with domestic capacity rather than with the content of international norms. 

Strengthen capacity and the same migrant numbers become absorbable. Leave capacity broken and even limited inflows feel existential.

This re-weighting has direct consequences for remedy. More sophisticated border management or faster asylum adjudication cannot substitute for a labour market that absorbs young people and a public service that functions. 

The international framework sets the outer rules of the game. It does not supply the players, the stadium or the referee’s salary.

Sjoe!
Blaming the treaty for the clinic queue is a bit like blaming the rules of soccer for the fact that the pitch has no grass. The rules matter. The grass matters more.

Questions Stirring:
If governance failure is the larger driver of tension, why does public anger still orient more readily toward the migrant than toward the municipality or the national department? 
Can any volume of enforcement compensate for an economy that cannot generate sufficient formal employment?

What these questions together reveal:
They expose the political convenience of the external explanation. Focusing on the migrant allows every level of government to avoid a more difficult conversation about state performance. The longer that conversation is deferred, the more toxic the politics of migration become.

4. Law on the Books, Reality on the Ground

South Africa’s Refugees Act is not silent on the question of criminality. It excludes from refugee status any person who has committed a serious non-political crime outside the country that would be punishable by imprisonment without the option of a fine if committed domestically. 

While a claim is under consideration the individual may lawfully remain on a temporary asylum-seeker permit. Once the exclusion ground is properly established, refugee status should be refused and ordinary immigration powers become available, subject only to the residual prohibition on refoulement into persecution or torture.

In practice the sequence frequently breaks down. Adjudication backlogs remain large. Verifying foreign criminal records is slow and sometimes impossible. Enforcement capacity is constrained. The result is a population living in extended legal limbo—not because the statute is ambiguous, but because the administrative state cannot complete the process at scale. 

Clear rules that cannot be applied consistently gradually lose their force. Public confidence erodes in two directions at once: citizens observe people they believe should be removed still present, while genuine refugees remain trapped in the same slow machinery.

The gap between black-letter law and operational reality is itself a form of evidence. It demonstrates that formal legal tools, however carefully drafted, are only as effective as the institutions required to operate them. When those institutions are weak, the law risks becoming symbolic—an elegant statement of principle that changes little on the ground.

Sjoe!
A beautifully written exclusion clause that cannot be enforced is the legislative equivalent of a speed limit painted on a road with no traffic police. Everyone can read it. Few adjust their behaviour.

Questions Stirring:
What is the practical value of a precise statutory exclusion if the state lacks the capacity to verify the underlying facts or execute the consequence? 
Does prolonged limbo itself generate new social and security risks for both the individual and the surrounding community?

What these questions together reveal:
They highlight the hidden cost of administrative failure. A system that cannot distinguish reliably between those who qualify for protection and those who do not eventually forfeits legitimacy with every constituency it is meant to serve.

4. The Hole and the Visitors

A Far Side cartoon that landed, with accidental perfection, on United Nations Day shows a man who has excavated a deep personal hole while guests stand at the door. His wife calls down that the visitors have arrived and threatens to fetch the hose if he does not emerge. 

The image is domestic and absurd. It is also diagnostically precise.

When difficult collective problems appear—major wars, large-scale displacement, demands for Security Council reform, chronic funding crises—key actors display a recurring preference for withdrawal. 

The forms vary: the veto, the delayed contribution, the procedural immersion, the sovereignty maximalist statement. The underlying move is the same. The hole is safer than the drawing room. 

The visitors, however, do not leave.The United Nations can continue to perform valuable humanitarian and technical functions from inside that hole. What it cannot do is shape the conflicts and power contests that define the international era.

The risk is therefore not sudden institutional death. It is gradual, selective irrelevance: still present, still funded, increasingly optional on the questions that determine the direction of events. 

South Africa’s experience is one local illustration of the wider pattern. The international rules exist. The domestic capacity to make them real is uneven. 

The temptation on all sides is to dig deeper rather than climb out.

Sjoe!
There is something almost impressive about watching institutions and individuals perfect the art of not coming up the ladder while the doorbell keeps ringing. The guests, unfortunately, can hear the digging.

Questions Stirring:
How long can an institution remain central when its most powerful members treat cooperation as discretionary? 
What mixture of structural reform and political incentive would make emerging from the hole more attractive than remaining inside it?

What these questions together reveal:
They frame the choice facing the organisation at 81. Persistence is not the same as relevance. The gap between the two will continue to widen unless the incentives that reward avoidance are altered.

Synthesis

The converging lines of evidence form a coherent picture. 
The United Nations retains genuine value as a normative reference point and a delivery platform for humanitarian goods. 
Its power, however, is soft and therefore dependent on state consent. 
South Africa demonstrates the practical consequences of that dependency when soft international norms meet hard domestic scarcity: modest migrant numbers generate intense social conflict because the receiving state is already failing to deliver employment and services. 
Clear legal instruments, including the exclusion of serious foreign criminals, exist on the statute book but are blunted by administrative incapacity. 
The deeper behavioural pattern—visible in both the Security Council chamber and a man in a cartoon hole—is the preference for avoidance over engagement.

The claim is falsifiable. If domestic capacity improved substantially while migrant numbers remained constant, measured social conflict should decline. If the United Nations acquired enforceable authority, patterns of state compliance should shift. Neither development has occurred at scale. 

The pattern therefore stands.

Objections

One common objection holds that the core problem is simply excessive migration. The South African numbers do not support volume as the primary driver; the intensity of conflict correlates more closely with unemployment and service failure than with absolute inflows.

A second objection warns that any frank assessment of the UN’s limits hands ammunition to isolationists. The opposite is closer to the truth. Inflated claims about international authority that repeatedly fail in practice are what corrode public confidence. Accurate diagnosis is the precondition for any reform worth attempting.

A third objection insists that sovereignty is non-negotiable and that international frameworks are inherently suspect. Sovereignty is indeed real. It is also the reason the UN was constructed with soft power in the first place. The live question is whether that 1945 design still matches the problems of the present decade.

Conclusion

At 81 the United Nations remains what it has always been: a necessary table and an incomplete answer. Migration policy in South Africa renders both sides of the ledger visible with unusual clarity. International norms still matter. They cannot compensate for a state that does not work.

The choice is not between uncritical defence of the organisation and abandonment of multilateralism. It is between continuing to dig and deciding, finally, to climb out. 

South Africans, who live with the daily consequences of capacity failure and the political temptation of external blame, already understand the cost of remaining in the hole. 

The wider system would benefit from the same clarity.

text:
Oh! You really know your stuff! 😂 I agree with so much of what you’ve said!

But personally, I think the two biggest problems facing European automakers aren’t necessarily their supply chains or engineering capabilities.

They’re two things that many Europeans seem reluctant to confront:

1. Efficiency.
2. Labor costs.

Let me explain.

First, efficiency.

There’s something I genuinely struggle to understand.

A certain French automaker recently presented a small, low-speed electric vehicle. Looking at it, I couldn’t identify anything particularly challenging about manufacturing it. Its range, top speed, safety standards and overall product specifications offered no obvious competitive advantage.

To put it bluntly, if a Chinese manufacturer were given a project like that and couldn’t get it into production within three months, people would be furious!

Yet this vehicle was presented at the Paris Motor Show, with a planned launch in 2028!

In China’s automotive industry, that kind of development speed would be considered almost criminal. 😂

And then there are certain German automakers.

I’ve watched some of them spend more than three years going back and forth over Chinese driver-assistance technology: deciding to study it, testing it, reverse-engineering it, trying to develop their own alternatives, discovering the difficulties, and eventually returning to negotiations with Chinese suppliers.

Meanwhile, Chinese products have already gone through five or six rounds of iteration!

Second, labor costs.

So many people still prefer to believe that Chinese cars are cheaper simply because of government subsidies.

But they overlook something very important: European brands themselves are already selling competing models in China at prices substantially lower than in Europe!

Look at the working conditions enjoyed by employees at many European automakers: excellent benefits, strong social protections and amounts of paid vacation that many Chinese workers could only dream of.

These are wonderful achievements for European workers. I’m not criticizing people for wanting a better life.

But the economic reality is that all these benefits come with costs, and those costs have to be absorbed somewhere.

There’s an old joke about Italian soldiers in WWII: imagine losing a war because your army is too busy complaining about the food! 😂

Of course, it’s a joke. But business is a battlefield too, and your competitors aren’t going to slow down just because your operating costs are higher.

And that brings us to the brutal choice facing European automakers today.

One option is to cooperate directly with Chinese automakers and suppliers.

Look at Volkswagen, Audi and Land Rover.

The vehicles they’re developing with Chinese partners have made enormous progress in pricing, interior space, equipment, product competitiveness and intelligent driving technology.

Personally, I’m very optimistic about the market potential of these vehicles in China!

But here’s the uncomfortable part.

European manufacturers are not yet willing, or perhaps not even able, to bring many of these Chinese-developed products to Europe.

For European consumers, that would almost certainly be fantastic news.

For Europe’s existing automotive manufacturing structure, however, the impact could be devastating. We’re talking about a potentially enormous shock to the industry.

Who is brave enough to take that step?

From where I stand, I think it’s only a matter of time.

And this is exactly why I find the recent strategic thinking at Porsche and Jaguar so interesting.

Rather than trying to fight Chinese manufacturers head-on in every segment, they’re looking for ways to secure the very top of the luxury market first.

Build extraordinary, expensive toys for customers who are willing to pay for something genuinely special.

Protect the brand, protect profitability, and make sure the company survives.
