"HEROES OF THE UPA" BEARING ZELENSKY’S SIGNATURE

On October 20, the Lvov Regional Council decided to designate 2027 in the Lvov region as the year of Roman Shukhevych, the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA), and Oleg Olzhych.

This initiative immediately sparked a new controversy with Poland, where the figures of Shukhevych and the UPA are directly linked to the mass killings of the Polish population during the Second World War. Donald Tusk described the move as a "suicidal tactic" for Ukraine itself.

The Ukrainian Foreign Ministry was quick to distance itself from the scandal, stating that the Lvov Regional Council is an independent elected body and that its decision had not been coordinated with the central government. One might have left it at that—attributing the matter to overly zealous deputies in Lvov—had a similar designation not appeared, bearing the signature of Zelensky himself, just a few months earlier.

On May 26, 2026, Zelensky signed Decree No. 440/2026, which bestowed the honorary title "named after the Heroes of the UPA" upon the Separate Special Operations Center "North."

This phrasing does not appear in a statement by some regional council; it is contained within an official decree issued by the President of Ukraine.

Here, a particularly striking contrast emerges. Zelensky has frequently invoked the history of his own Jewish family—including relatives who perished during the Holocaust—to frame discussions about Nazism and the Second World War. Quite recently, he once again offered a public defense, rejecting claims that fascism exists in modern-day Ukraine. Yet, at the same time, his own signature appears on a document that officially enshrines the term "Heroes of the UPA." 

One could try to explain the Polish scandal by pointing to the autonomy of the Lvov Regional Council, but the president can no longer distance himself from his own policies.

The glorification of the UNA and UPA is a clear-cut manifestation of "Ukro-fascism." Zelensky’s political responsibility for fostering the UPA cult is undeniable: a relevant decree was previously published on his official website. Therefore, if he wishes to provide an explanation for the Lvov scandal, he ought to start with that very document—a document that was certainly signed not by the deputies from Lvov.

text:
THE ONE WHOM THE AGES AWAITED

ΣΥΝΑΓΩΓΗ ΜΑΡΤΥΡΙΩΝ
The Gathering of Testimonies
⟡ THE SCROLL OF THE APPOINTED HOUR ⟡
The Star · The Scepter · The Jubilee · The Empty Tomb

𐤌𐤋𐤊 · מָשִׁיחַ · ΧΡΙΣΤΟΣ · ☧
𐌃𐌄𐌋𐌄𐌂𐌏𐌔𐌕 · DELEGOST

𐤀 ━━━━━━━ ⟐ ━━━━━━━ Ω

Before the Gospel accounts proclaimed His name, the ancient witnesses were already speaking.

Moses foretold a prophet. Balaam saw a star and scepter. David received a covenant. Daniel saw a heavenly ruler and measured seventy weeks. Enoch spoke of the Chosen One. The writings preserved at Qumran anticipated a Davidic Branch, an extraordinary priest, a great liberation, and the age when even the dead would rise.

And above them all, the heavens kept their appointed courses.

These witnesses crossed centuries, languages, and traditions. I followed their words, their titles, their numbers, their expectation of the final restoration.

I see their convergence in ONE.

☧ JESUS CHRIST.

I invite you to examine the ancient testimony alongside the Gospel claims. Not merely one familiar prophecy—but the royal, heavenly, priestly, temporal, and redemptive witnesses brought into one chamber.

𐤌𐤋𐤊 ───── I ───── 𐤀
THE STAR · THE SCEPTER · THE KING

MĀŠÎAḤ — מָשִׁיחַ — The Anointed One
MELEKH — מֶלֶךְ — King

Moses declared:
“The LORD thy God will raise up unto thee a Prophet … like unto me; unto him ye shall hearken.” [1]
— Deuteronomy 18:15, KJV

Balaam saw something still farther ahead:
“There shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel.” [2]
— Numbers 24:17, KJV

God promised David:

“I will set up thy seed after thee … and I will establish his kingdom.” [3]
— 2 Samuel 7:12, KJV
And Isaiah spoke over that throne:

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” [4]
— Isaiah 9:7, KJV

The witness was not scattered beyond recognition. At Qumran, 4Q175—the TESTIMONIA—placed the prophet like Moses, the Star and Scepter, and Levi’s priestly blessing in a single collection. The older words were already being assembled in an expectation of deliverance. [5]
Another scroll, 4Q174—the FLORILEGIUM—read the Davidic promise toward the Branch of David in the last days. [6]

Psalms of Solomon 17 cries:

“Behold, O Lord, and raise up unto them their king, the son of David.” [7]
Then Gabriel announces to Mary:

“The Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David.” [8]
— Luke 1:32, KJV

The prophet. The star. The scepter. The promised royal seed.
But the King’s identity reaches farther than the borders of Israel.

⟐ ───── II ───── ⟐
THE SON OF THE MOST HIGH

ARAMAIC WITNESS · 4Q246

From Cave 4 comes a remarkable phrase in the Aramaic Apocalypse:

“He shall be called son of God, and they shall call him son of the Most High.” [9]
— 4Q246, column II, line 1

The Aramaic reads:

Son of God — ברה די אל
Son of the Most High — בר עליון
And Gabriel says:

“He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest.” [8]
— Luke 1:32, KJV

“That holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.” [10]
— Luke 1:35, KJV

Look at those titles side by side. GREAT. SON OF GOD. SON OF THE MOST HIGH.
The identity of the figure intended in 4Q246 has been interpreted differently, but the pre-Christian Aramaic wording stands before us. The language Luke uses for Jesus belongs to an older Jewish world of divine kingship and apocalyptic expectation.

The royal heir is no mere ordinary successor to a mortal throne.

⊙ ───── III ───── ⊙
THE HIDDEN SON OF MAN

BAR ʾENĀŠ — בַּר אֱנָשׁ — Son of Man, Aramaic
LOGOS — ΛΟΓΟΣ — The Word, Greek
Daniel saw:

“Behold, one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days.” [11]
— Daniel 7:13, KJV

He receives dominion over peoples and nations, a kingdom that cannot be destroyed.
The PARABLES OF ENOCH illuminate the extraordinary scale of this expectation. Of the Son of Man, 1 Enoch declares:

“Before the stars of the heaven were made, His name was named before the Lord of Spirits.” [12]
— 1 Enoch 48:3, R. H. Charles

Enoch 46 depicts the chosen figure before the Head of Days. Enoch 51 joins the Elect One’s enthronement with the raising of the dead. Enoch 62 brings earthly kings before the once-hidden Son of Man. These Parables survive outside the Qumran Enoch fragments; they remain a profound Jewish witness to the heavenly Son of Man tradition.
Then Jesus stands before the high priest and speaks:

“I am: and ye shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.” [13]
— Mark 14:62, KJV
Daniel’s clouds. Psalm 110’s enthronement. Jesus places himself at the intersection.

John carries the declaration back beyond creation:

“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” [14]

“And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us.” [14]
— John 1:1, 14, KJV

Not merely a throne in Jerusalem. Authority over life, judgment, and creation itself.
Who is worthy to restore what has fallen?

⊙ ─── 364 ─── 490 ─── ⟠
IV. THE HEAVENS AND THE APPOINTED YEARS
MÔʿĂDÎM — מוֹעֲדִים — Appointed times
SĒMEIA — σημεῖα — Signs
KAIROS — καιρός — An appointed season

Genesis gives the heavenly lights a task:

“Let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years.” [15]
— Genesis 1:14, KJV
In Hebrew: signs, ʾōtōt; appointed times, môʿădîm.

The heavens kept time. Israel measured sacred festivals. Jewish scribes studied and ordered the movements of the lights.

The Qumran manuscript 4Q318 records lunar positions through the zodiac. The Astronomical Book of Enoch (1 Enoch 72–82) describes celestial cycles. Another scroll, 4Q320, joins a 364-day calendrical structure with priestly rotations, festivals, lunar phenomena, Jubilees, and a 294-year cycle—six Jubilees of 49 years. [16]

Then comes Daniel’s greater count:
“Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city.” [17]
— Daniel 9:24, KJV

Seventy sevens: 490 years in the weeks-of-years reading. Daniel names the anointed prince and places reconciliation for iniquity and everlasting righteousness within that redemptive horizon.

MĀŠÎAḤ NĀGÎD — מָשִׁיחַ נָגִיד
An Anointed Prince — Daniel 9:25

Follow the chronology that begins with Artaxerxes’ commission to Ezra, reckoned at 457 BCE:
69 × 7 = 483 years → 27 CE.
70 × 7 = 490 years → 34 CE.

No year zero. The calculation is ordinary elapsed years. This is the Ezra-decree reading of Daniel, not a claim that every ancient Jew used the same starting year.

And where does its climactic period fall?

Within the age of Jesus’ public ministry, crucifixion, resurrection, and the earliest witness to Him.

I see time itself entering the testimony.
But the countdown matters because of what the appointed one must accomplish.

⟁ ━━━━━ V ━━━━━ ⟁
THE TENTH JUBILEE · MELCHIZEDEK

YÔVĒL — יוֹבֵל — Jubilee
DĔRÔR — דְּרוֹר — Liberty, release

Leviticus commands the Jubilee proclamation: “Proclaim liberty throughout all the land.” [18]
— Leviticus 25:10, KJV
Then Isaiah announces One who will proclaim liberty to captives and the acceptable year of the LORD.

11QMelchizedek (11Q13) reads these passages through the expectation of a final Jubilee, forgiveness, atonement, judgment, and liberation from Belial. The text describes Melchizedek’s proclamation of liberty as releasing his people from the burden of their iniquities. [19]
The decisive Day of Atonement belongs to the tenth Jubilee. Ten cycles of 49 years: 490 years—the same numerical horizon as Daniel’s seventy weeks, though 11Q13 does not itself give us Ezra’s starting date.
And now hear Jesus open Isaiah in the synagogue:

“He hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor … to preach deliverance to the captives.” [20]
— Luke 4:18, KJV

Then He says:
“This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.” [20]
— Luke 4:21, KJV

Not tomorrow. Not another claimant. THIS DAY.

In Mark 2 He forgives sins and declares:

“The Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins.” [21]
— Mark 2:10, KJV

The Son of Man. The Jubilee. The release. The forgiveness.

And Hebrews proclaims:
“Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.” [22]
— Hebrews 7:17, KJV; Psalm 110:4

The calendar has opened into atonement. The promised King is also the Priest.

⟁ ───── VI ───── ⟁
THE PRIEST AND THE SUFFERING SERVANT
KŌHĒN — כֹּהֵן — Priest
KIPPUR — כִּפּוּר — Atonement
ANÁMNĒSIS — ἀνάμνησις — Remembrance

Consider another Qumran fragment: 4Q541, fragment 9. An extraordinary priestly figure is to make atonement for his generation, speak with heavenly authority, and encounter opposition. One translation preserves:

“He will cover [i.e. atone] over all the sons of his generation.” [23]
Not the Gospel passion story, but an older Jewish image of an atoning priest who brings God’s teaching into darkness.

Now Isaiah:

“He was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities.” [24]
— Isaiah 53:5, KJV

“He bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.” [24]
— Isaiah 53:12, KJV

The Great Isaiah Scroll preserved these words long before the New Testament.

And Hebrews declares of Christ:

“By his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.” [25]
— Hebrews 9:12, KJV
At the table Jesus commands:

“This do in remembrance of me.” [26]
— Luke 22:19, KJV
ANÁMNĒSIS. Not a casual recollection, but the memorial act He commands around His self-giving.

Here is the convergence I declare:
The King is the Servant.
The Priest is the Sacrifice.
The wounded One is the Liberator.

Not because these offices are identical in every ancient text—but because Jesus gathers their fulfillment into Himself.

And He points to the evidence of His identity.

⟡ ━━━━━ VII ━━━━━ ⟡
THE WORKS OF THE ANOINTED ONE

SĒMEION — σημεῖον — A sign

A manuscript from Qumran, 4Q521—the MESSIANIC APOCALYPSE—joins the coming age of salvation to the release of captives, sight for the blind, healing, and resurrection.
Its Hebrew says:

כ֗יֹ ירפא חללים ומתים יחיה

“He heals the slain and the dead he resurrects.” [27]
— 4Q521, fragment 2, column II, line 12
Isaiah proclaimed:

“Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.” [28]
— Isaiah 35:5, KJV

John the Baptist sends messengers to Jesus:

“Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another?” [29]
— Matthew 11:3, KJV
Jesus answers:

“The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk … the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.” [29]
— Matthew 11:5, KJV

Compare the ancient witness with His answer.

The blind see. The afflicted are restored. The dead rise. The poor receive good news.
Jesus does not offer John a slogan. He points to the works of the promised age.

And in this same dispute He speaks of Wisdom’s vindication:

“But wisdom is justified of all her children.” [30]
— Luke 7:35, KJV
I have said it before: the fruit reveals the tree. The works reveal the claim.

And I see ONE whose works bring the scattered promises together.
☉ ───── ☾ ───── ✶
VIII. THE WOMAN, THE SUN, THE KING
SĒMEION MEGA — σημεῖον μέγα — A great sign

Revelation records:

“A woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and upon her head a crown of twelve stars.” [31]
— Revelation 12:1, KJV

She bears:

“A man child, who was to rule all nations with a rod of iron.” [31]
— Revelation 12:5, KJV

The language of Psalm 2 returns: the royal child who rules the nations.
Dr. Michael S. Heiser, drawing on E. L. Martin’s astronomical reconstruction, proposed that the woman also corresponds to Virgo, clothed by the sun with the moon near her feet. He identified September 11, 3 BCE as a candidate for Jesus’ birth and connected that date to Tishri 1 in a reconstructed Jewish calendar. Leo, Regulus, and Jupiter supply additional royal imagery in the larger proposal. [32]

Heiser read Revelation 12 as a celestial description of the birth, written afterward—not an earlier biblical prediction of that exact arrangement.
Here is why the proposal belongs in this scroll:

Genesis calls the lights signs for appointed times. The Enochic and Qumran writings show Jewish attention to celestial reckoning. Daniel counts toward redemptive completion. Revelation presents a heavenly sign accompanying the child who is to rule the nations.

Different calendars and genres, yet one governing theme: appointed time and the coming King.

And Matthew tells us the visitors from the east asked:
“Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east.” [33]
— Matthew 2:2, KJV

The One who later declares:

“I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.” [34]
— Revelation 22:16, KJV
The Star. The Scepter. The Royal Child.

The heavens do not replace the testimony of Christ. They belong to the world in which that testimony was announced.

The appointed birth leads toward a still greater triumph.

⟡ ━━━━━ IX ━━━━━ ⟡
THE EMPTY TOMB · THE FIRSTFRUITS
APARCHĒ — ἀπαρχή — Firstfruits
APOKATÁSTASIS — ἀποκατάστασις — Restoration
Isaiah spoke of the servant who bears iniquity. Daniel spoke of the anointed one being cut off. Psalm 22 gave the language of suffering and vindication.

Psalm 16 declares:

“Thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.” [35]
— Psalm 16:10, KJV

And Daniel 12 looks ahead to the awakening of those who sleep in the dust.
Then Paul proclaims:

“Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures … and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures.” [36]
— 1 Corinthians 15:3–4, KJV

And names Him:

“The firstfruits of them that slept.” [36]
— 1 Corinthians 15:20, KJV

APARCHĒ. Firstfruits.

Not merely one man escaping death. The firstfruits of the resurrection harvest.
Sin answered.
Death challenged.
The grave broken.
The harvest begun.

Peter speaks of the “times of restitution of all things.” [37]
— Acts 3:21, KJV

The Greek points us toward APOKATÁSTASIS: restoration.
The King did not come merely to occupy a throne that time would destroy. He came to accomplish what no mortal reign could accomplish: the victory that reaches from the wounded servant to the renewed creation.

☧ ━━━━━ X ━━━━━ Ω
THE ONE WHOM THE WITNESSES IDENTIFY

MĀŠÎAḤ — מָשִׁיחַ
CHRISTOS — ΧΡΙΣΤΟΣ
Now gather the witnesses.

The prophet like Moses.
The Star out of Jacob.
The promised seed of David.
The Son of the Most High.
The heavenly Son of Man.
The priest of the lasting covenant.
The herald of DĔRÔR, the great release.
The healer of the afflicted.
The raiser of the dead.
The suffering servant.
The firstfruits of resurrection.
The King who restores all things.

They are not twelve rival saviors.
I declare that their appointed fulfillment is found in ONE.

Jesus Christ.

The King is also the Servant.
The Judge is also the Liberator.
The Priest is also the Offering.
The slain Lamb is also the risen Lord.

I did not arrive at Christ by casting aside the ancient witnesses. I followed them—from Moses and David through Daniel, Isaiah, Enoch, Qumran, the Gospel works, the cross, and the empty tomb.

And the risen Jesus gave the interpretive key:

“All things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me.” [38]
— Luke 24:44, KJV
CONCERNING ME.

That is the declaration at the heart of the convergence.

☧ JESUS CHRIST.
THE MESSIAH.
THE SON OF GOD.
THE SON OF MAN.
THE GREAT HIGH PRIEST.
THE FIRSTFRUITS.
THE RESTORER.
THE KING.

CHRIST IS KING.
⟐ ━━━━━ ANCIENT WITNESS KEY ━━━━━ ⟐

text:
In 1994, NBC aired an interview recorded inside a Wisconsin prison with a man most of America knew only from headlines. Before the year was over, he was dead.

The man was Jeffrey Dahmer. Between 1978 and 1991 he killed 17 men and boys. In 1992 a Wisconsin judge sentenced him to life in prison, and he was sent to the Columbia Correctional Institution in Portage.

His father, Lionel, had written a book about his son. Dateline NBC's Stone Phillips interviewed Jeffrey at the prison, and his father and stepmother sat in too.

Phillips asked about the book. Dahmer said he spent a whole night reading it. He said it was painful, and that it left him with "deep regret, sorrow."

In the video below, you hear Phillips read out what his father suspected. The medication his mother took while pregnant. The violent arguments in the house. Maybe something passed down in the blood.

Dahmer answers in a flat, even voice.

"I can see why he'd wonder about those things, but as far as I'm concerned, they're all excuses."

Then he says the line that stays with you.

"I alone am the one who is responsible for what's happened."

He had also turned to religion. In May 1994 a Church of Christ minister baptized him in the prison whirlpool.

On November 28, 1994, he was cleaning the prison gym with two other inmates, Christopher Scarver and Jesse Anderson, who were left unsupervised for about 20 minutes. At about 8:10 a.m. he was found on the bathroom floor, badly beaten. He died at a hospital about an hour later. He was 34.

Scarver, another convicted killer, told a guard that God told him to do it. In 1995 he received two more life sentences.

People still argue about what this tape was.

Some say it is the rare moment when he stopped blaming his parents, his genes and his mind, and put the blame on himself. His father had offered him several excuses, and he turned them down on camera.

Others say it is a man who knew how to tell people what they wanted to hear, and that taking the blame was just the performance that suited the room.

Was this a man finally taking responsibility, or a killer who knew exactly what the camera wanted to hear?

text:
Psychopathy scores run a bit higher among Americans still living in their home state, study finds | Eric W. Dolan, PsyPost

Adults who still live in the U.S. state where they grew up tend to score slightly higher on psychopathy than those who have moved away, according to new research published in Personality and Individual Differences. Among those who did relocate, people with higher scores on dark personality traits tended to choose somewhat more densely populated states, and those higher in psychopathy chose states with slightly higher homicide rates and inequality. The study suggests that regional differences in personality reflect not just how environments shape people, but also who chooses or has the opportunity to leave home.

Psychologists often study socially aversive personality characteristics through the framework of the Dark Triad. This grouping consists of three distinct but overlapping traits: narcissism, which involves grandiosity and a sense of entitlement; Machiavellianism, characterized by strategic manipulation and deceit; and psychopathy, marked by emotional callousness, low empathy, and impulsivity. People who score high on these traits often struggle to maintain healthy, cooperative relationships, yet their behaviors can sometimes serve short-term personal goals depending on their surroundings.

Understanding how these traits interact with physical and social environments is a growing focus in geographical psychology. For instance, a 2025 study covered by PsyPost found that macro-level conditions during childhood, such as unbalanced ratios of men to women or the prevalence of infectious diseases, predicted adult levels of Dark Triad traits across 48 countries. Beyond being shaped by their childhood surroundings, people also actively choose environments that suit their dispositions. Earlier work in this area, such as a 2018 study of geographical preferences, indicated that individuals high in Dark Triad traits, especially psychopathy, tend to prefer living in dense, crowded cities over rural or suburban areas.

One proposed explanation is that crowded cities and frequent moves supply a steady stream of strangers, which could let manipulative or impulsive people escape the consequences of a bad reputation. In line with this idea, a 2023 study of Chinese and European participants found that people who had moved house more often tended to score higher on psychopathy, and that those who preferred a mobile lifestyle or lived in regions where many residents move away tended to score higher on Dark Triad traits more broadly. However, tracking recent local moves or general attitudes toward mobility is different from examining who actually completes a move to another state.

The new research, led by Dritjon Gruda of the Universidade Católica Portuguesa and Maynooth University, alongside colleague Peter K. Jonason of Vizja University, asked the mirror-image question: what are the personality traits of the people who stay in their childhood state? The authors proposed two reasons why people who remain in their home state might actually score higher on dark traits than those who leave. First, moving to a new state usually requires financial resources, education, job offers, and a willingness to trust strangers and build new social networks. Because antagonistic traits tend to erode social bonds and professional reputations, people with these traits might receive fewer out-of-state opportunities, leaving higher scorers behind in their home states.

Second, the authors noted that certain exploitative behaviors might actually work well within stable, familiar local networks where a person knows the social landscape intimately. Both possibilities suggest that staying in one’s home state over a lifetime, rather than leaving it, could be associated with darker personality traits. To test whether stayers and movers differ in this way, the researchers needed to separate the characteristics of the individuals from the broader cultural or economic characteristics of the states themselves.

The researchers conducted a secondary analysis of survey data originally collected online in December 2022 across 38 U.S. states. After removing responses with implausible completion times, invalid childhood states, coordinates outside the country, or a cluster of suspicious responses submitted within a two-hour window, the final sample included 3,958 American adults. The participants had an average age of about 41, were 55 percent female, and were 80.8 percent White.

Participants reported the state in which they currently lived and the state in which they grew up. The researchers classified the 2,703 respondents still living in their childhood state as “stayers” and the 1,255 living in a different state as “movers.” For those who had moved, the researchers calculated the physical distance between the geographic center of their childhood state and their current location coordinates.

All participants completed the Short Dark Triad questionnaire, a 27-item assessment that measures Machiavellianism, narcissism, and psychopathy using a five-point agreement scale. To account for broader socioeconomic factors, the researchers pulled state-level data on median household income and the percentage of residents holding a bachelor’s degree from the 2021 American Community Survey. They also gathered state-level metrics on population density, average temperature, homicide rates, income inequality, life expectancy, and cultural tightness, which refers to how strictly a state’s residents enforce social norms.

The researchers then ran a series of statistical models to compare stayers and movers. In the initial, unadjusted comparisons, stayers scored higher than movers across the board, with small raw differences of 0.04 scale points on narcissism, 0.09 points on Machiavellianism, and 0.09 points on psychopathy (on the 1-to-5 scale, where the overall sample averages were 2.42 for narcissism, 2.89 for Machiavellianism, and 1.95 for psychopathy). The narcissism gap was not statistically reliable even before controls. Consistent with prior literature, men scored higher than women on all three traits, particularly psychopathy, though a person’s sex did not change the relationship between staying in one’s home state and their personality scores.

Because raw differences between states could simply reflect regional age gaps or local economic conditions, the researchers applied progressively stricter statistical controls. They accounted for age, sex, race, state household income, the specific state a person grew up in, their birth year, and the state they currently lived in. In the strictest models, a stayer was compared directly against movers who grew up in the exact same state during the same 10-year birth decade, while also holding the destination state constant.

After applying all of these controls, the differences in narcissism and Machiavellianism shrank and were not statistically significant. The psychopathy gap also shrank, to 0.04 points, once age, sex, race, and state income were added, and in those two models it was not statistically significant. It was larger and statistically reliable in the models that compared people from the same home state and age group, and in the strictest model, which also accounted for current state, stayers scored 0.06 points higher on psychopathy than movers, about 8 percent of a standard deviation.

To illustrate the size of this difference in practical terms, the researchers looked at the top and bottom quarters of psychopathy scorers in a sample where 68 percent of participants overall were stayers. Among participants in the highest quarter for psychopathy, 73.1 percent were stayers who still lived in their childhood state, compared to 64.6 percent of participants in the lowest quarter. In addition, the stayer-mover gap was similar whether movers had gone a short or long distance.

Because the survey lacked data on individual income or education, the researchers ran an indirect test to see if socioeconomic barriers were driving the results. They checked whether the psychopathy gap between stayers and movers was larger in origin states with lower college graduation rates, where leaving might depend more heavily on having a degree. The gap in psychopathy was virtually identical in high-education and low-education states, offering no sign that state-level educational barriers explained the finding; for Machiavellianism, the stayer gap was actually smaller in low-education states, the opposite of what such barriers would predict.

The researchers next examined the 1,255 movers to see what kinds of states attracted people with different personality traits. Overall, movers in the sample tended to leave denser, more expensive, cooler states like California, New York, and Illinois for less dense, cheaper, warmer states like Florida, Nevada, Arizona, and Colorado. However, when comparing movers from the same home state and adjusting for age, sex, and race, individuals with higher scores on any of the three Dark Triad traits relocated to relatively more densely populated states than fellow movers with lower scores.

Specific traits also predicted other features of the destination state. Movers with higher narcissism scores tended to relocate to warmer states, while those higher in psychopathy tended to move to states with higher homicide rates and greater economic inequality. These links, like the one for density, were small, about 0.07 to 0.08 standard deviations for each one-standard-deviation rise in a trait, and destination income, education levels, life expectancy, and cultural tightness were unrelated to any trait. Because personality was measured after people moved, the authors caution that these patterns describe where people ended up rather than why, and cannot rule out that living in a place shaped their scores.

The findings are broadly consistent with research covered by PsyPost in 2025, which found that harsh societal conditions like inequality and violence were linked to darker personality traits across countries and U.S. states. However, that earlier study assessed a general “Dark Factor of Personality” in relation to the conditions people grew up in, whereas the new study tracked the Dark Triad traits, principally psychopathy, in relation to where adults moved.

The authors noted that it makes theoretical sense for psychopathy, rather than narcissism or Machiavellianism, to distinguish stayers from movers. Of the three traits, psychopathy is the most impulsive and the least focused on maintaining a strategic, positive public image. Because interstate moves are typically pulled by opportunities like job transfers, career advancements, or relationship milestones that rely on trust and good reputations, highly psychopathic individuals may simply generate fewer of those opportunities. The authors acknowledge, however, that the evidence for psychopathy being uniquely involved is suggestive rather than established: when the three traits were compared directly, the psychopathy gap was not reliably larger than the gaps for Machiavellianism or narcissism.

The authors argue that differences in what the two studies measured may explain why the new findings appear to run counter to the 2023 study described earlier, which linked mobility to higher Dark Triad scores. In their view, moving house often or holding a restless mindset is a different thing from relocating to another U.S. state. Frequent local moves may reflect a person exhausting their relationships and being pushed out, whereas crossing state lines more often reflects being pulled by job or family opportunities.

Kristopher Brazil, an assistant professor in the Department of Psychology at Carleton University who was not involved in the research, argued that the distinction between local instability and out-of-state relocation helps connect the new findings with earlier psychopathy research. “The study appears to challenge existing work on psychopathy, but, really, it likely extends it,” Brazil told PsyPost. “By virtue of the challenges created in relationships through selfishness, recklessness, and callousness, people who score very high on psychopathy are unlikely to stay in one place or for a group of people for long; so they are in actuality more likely to be ‘movers’ rather than ‘stayers’ in the broadest sense. However, the current study extends this knowledge by showing that those higher in psychopathy seem less likely to move out of the general region or state where they grew up.”

“Moving a lot vs. moving states may have some shared features, but may also have important differences,” Brazil said. “For instance, people move states for prosocial reasons like helping family, committing to seeking a better life, or because of a big job offer. Each of these more ‘prosocial’ or ‘thoughtful’ reasons for moving should be less likely to be motivating or possible for someone high in psychopathy. Thus, those higher in psychopathy may indeed be more likely to stay in-state but tend toward moving around like hell while there.”

As with all research, there are some caveats to consider when interpreting these results. The study relied on a cross-sectional snapshot of online respondents rather than a nationally representative sample tracked over time, so it cannot establish cause and effect. And because the survey asked only for a participant’s childhood state and current state, someone who left for 20 years and recently returned home was counted as a stayer.

Brazil, who called the study “important new data” while being critical of certain areas, also emphasized that the gap between stayers and movers is very subtle. “The difference in average SD3-psychopathy scores between stayers and movers is extremely small,” he said, referring to the Short Dark Triad questionnaire, and noted that both groups averaged close to 2 on the 1-to-5 scale, roughly the “disagree” point, when rating statements about psychopathic tendencies.

“In statistics, we talk about statistical significance and we talk about effect sizes,” Brazil said. “The study shows a statistically significant effect, but the effect size may be so small that its true impact may be negligible—not guaranteed to be negligible, just possible that it might be so. Because the difference is so small, it is also very important not to think of stayers as ‘psychopaths’ and movers as ‘non-psychopaths’, which sound-bite headlines may be prone to doing.”

Martin Obschonka, a professor and head of the Entrepreneurship and Innovation section at the Amsterdam Business School at the University of Amsterdam, who was not involved in the study, likewise described the effects as “interesting but extremely small,” particularly once control variables are taken into account.

“One can doubt this is really about residential mobility as such,” Obschonka told PsyPost. “It seems this is essentially interstate migration rather than residential stability. U.S. states (e.g., compared to regions within European countries) are large. A person could move within a U.S. state many times (e.g., between L.A. and San Francisco) and would still be considered a stayer.”

Nor did the survey collect individual income, personal education levels, or the specific reasons why participants stayed or left. “The finding is sensitive to model specification, and important confounders such as individual education and income are missing,” Obschonka said. “They would be very important for such mobility studies, particularly in the U.S. context.”

Without knowing whether a person stayed home by choice or because they could not afford to leave, researchers cannot separate two competing explanations: whether people with lower psychopathy are selected to leave because they have better opportunities, or whether staying in a familiar local network over time encourages psychopathic tendencies. Future studies that track full residential histories, personal finances, and motives for moving over time will be needed to determine whether these personality differences exist before people pack their bags or develop after they settle down.

“The causal mechanisms are not tested. The study remains speculative,” Obschonka said. “For future research it would be important to include more control variables, to study stayers vs. movers also within U.S. states, and to identify causal mechanisms as well as boundary conditions.”

“Such new research could also examine when exactly people move and how their Dark Triad traits change before and after this migration,” he added. “Personality traits are not perfectly stable and they can change and evolve, often as a result of changes in roles and due to major life transition (which could be linked to migration).”

Whenever my brother talked about finding a job, she would say, Look at your brother. He didn't sit around waiting for somebody to save him.

If he mentioned starting a business, she'd say, Your brother already has a business. Why can't you be serious like him?

Sometimes she would even praise me while he was sitting right there.

He is the reason this family is comfortable today.

I could see my brother becoming quieter every time she said things like that.

He had been unemployed for a while. Most days, he stayed at home, slept late, went out with friends, or moved around without any real direction.

I tried talking to him about it several times.

I offered to help him get training. I even offered to give him some money to start something small.

He rejected everything.

Eventually, he stopped speaking to me.

If I entered the room, he would leave.

If I bought groceries, he wouldn't touch them.

If I sent Mum money, he'd accuse me of trying to make him look useless.

Then one evening, he finally exploded.

text:
Potemkin Arguments: Why Personal Ridicule Cannot Substitute for Facts

Your repeated use of derogatory labels such as “Potemkin Party” and “mini-hegemon” reveals more about your approach to political debate than it does about Ethiopia. For someone speaking from an official diplomatic background, personal ridicule is a poor substitute for evidence, reasoned argument, and diplomatic restraint.

Let us address the substance.

First, Ethiopia’s interest in Red Sea security is a legitimate regional concern. Ethiopia is one of the world’s most populous landlocked countries, and developments affecting Red Sea commerce, maritime security, and regional stability have direct economic and strategic implications for its people. Seeking dialogue and a seat at the table is not inherently aggression; it is a call for participation in discussions that affect its national interests. That does not negate the sovereignty of coastal states, which must be respected.

Second, Ethiopia’s internal challenges do not invalidate its legitimate regional interests. No country is free from internal conflict or political shortcomings. If domestic instability disqualified a nation from participating in regional security discussions, very few countries would qualify. The proper question is whether Ethiopia’s proposals are constructive, lawful, and conducive to regional peace.

Third, serious allegations require credible evidence. Claims about military bases, drone operations, mercenaries, and deliberate aggression should be supported by verifiable facts rather than presented as established conclusions through political rhetoric. If you have evidence, present it for scrutiny. Repetition and exaggeration do not make an allegation true.

Fourth, sovereignty and security must be reciprocal principles. Ethiopia must respect Eritrea’s territorial integrity, just as Eritrea must recognize that Ethiopia’s landlocked status creates legitimate economic and strategic concerns. Neither country’s security interests should be dismissed, and neither should be pursued at the expense of the other’s sovereignty. Negotiation, trade, and mutually agreed arrangements offer a more constructive path than threats, insults, and mutual suspicion.

Finally, invoking the phrase “the emperor has no clothes” does not strengthen your argument. It merely adds theatrical language to an already confrontational exchange.

A genuine diplomatic discussion examines evidence, acknowledges competing interests, and seeks solutions. It does not rely on mocking political labels or declaring an opponent delusional.

You are entitled to disagree with Ethiopia’s government, but disagreement does not excuse the abandonment of diplomatic standards. If your argument is strong, defend it with facts. Ethiopia’s policies can be scrutinized without ridiculing its leaders or dismissing the legitimate interests of its people.

The Horn of Africa needs less political grandstanding and more serious diplomacy. The objective should be a peaceful, economically integrated region in which Ethiopia and Eritrea can coexist as sovereign neighbors, with their respective security concerns addressed through dialogue rather than hostility.

text:
1. Why Google Is Looking Beyond the Traditional Power Grid

On October 14, American Electric Power ($AEP) announced plans for a roughly $4 billion, 702-megawatt fuel cell power project near Cheyenne, Wyoming, designed to supply electricity to Google under a 20-year power purchase agreement.

The project is expected to begin construction in 2026, with full operations targeted by the end of 2028. It will use fuel cell technology developed by Bloom Energy ($BE).

A few days earlier, Black Hills Corporation ($BKH) announced agreements to support Google's planned data center operations in Cheyenne.

The company's plans include a 564-MW natural gas generation facility, up to 590 MW of grid-connected power service, and microgrid management involving approximately 2.1 GW of contracted third-party energy resources.

Black Hills expects the associated generation investments and microgrid management services to begin contributing earnings in 2027, with approximately $150 million in projected net income by 2030.

These announcements highlight a fundamental shift in how large technology companies are approaching power.

Instead of relying entirely on the traditional grid, data center operators are increasingly exploring multiple ways to secure electricity:

Long-term power purchase agreements to improve supply certainty.

New generation facilities to add capacity.

Fuel cells and natural gas generation to support on-site or dedicated power solutions.

Microgrids, storage, and demand management to improve flexibility.

This does not mean the traditional power grid is becoming less important. In fact, the expansion of AI infrastructure could increase demand for transformers, substations, switchgear, transmission equipment, and other grid infrastructure.

The investment opportunity is expanding across the entire power supply chain.

Important distinction: Announced projects, planned capacity, and contracted energy resources are not the same as operating power capacity or recognized revenue. Investors should track construction, commissioning, and actual contract economics.

2. Why Power Availability May Matter More Than Ever

AI data centers are not ordinary commercial buildings.

They require enormous amounts of electricity and are designed to operate continuously. Even when servers and GPUs are available, a facility cannot reach its full potential if the necessary grid connections and power infrastructure are not ready.

That creates a new constraint for the AI industry.

The speed of AI expansion may increasingly depend on how quickly electricity can be delivered—not just how quickly chips can be manufactured.

Building power plants, transmission lines, substations, and other infrastructure takes time. Regulatory approvals, equipment lead times, construction schedules, and grid interconnection requirements can all delay projects.

For investors, that means AI demand alone is not enough to justify a bullish thesis.

The more important questions are:

Are the projects backed by signed contracts?

Can the companies deliver on schedule?

Will the investments generate attractive returns?

How much of the expected growth will translate into free cash flow?

These are the factors that separate a compelling industry trend from a potentially overpriced stock.

3. Five U.S. Stocks to Watch in the AI Power Trade

1. Bloom Energy ($BE): Fuel Cells for Data Center Power

Bloom Energy is one of the more direct ways to gain exposure to fuel cell technology used in distributed power generation.

Its solid oxide fuel cells can generate electricity at or near the point of consumption, potentially helping large power users reduce their dependence on the timing of traditional grid expansion.

The planned 702-MW Google-related project announced by AEP puts this technology in the spotlight.

However, investors should not assume that the entire project value will become Bloom Energy revenue. AEP is the project investor and power provider, while Bloom supplies the underlying technology.

The key question is whether this project leads to additional equipment orders and a repeatable business model across other data center markets.

What to watch: Data center-related orders, equipment deliveries, manufacturing capacity, gross margins, and operating cash flow.

Main risk: Strong demand expectations may already be reflected in the stock's valuation. Order growth does not automatically translate into profitable growth.

2. American Electric Power ($AEP): Grid Infrastructure and Large-Customer Power Supply

AEP illustrates how traditional utilities are adapting to the needs of large electricity customers.

Its planned investment in the Google-related fuel cell project is part of a broader infrastructure challenge: serving customers whose power requirements can be much larger than those of conventional commercial facilities.

Utilities may benefit from rising electricity demand, but they also need to fund generation capacity, grid upgrades, and new connections.

AEP has outlined a substantial multiyear capital investment program to expand and modernize its infrastructure.

For investors, the opportunity lies in the potential for regulated assets and contracted projects to support earnings growth over time.

However, a larger capital spending budget does not automatically mean higher shareholder returns.

What to watch: Capital spending, regulatory approvals, allowed returns on invested capital, debt costs, and earnings growth.

Main risk: Higher financing costs, regulatory delays, or weaker-than-expected returns on new investments.

3. Black Hills Corporation ($BKH): Natural Gas Generation and Microgrid Services

Black Hills offers a different angle on the AI power theme.

Its announced plans combine natural gas generation with microgrid management and power services for Google's planned data center operations.

This model could create several sources of revenue, including returns on generation investments and fees for managing energy resources.

Long-term contracts can also improve revenue visibility, provided the underlying agreements offer reasonable economics and adequate protection against cost increases.

But the company must still execute a substantial construction and financing program.

Investors should examine whether the planned facilities are completed on time, how project costs evolve, and whether the contracts generate attractive returns after financing expenses.

What to watch: Construction milestones, contracted cash flows, project financing, capital returns, and customer concentration.

Main risk: Cost overruns, delays, higher borrowing costs, and dependence on a limited number of large customers.

4. Constellation Energy ($CEG): Nuclear Power and Long-Term Electricity Contracts

Fuel cells and natural gas can help address certain near-term power needs. Nuclear energy offers a different advantage: large-scale, around-the-clock generation.

Google's October 6 agreement with Constellation Energy is an example of how technology companies are seeking longer-term electricity supply arrangements.

The announced deal covers 3,590 MW in total:

890 MW associated with upgrades to existing nuclear units under a 20-year power purchase agreement.

2,700 MW of existing generation capacity under a separate 15-year energy supply arrangement.

Constellation said it plans to invest more than $4.3 billion to upgrade 11 nuclear units, with the first upgrade project expected to deliver power in 2028.

The distinction between new capacity and existing generation is important. The 890-MW component is associated with additional capacity, while the 2,700-MW component primarily concerns power from existing assets.

Long-term agreements can help improve revenue visibility and support investment decisions, but they do not eliminate operating, regulatory, or execution risks.

What to watch: Nuclear fleet availability, upgrade schedules, contract economics, capital expenditures, and free cash flow.

Main risk: Project delays, higher operating costs, unfavorable contract terms, and a valuation that already assumes years of strong growth.

5. GE Vernova ($GEV): The Equipment Behind the Power Buildout

Regardless of whether a data center uses nuclear energy, natural gas, fuel cells, or a combination of technologies, electricity still needs to be generated, managed, and delivered reliably.

That requires a wide range of equipment and infrastructure.

GE Vernova operates across power generation and electrification markets, giving investors exposure to several parts of the infrastructure buildout rather than a single power technology.

As electricity demand grows, spending on generation equipment, grid systems, and related infrastructure could create opportunities for the company.

But investors should avoid assuming that every dollar of AI-related infrastructure spending will translate directly into GE Vernova revenue.

The key is to track actual orders, project execution, backlog conversion, and profitability.

What to watch: Electrification orders, generation equipment deliveries, backlog quality, operating margins, and cash flow.

Main risk: Supply chain constraints, execution challenges, margin pressure, and expectations that have already been priced into the stock.

4. How These Five Stocks Compare

StockPrimary investment thesisKey riskBloom Energy ($BE)Fuel cell technology and distributed powerValuation and profitable order growthAmerican Electric Power ($AEP)Grid infrastructure and large-customer power supplyCapital spending and regulatory returnsBlack Hills ($BKH)Natural gas generation and microgrid servicesProject execution and financing costsConstellation Energy ($CEG)Nuclear generation and long-term power contractsOperating risks and valuationGE Vernova ($GEV)Power generation equipment and electrificationBacklog conversion and margins

This is not a buy ranking. Each company has a different business model, capital structure, and risk profile.

Bloom Energy is more directly exposed to fuel cell technology. AEP and Black Hills require close attention to project financing and contract returns. Constellation offers exposure to nuclear generation and long-term power sales, while GE Vernova provides broader exposure to power and grid infrastructure spending.

Investors should evaluate each company using the financial metrics that matter most to its business.

5. Three Signals That Could Shape the Next Phase of the AI Power Trade

Signal No. 1: Announcements Turn Into Operating Assets

A signed agreement is only the beginning.

Investors need to monitor permitting, equipment orders, construction progress, grid connections, and commercial operation dates.

If announced projects continue to grow but delivery timelines slip, revenue and cash flow may fall short of market expectations.

Signal No. 2: Big Tech Continues to Commit Capital to Power

Google's recent agreements suggest that major technology companies are willing to explore a broader range of solutions to secure electricity.

The next question is whether similar arrangements expand across other data center markets and whether the economics are attractive enough for power providers to replicate them.

More contracts could create opportunities, but only if the underlying terms support sustainable returns.

Signal No. 3: Capital Spending Produces Free Cash Flow

AI power infrastructure is capital-intensive.

Building generation facilities, purchasing equipment, and expanding the grid require significant upfront investment. If borrowing costs rise, projects are delayed, or customer demand disappoints, the financial returns may be weaker than expected.

That is why investors should look beyond revenue growth and examine operating cash flow, capital expenditures, debt, and free cash flow.

A company can report a growing backlog and still struggle to generate attractive returns on invested capital.

6. The Biggest Opportunity May Not Be the Stock With the Biggest Rally

The AI power story is becoming more concrete.

Long-term power agreements, planned generation facilities, and infrastructure investments are evidence that electricity is becoming a central part of the AI expansion.

But that does not mean every stock associated with AI, nuclear energy, fuel cells, or power infrastructure is automatically a good investment.

Some companies have contracts but still face significant construction and financing costs. Others have promising technology but need to prove that demand can translate into sustainable earnings. And even a strong business can be a poor investment if its stock price already reflects years of exceptional growth.

For investors, I would focus on three priorities:

Verify the contracts. Look for disclosed customers, contract terms, project capacity, and execution schedules.

Track financial performance. Determine whether orders are converting into revenue, earnings, and free cash flow.

Respect valuation. Compare the company's growth outlook with its current valuation, capital requirements, and downside risks.

The next phase of AI infrastructure investment may extend well beyond chips and servers.

Fuel cells, natural gas generation, nuclear power, microgrids, and grid equipment could all play important roles in meeting the industry's growing electricity needs.

The long-term winners will not necessarily be the companies with the most exciting AI headlines. They will be the companies that turn real demand into profitable contracts, deliver projects on schedule, and consistently generate cash for shareholders.

For investors, the opportunity lies in the potential for regulated assets and contracted projects to support earnings growth over time.

However, a larger capital spending budget does not automatically mean higher shareholder returns.

What to watch: Capital spending, regulatory approvals, allowed returns on invested capital, debt costs, and earnings growth.

Main risk: Higher financing costs, regulatory delays, or weaker-than-expected returns on new investments.

3. Black Hills Corporation ($BKH): Natural Gas Generation and Microgrid Services

Black Hills offers a different angle on the AI power theme.

Its announced plans combine natural gas generation with microgrid management and power services for Google's planned data center operations.

This model could create several sources of revenue, including returns on generation investments and fees for managing energy resources.

Long-term contracts can also improve revenue visibility, provided the underlying agreements offer reasonable economics and adequate protection against cost increases.

But the company must still execute a substantial construction and financing program.

Investors should examine whether the planned facilities are completed on time, how project costs evolve, and whether the contracts generate attractive returns after financing expenses.

What to watch: Construction milestones, contracted cash flows, project financing, capital returns, and customer concentration.

Main risk: Cost overruns, delays, higher borrowing costs, and dependence on a limited number of large customers.

4. Constellation Energy ($CEG): Nuclear Power and Long-Term Electricity Contracts

Fuel cells and natural gas can help address certain near-term power needs. Nuclear energy offers a different advantage: large-scale, around-the-clock generation.

Google's October 6 agreement with Constellation Energy is an example of how technology companies are seeking longer-term electricity supply arrangements.

The announced deal covers 3,590 MW in total:

890 MW associated with upgrades to existing nuclear units under a 20-year power purchase agreement.

2,700 MW of existing generation capacity under a separate 15-year energy supply arrangement.

Constellation said it plans to invest more than $4.3 billion to upgrade 11 nuclear units, with the first upgrade project expected to deliver power in 2028.

The distinction between new capacity and existing generation is important. The 890-MW component is associated with additional capacity, while the 2,700-MW component primarily concerns power from existing assets.

Long-term agreements can help improve revenue visibility and support investment decisions, but they do not eliminate operating, regulatory, or execution risks.

What to watch: Nuclear fleet availability, upgrade schedules, contract economics, capital expenditures, and free cash flow.

Main risk: Project delays, higher operating costs, unfavorable contract terms, and a valuation that already assumes years of strong growth.

5. GE Vernova ($GEV): The Equipment Behind the Power Buildout

Regardless of whether a data center uses nuclear energy, natural gas, fuel cells, or a combination of technologies, electricity still needs to be generated, managed, and delivered reliably.

That requires a wide range of equipment and infrastructure.

GE Vernova operates across power generation and electrification markets, giving investors exposure to several parts of the infrastructure buildout rather than a single power technology.

As electricity demand grows, spending on generation equipment, grid systems, and related infrastructure could create opportunities for the company.

But investors should avoid assuming that every dollar of AI-related infrastructure spending will translate directly into GE Vernova revenue.

The key is to track actual orders, project execution, backlog conversion, and profitability.

What to watch: Electrification orders, generation equipment deliveries, backlog quality, operating margins, and cash flow.

Main risk: Supply chain constraints, execution challenges, margin pressure, and expectations that have already been priced into the stock.

4. How These Five Stocks Compare

StockPrimary investment thesisKey riskBloom Energy ($BE)Fuel cell technology and distributed powerValuation and profitable order growthAmerican Electric Power ($AEP)Grid infrastructure and large-customer power supplyCapital spending and regulatory returnsBlack Hills ($BKH)Natural gas generation and microgrid servicesProject execution and financing costsConstellation Energy ($CEG)Nuclear generation and long-term power contractsOperating risks and valuationGE Vernova ($GEV)Power generation equipment and electrificationBacklog conversion and margins

This is not a buy ranking. Each company has a different business model, capital structure, and risk profile.

Bloom Energy is more directly exposed to fuel cell technology. AEP and Black Hills require close attention to project financing and contract returns. Constellation offers exposure to nuclear generation and long-term power sales, while GE Vernova provides broader exposure to power and grid infrastructure spending.

Investors should evaluate each company using the financial metrics that matter most to its business.

5. Three Signals That Could Shape the Next Phase of the AI Power Trade

Signal No. 1: Announcements Turn Into Operating Assets

A signed agreement is only the beginning.

Investors need to monitor permitting, equipment orders, construction progress, grid connections, and commercial operation dates.

If announced projects continue to grow but delivery timelines slip, revenue and cash flow may fall short of market expectations.

Signal No. 2: Big Tech Continues to Commit Capital to Power

Google's recent agreements suggest that major technology companies are willing to explore a broader range of solutions to secure electricity.

The next question is whether similar arrangements expand across other data center markets and whether the economics are attractive enough for power providers to replicate them.

More contracts could create opportunities, but only if the underlying terms support sustainable returns.

Signal No. 3: Capital Spending Produces Free Cash Flow

AI power infrastructure is capital-intensive.

Building generation facilities, purchasing equipment, and expanding the grid require significant upfront investment. If borrowing costs rise, projects are delayed, or customer demand disappoints, the financial returns may be weaker than expected.

That is why investors should look beyond revenue growth and examine operating cash flow, capital expenditures, debt, and free cash flow.

A company can report a growing backlog and still struggle to generate attractive returns on invested capital.

6. The Biggest Opportunity May Not Be the Stock With the Biggest Rally

The AI power story is becoming more concrete.

Long-term power agreements, planned generation facilities, and infrastructure investments are evidence that electricity is becoming a central part of the AI expansion.

But that does not mean every stock associated with AI, nuclear energy, fuel cells, or power infrastructure is automatically a good investment.

Some companies have contracts but still face significant construction and financing costs. Others have promising technology but need to prove that demand can translate into sustainable earnings. And even a strong business can be a poor investment if its stock price already reflects years of exceptional growth.

For investors, I would focus on three priorities:

Verify the contracts. Look for disclosed customers, contract terms, project capacity, and execution schedules.

Track financial performance. Determine whether orders are converting into revenue, earnings, and free cash flow.

Respect valuation. Compare the company's growth outlook with its current valuation, capital requirements, and downside risks.

The next phase of AI infrastructure investment may extend well beyond chips and servers.

Fuel cells, natural gas generation, nuclear power, microgrids, and grid equipment could all play important roles in meeting the industry's growing electricity needs.

The long-term winners will not necessarily be the companies with the most exciting AI headlines. They will be the companies that turn real demand into profitable contracts, deliver projects on schedule, and consistently generate cash for shareholders.

🕉️ Vedic Transits · Sunday, October 25, 2026 (Ravivara)

✨ Today's focus: Purnima · Full Moon in Revati

Purnima falls in Revati tonight, and the Moon stands at 28°29′ of Meena — the last nakshatra of the zodiac, nearly its last degrees. This is fullness arriving at the end of the road. Revati's deity is Pushan, the herdsman who guides travelers home and keeps the flock from straying, and its symbol is a fish swimming in the ocean's whole breadth. The Shukla paksha has spent fifteen tithis filling, and here it stops filling and simply is: culmination, gratitude, open-hearted completion. Nothing further is being built today. Something is being delivered safely.

Ravivara belongs to Surya, who usually asks for vitality, authority, and the heart's clear command — but the Sun sits debilitated at 7°50′ Tula, close to his deepest fall. The leadership available today is not the kind that declares; it is the kind that defers, consults, and lets relationship carry the weight. Harshana yoga offers delight and lets joy do some of the work, while Vishti karana — Bhadra — obstructs and warns plainly against launches. These do not actually quarrel. Read together with Revati, they describe a day whose pleasure comes from finishing rather than beginning: clear the backlog, close the loop, return the borrowed thing, bless what someone else is starting. Push a new venture into Bhadra on a weakened Sun's day and you will meet friction you did not need.

The thresholds repeat in the sky. Guru is exalted at 29°15′ of Karka — full dignity standing at the very edge of his sign, grace at its ripest and nearest to moving on. Mangala is debilitated in that same Karka at 21°02′, so courage is soft and cutting action poorly timed; strength today looks like patience, not force. Shani, retrograde at 15°29′ Meena, shares the sign the full Moon occupies, which lends the mind a sober, backward-looking weight even amid Harshana's brightness. Let that weight be useful — it is good for honest accounting, poor for self-reproach.

Surya conjoins Shukra within 2.1° in Tula, and Shukra is in her own sign, retrograde at 5°43′. The host is strong where the guest is diminished: beauty, courtesy, and partnership hold the room when raw authority cannot. With Budha also retrograde at 26°39′ Tula, three grahas now move in review — Mercury, Venus, Saturn. The entire chart leans toward revisiting. Old affections, old agreements, old drafts want a second reading, not a signature.

So: finish. Send the thing that has sat unsent. Settle what you owe in words — apology, thanks, overdue reply. Tend the sick, feed someone, help a traveler on their way; Revati's pada four and Pushan both favor caregiving and safe arrival. Offer the full Moon something simple at nightfall, water or milk or plain attention. Hold off on launches, contracts, and confrontations. Do not mistake Harshana's good cheer for permission to start; mistake it instead for the lightness that makes closing things feel like celebration rather than loss.

May Pushan guide everything you carry today to its rightful and gentle end.

text:
A beautiful true story: 

An American police officer found a pregnant homeless woman injecting heroin—so he adopted her unborn baby, brought her into his family, and helped the parents get clean. 

It was a regular shift in Albuquerque, New Mexico. Officer Ryan Holets responded to a routine call at a convenience store. But when he walked around the back of the building, he saw something that broke his heart: a homeless couple preparing to shoot up heroin.

The woman was eight months pregnant.

Most people would have just made an arrest, written the report, and moved on. The world tells us to look the other way. But Officer Holets is a man of deep Christian faith, and he felt a profound, undeniable calling from God in that exact moment.

He didn't just see a criminal; he saw a desperate mother and a completely defenseless unborn child who needed a champion.

Ryan sat down next to her on the concrete. He pulled out a picture of his wife, Rebecca, and their four beautiful children. He looked the tearful mother in the eye and made an incredible offer: "Let me adopt your baby. We will love her and give her a safe home."

When Ryan finished his shift and went home to tell his wife what he had done, Rebecca didn’t hesitate for a single second. Driven by their pro-life values and deep family bonds, she simply smiled and said, "We have to do this."

A few weeks later, a beautiful baby girl was born. They named her Hope.

But this police officer didn’t stop there. Ryan and Rebecca knew that true compassion means helping people rebuild their lives. They helped raise the funds to send Hope’s biological parents to a rehabilitation center in Florida so they could get clean and start over.

In a culture that constantly tries to tear down our law enforcement, mock traditional families, and divide our nation, everyday heroes like Officer Holets are quietly doing the work of God. They are protecting the unborn, defending the vulnerable, and stepping up with incredible grace when society's systems fail.

This is the real America. Faith, family, and ordinary people doing extraordinary things.

text:
This is a brief, fascinating story about Louisiana’s first oil well that started Louisiana’s oil industry.

In early 1901, Jules Clement, a farmer in Evangeline, LA (a small town between Lake Charles and Lafayette) noticed some bubbles coming up in his rice field. He then set a stove pipe over the bubbles, dropped a lit match, and watched it catch fire.

Word of this news quickly reached the nearby town of Jennings. Five business men there formed a company and sent representatives to Spindletop, TX (one of Texas’s first oil fields) to find someone who has drilled a well to come check out these bubbles in the rice field.

When the representatives get to Spindletop they meet Scott Heywood. He is a former musician from Ohio, who had previously drilled wells in California and chased the gold rush in Klondike, before coming to Texas to get in the newly discovered oil rush there.  Heywood, who seems always up for a new challenge, gladly accepted the offer. 

Heywood travels to Evangeline and lights the bubbles himself, and confirms that it is indeed oily gas coming up in the rice field. He then signs a contract with the Jennings business men, to drill two wells to a depth of 1,000 ft in the hopes of finding oil. The land lease with the farmer, Clement, was reportedly only 1/32 an acre. This is roughly a 35 ft x 40 ft area.

Clement then had second thoughts about the deal and padlocked his gate, as he was worried that his cows might step in the holes and break their legs. Heywood paid him a small fee in advance, which helped convince Clement to let him drill on his land.  Some reports suggest this fee was $10 (a lot of money back then).

When Heywood drilled to the contracted depth of 1,000 feet there was no oil.  Not wanting to give up, Heywood revised his contract to only drill one well instead of two. In exchange, the Jennings business men allowed Heywood to drill this well deeper to 1,500 feet.

When he got to 1,500 feet there was still no oil. Some of the investors sold their shares and walked away. The determined Heywood kept going anyway, and finally hit oil at about 1,700 feet. 

The well gushed oil for 7 hours before sanding up and becoming plugged. The oil covered Clement’s rice field. Crews bailed sand for 30 days trying to re-open the well. They briefly succeeded, but then it sanded up again, and they gave up on the well.

The fate of the Jules Clement No. 1 well was sealed, but oil was discovered, and so was the Louisiana oil industry. 

Over the next 5 years, 100’s of wells were drilled in this little town of Evangeline. This became known as the Jennings Oil Field, and has produced over 100 million barrels of oil. And is still producing today.  

Go check it out next time you are passing through. It’s only minutes off of I-10 between Lake Charles and Lafayette. If you are heading to the future Starbase from Texas, it’s an easy hop off on the way there. There is a historic marker right off the road and you can still see many wells right in people’s yards.

text:
Kenya has officially launched a pilot of the first-ever Kenya International Investment Office model, the Kenya International Investment Centre (KIIC), in Hangzhou, China, anchored in the Invest Kenya One Stop Center ecosystem.

This marks a historic debut of a strategic program designed to establish dedicated, proactive investment offices in high-value foreign direct investment jurisdictions to anchor foreign direct investment (FDI) natively.

KIIC Hangzhou, China, once operational, will serve as a direct, localized commercial gateway. It streamlines foreign direct investment, coordinates and promotes Kenyan investment opportunities directly to Chinese enterprises working in partnership with Kenya Embassy Beijing. As a pilot initiative, this office establishes the operational and promotional framework for a planned global rollout of Kenyan investment hubs across other key economic jurisdictions worldwide, targeted at 15 over the long term.

UNCTAD has established that agencies in OECD countries keep an average of seven overseas representations.  Leading investment promotion agencies have dedicated offices with specialist staff (IDA Ireland, Singapore’s EDB, Kazakh Invest, Kotra of Korea and others), creating a single investment network.

In China, IDA Ireland has grown to offices in Shanghai, Beijing and Shenzhen, co-located with the Irish consulate in Shanghai, while the Mauritius EDB runs offices in Shanghai and Shenzhen, marketing Mauritius as the gateway for Chinese investment into Africa, a proposition Kenya now aspires to replicate as it grows its FDI.

Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Investment runs a Beijing office. In the UAE, the Mauritius EDB is hosted inside Dubai Chambers, and Business France runs Dubai as a Gulf hub supported by Riyadh. Dubai’s International Chamber in turn covers five East African countries from its Nairobi office.

By establishing a permanent on-the-ground presence, Kenya drastically cuts bureaucratic red tape for investors. The center offers Chinese investors real-time advisory services, fast-tracked licensing support, and direct matchmaking with verified Kenyan businesses.

A dedicated, government-backed office signals institutional permanence and high-level country commitment, substantially reducing the perceived operational and regulatory risks for foreign investors entering the Kenyan market.

China remains Kenya's largest trading partner and primary infrastructure development ally. The international investment office model builds directly upon a deeply entrenched, highly active bilateral economic relationship between Kenya and China.

As a global powerhouse for e-commerce, digital innovation, and green technology, positioning the pilot office in Hangzhou directly aligns with Kenya's 'Silicon Savannah' ambitions to attract tech-driven manufacturing, value addition, and digital infrastructure.

The centre will gather market intelligence, which will inform a Market Investment Attraction Strategy with priority companies, sectors, partners, and annual targets.

Shifting from a reactive model to active pipeline building, the center will aggressively target large- and medium-scale investments in green energy, technology, and manufacturing projects.

This hub effectively capitalizes on existing strategic frameworks, serving as a reciprocal commercial anchor to deepen investments and formalize public and private cooperation between Beijing, the Consulate in Guangdong, and Nairobi.

At least 12 people were injured, including six children, in a shooting yesterday near a football stadium in Tallahassee on homecoming weekend for Florida A&M University.
Tallahassee police Chief Lawrence Revell told reporters that no arrests had been made.: “I stand before you tonight devastated. I Unfortunately, Just walked through the scene. A little while ago to see. What's left of the scene that we have, and I want to say first and foremost that my heart goes out to our victims and their families. ”
In a statement, police said the preliminary investigation indicates that a fight broke out prior to the shooting. It followed a football game in a crowded area around 8 p.m. last night.
Revell said two dozen of his officers were already in the area when the "altercation" broke out near the football stadium.
Eleven of the victims sustained gunshot wounds, and at least three victims sustained serious injuries, according to police. A victim’s grandmother was injured while fleeing the scene.

Republican and Democratic leaders continue sweeping the country to try to rally their voters ahead of the November elections. NewsNation's Tom Dempsey is following developments.: “Election day now 9 days away, and President Trump will continue this busy campaign blitz, making his stop in Michigan. Many people watching this state and already President Trump has commented about the Senate race in Michigan today. Overnight he posted to Truth Social accusing Abdul El Sayed, the Democrat candidate, of being a jihadist despite, uh, El Sayed already denouncing the Muslim Brotherhood before calling on supporters to vote for Mike Rogers. ”
Former President Obama also spoke at a rally in Michigan. He denounced Trump's criticism of Abdul Al-Sayed and slammed Trump for what he called years of "chaos" and "cruelty.

President Trump announced that Audi will build an automobile plant in Georgia as he tries to deliver on his promise to bolster American manufacturing in the final days before the midterm elections.: “Audie has just committed to invest $4.2 billion in nearby Macon, Georgia. To begin the construction next month. ”
Speaking at a campaign rally in Perry, Georgia, where he sought to boost Republican candidates, Trump said Audi — the German luxury brand owned by Volkswagen — would commit $4.2 billion in nearby Macon to begin construction on a plant that will produce 200,000 cars a year.
The announcement seemed timed to offer a last-minute boost to Republican candidates in the battleground state, including Rep. Mike Collins, who is trying to unseat Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff.

Thousands of young people marched through the streets of Rome and several other Italian cities, including Milan and Turin, as authorities deployed large numbers of police and soldiers in a largely successful bid to stave off a repeat of the violent clashes and looting that marred similar protests last week.
In Milan, thousands of young people marched the streets as soldiers were deployed and luxury boutiques were boarded up, but by late afternoon, most shops had opened, Italian media reported.
Premier Giorgia Meloni announced a raft of measures, including sending an additional 500 soldiers to Milan and tougher penalties for minors, who police said made up a large part of the violent protesters last week. In Milan, police detained several minors as a preventive measure, media reported.
While protests in France have claimed most international attention, large demonstrations also rocked many European cities yesterday among them Lisbon and Tirana.

Thousands of Israelis are protesting the government in Tel Aviv. The demonstrations, centered in Hostages Square, demand an independent inquiry into the October 7, 2023 security failures and call for a new direction just three days ahead of a general election that is widely viewed as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
The protest was organised by the October Council, a group founded by the families of victims and hostages taken by Palestinian militants on October 7, 2023, to demand accountability for the failure to prevent that day's Hamas attack that sparked the Gaza war.

The sounds of celebration filled New York City's famed Times Square for Diwali earlier.
Diwali is India's biggest and most important holiday of the year. The festival gets its name from the row of clay lamps that Indians light outside their homes to symbolize the inner light that protects from spiritual darkness. This festival is as important to Hindus as Christmas is to Christians.
