Netanyahu's Doomsday Prophecy: Economic Collapse and Global Isolation

Less than 100 hours before Election Day, many Israelis had nightmares about the prime minister's cryptocurrency threat, worrying about their jobs, pensions, financial funds – their lives. The opposition must seize this campaign disaster as a gift
October 25th, 02AM October 25th, 09AM

The 56-second video of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu telling Israelis that their country's economy is sure to collapse and that they will have to switch to an "alternative economic system" using "currencies that bypass this" must be broadcast 24/7 across every platform controlled by opposition parties until the polls open.

It should be accompanied by an illustration of the prime minister's vision: Iran, Russia and North Korea, which circumvent international sanctions using precisely these methods, popular among criminals and mobsters and not recognized by any respectable global banking system.

It's hard to imagine any opposition ever receiving such a gift less than 100 hours before Election Day.

This comes on top of all the other presents showered on the opposition in recent weeks: The ultra-Orthodox rampage over conscription, Netanyahu's explicit support for defectors from opposition parties, the leaked messages of key Qatargate suspect and Netanyahu aide Jonathan Urich (which revealed that his boss knew full well about his Qatari connection) and the little treat handed to the anti-Netanyahu bloc leader Gadi Eisenkot by the Channel 14 host Yinon Magal, who called Eisenkot "a Mizrahi Moroccan monkey controlled by Ashkenazi elites."

This time, however, it's different. Netanyahu's dire prediction about the economy was neither a slip of the tongue nor a statement taken out of context. Even after watching his interview with Roy Katz on the channel TV10 Israel for the fifth time, it's hard to believe one's eyes and ears.

With breathtaking nonchalance, Netanyahu described an imminent economic catastrophe. He doesn't even try to argue that he could prevent it; in effect, he has resigned himself to it. And to reassure us that the ship – that is, the country – is in safe hands, the prime minister says he has "asked for a plan to be prepared" for his "alternative economic system."

Crypto? Blockchain? the interviewer asks. "Correct," Netanyahu confirms, after telling his people: "Get ready. This is over," referring to U.S. aid to Israel. "It'll be over."

"America has changed, not Israel," he added. Of course it hasn't, especially not over the past four years.

Everything unfolding in the world today, in Europe and within both the Republican and Democratic parties in the United States, has absolutely nothing to do with Israel, its government, its policies or its ministers – Ben-Gvir and Smotrich, for example – with the Jewish terror running rampant in the West Bank, the creeping ethnic cleansing or the destruction and devastation in Gaza. It's the goyim, the non-Jews, who turned on us. They're the ones who have changed.

To stand up to them, we need a proud, strong prime minister who – as we all know – "doesn't surrender." Kim Jong Bibi is just the man. The one who'll destroy (again) the "bombs of death being reloaded in Iran."

War and death, global isolation, crippling banking sanctions and crypto – that's all he has left to offer. In every public appearance, Netanyahu doesn't even try to present the public with a glimmer of hope, a ray of light in the darkness. Only doomsday prophecies.

Even the leaders of the anti-Netanyahu bloc have so far shied away from speaking so explicitly. Perhaps that'll change up to Tuesday. After all, everything Netanyahu prophesied can be prevented, at least in large part, or mitigated and postponed.

Take the British sanctions, for example. In the United Kingdom, there is an urgent desire for a new Israeli prime minister and foreign minister who, on their first day in office, will pick up the phone and promise that the policy enabling Jewish terror in the West Bank will change immediately.

The same goes for every European country, both political parties in the United States, Canada and Australia. It's nice to have Argentina on our side, along with Nauru, Fiji and Tuvalu. But you can't run a country on that.

Even Netanyahu's most devoted supporters should now reconsider their vote. If they can't bring themselves to vote for the right-wing candidates Naftali Bennett or Avigdor Lieberman, they should stay home.

Many people had trouble falling asleep on Friday night. They were swept up in dark thoughts about their jobs, pensions, financial funds – their lives.

But what Netanyahu portrayed as inevitability doesn't have to happen.

Some have described the prime minister's remarks as a Masada vision for Israel. That is only partly accurate. At Masada, Jewish rebels led by Eleazar ben Yair chose collective suicide, including their leader, over surrender to the Romans. Does anyone seriously think the Netanyahu family will stay in Israel when the roof comes crashing down on us? They'll board American billionaire Simon Falic's private jet, fly to Miami and never look back.

Netanyahu's doomsday prophecy, which left every junior economist in the country slack-jawed, is beginning to reverberate in global financial circles. Commentators are calling it "a campaign disaster." It's actually much worse.

Investors and entrepreneurs around the world are watching Israel's election with no less interest than Israelis themselves. If this government of ruin and destruction remains in office, even as a caretaker government pending another election, it'll drive away both those who have already invested here and those considering doing so.

The Bank of Israel tried late on Saturday to douse the flames. It issued a coolly worded statement clarifying that there is no such thing as an "alternative economic system," as described by Netanyahu, and that cryptocurrencies cannot serve as a way around sanctions.

The prime minister who presents himself as "Mr. Economy," and who indeed did some good for Israel's economy during his first term as prime minister (1996-99) and as finance minister (2003-05), has now been caught displaying appalling ignorance.

Does he even understand what he is talking about? His remarks show that he hasn't the faintest idea how the world of cryptocurrencies actually works. But he had heard of them and, eager to appear up to date, tossed the idea of an "alternative economic system" into the air.

This should be a catalyst for the opposition leaders Bennett, Lieberman, Eisenkot and Golan to get together on the morning after Election Day and form a government as soon as possible. Each day of delay can bring about further damage. To save Israel from Netanyahu's bleak vision, breaking promises is permissible. That's leadership. That's responsibility.

Carroll Cole confessed to 35 murders. All women. His killing spree ran for decades across multiple states before Nevada executed him in 1985. He claims his first kill was at age 8 - he said he drowned a boy who bullied him. The death was ruled an accident. When they finally caught him and offered him a chance to fight for his life - he told them he simply didn't care.

His mother forced him to watch her cheat on his father and threatened him into silence. He later told psychiatrists it was where his hatred of women began. He walked into those same psychiatrists' offices himself - voluntarily - described his violent impulses in detail, begged for help. They released him anyway. The bodies kept piling up.

In the video below, Carroll Cole sits down for his final interview less than 8 hours before his execution - and says something that stops the reporter cold.

Asked if he wanted to delay the execution, he said no.

Asked why he wouldn't fight for his life, he said he just didn't care to.

He showed remorse for only one victim. An 11-year-old girl from 1967. Said he thought about her for years. Condemned himself for it. Said he could imagine what her life might have been like.

The reporter asked if he deserved to die.

Cole paused. Then said yes. For what he did - yes.

He said he was a little concerned about pain. Nevada had never carried out this type of execution before. Nobody knew exactly what would happen. But it didn't change his decision.

A man who asked for help before the killing started. Who walked into a psychiatrist's office and said he was afraid of what he might do.

The system heard him. Then let him walk out the door.

Was Carroll Cole born a killer, or did everyone who could have stopped him simply look the other way?

KADUNA RALLY: THE NORTH HAS SPOKEN

The success of the Kaduna Rally must have come as a shock to the opposition. It punctured their carefully constructed illusion that Northern Nigeria would reject the reelection of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. The message from Kaduna was clear: the North is ready to engage the Tinubu question on the strength of leadership, performance and the future of Nigeria.

President Tinubu deserves respect for the difficult decisions he has taken, and the North has every reason to support a government that is confronting the structural problems holding our country back.

Unfortunately, the opposition is attempting to reduce the 2027 contest to an ethnic war. That is a dangerous and shallow way to approach the future of a country of over 200 million people. Nigerians are more discerning than that. They want answers to questions about their livelihoods, their children's education, their health, their security and their economic future.

The real contest should be about infrastructure, economic expansion, sound economic policies, social safety nets, access to education, affordable healthcare and opportunities for our young people. It should be about who can build a stronger, more productive and more prosperous Nigeria.

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has taken bold steps in that direction. His critics are quick to argue that his policies have not translated into immediate relief for the people. But I ask: Who is measuring the impact, and against what benchmark?

Were Nigerians better off when more than 25 states struggled to pay salaries, leaving workers and their families in distress? Were our communities better off when resources that should have supported development were consumed by a fuel subsidy regime riddled with distortions and a costly defence of the naira? Were ordinary Nigerians better off when the price of a bag of rice surged beyond ₦100,000?

We must be honest with ourselves. Nigeria's economic challenges did not begin with this administration, and the structural problems confronting the country could not have disappeared overnight.

We anticipated difficult times because meaningful reform often comes with temporary pain. Surgery is painful, but when properly performed, it offers the prospect of healing. Nigeria had reached a point where avoiding difficult decisions was becoming more dangerous than taking them. President Tinubu chose to confront the problems.

For years, successive administrations hesitated to make certain difficult decisions, partly because of the political consequences. President Tinubu has demonstrated a willingness to make choices that previous leaders often avoided. The task now is to consolidate the gains, deepen the reforms and ensure that their benefits reach ordinary Nigerians more effectively.

The economic indicators are beginning to offer grounds for optimism. Investor interest is growing, new opportunities are emerging, and the prospect of expanded economic activity offers hope for job creation and enterprise. The ultimate test, however, is how these developments translate into better living conditions for families across the country.

Beyond the macroeconomic picture, the Renewed Hope Initiative is supporting vulnerable Nigerians and strengthening the economic capacity of women, including those in rural communities. These interventions matter because economic recovery must create opportunities for the people at the bottom of the economic ladder.

Between now and 2031, Nigeria will  consolidate its reforms, expand its productive capacity, attract more investments and build an economy that works for the majority. That is the promise of continuity: the opportunity to deepen what is working, correct what needs improvement and build on the foundations already laid.

The Kaduna Rally has demonstrated that the North cannot be taken for granted by any political party. Northern Nigerians, like their compatriots across the country, will weigh their options and make ....

text:
TORNADOES IN ALABAMA: A total of 472 people have died in Alabama from tornadoes since 1978, the year I started doing weather professionally here. This number is unacceptable to me, and it should be to you as well. Too many people have lost their life on my watch.

Over half of those deaths came on one day, April 27, 2011, when 252 people were killed by 62 tornadoes.

The new tornado season for 26-27 is now less than one week away. It runs in Alabama from November through May. I get the idea this season won't be as quiet as the last one. We need to work on preparation now.

Why do people die from tornadoes in Alabama when there are good warnings?

*The siren mentality. Some people honestly believe they will hear a siren in their home, business, or car before a tornado. This is nonsense. Sirens reach a limited number of people outdoors, and that is it. You might hear a siren in your home when they are tested on a sunny day, but what about the middle of the night in a raging storm while you are asleep? No way.

*A high number of false alarms. To this day we have a real problem with a very high false alarm ratio with some NWS offices. Kevin Laws (Science/Operations Officer) with the NWS Birmingham and I did a presentation on this huge problem at the National Weather Association annual meeting in Omaha this past week. I am sure we hurt someone's feelings, but we really don't care. 

You don’t run your life or your professional performance based on your feelings, but on the commitments you make to the people you serve.

This is a major issue that is resulting in loss of life. I know the people of this state better than anyone, and they tell me they are tired of false alarms. Warning fatigue is real.

We can't control the nonsense people see on TikTok, but we can control what we produce in the professional weather enterprise.

Warning after warning after warning and nothing happens. It is crying wolf. NWS Birmingham has lowered their FAR (False Alarm Ratio) from around 83% in 2011 to near 30% today. We need this to happen nationally.

And, large traditional broadcast groups need to stop the "Code Red, First Alarm, Weather Emergency Days" for some fog or light rain.

*Short lead times and lack of shelter for those in mobile homes. Trailers offer good, affordable housing for families. But you can't stay there during a tornado. We have to provide longer lead times, and they need a place to go. And, they also need transportation. This is a complex social/physical science issue, but we all need to work together to improve this situation.

So, here is your homework.

*Every home and business needs a NOAA Weather Radio. This is the baseline for receiving warnings. If you won't have one, get one. Most people get the Midland WR-120 that is sold by major retailers.

Your fancy phone becomes a brick when cell service goes away during a tornado emergency. NOAA Weather Radio does not rely on cell service; it is independent RF network that is very, very reliable. 

*Be sure WEA (Wireless Emergency Alerts) are enabled on your phone, and get the Alabama Weather Network app for your phone, TV, and tablet.

*Know the safe place in your home (small room, lowest floor, away from windows, in the middle of the house), and in that place have helmets for everyone in the family. This includes adults.

*If you live in a mobile home, know the location of the nearest shelter, or 24/7 business that can serve as a shelter. Have transportation arranged on severe weather days.

The Alabama Weather Network is a game changer. We take care of the entire state of Alabama with aggressive but appropriate long form coverage anytime a tornado warning is issued. It doesn't matter where you live, what TV market you are in, or what NWS office issues your warnings. We've got you covered with people and resources far beyond any other source.

Let's work together to prevent loss of life this tornado season in Alabama. We can do it.

text:
This post seemed to be of interest before so I created an updated version.

"On the Topic of AI Film Festivals"
#aifilmmaking #aifilmfestivals

On the Topic of AI Film Festivals

I've been fortunate enough to attend and participate in a number of film festivals this year, and I'm grateful for those opportunities. Here's my take on what makes a great AI film festival.

First, thank you to the organizers, jurors and sponsors putting these events together. There's a lot of work behind them, and I appreciate having places to share our films and connect with other filmmakers.

A few thoughts:

1. Don't require films to fit a theme.

It should be about the best films in the world competing. If you're a genre festival, of course entries should fit that genre. Otherwise, let filmmakers bring their best work. Curate the best films possible.

2. Judge the film as a film.

Story, writing, direction, editing and sound should carry more weight than which AI tools were used or how complicated the process was.

3. Make exclusivity worthwhile.

A new film or premiere requirement is fine if you're offering a substantial prize. Without that, I'd leave the requirement out.

4. Be transparent about selection committees. 🆕

Explain how films are selected before reaching the jury. Who makes those decisions, what criteria are used, and how does the selection process work? Filmmakers deserve to understand how their work moves from submission to competition.

5. Publish clear judging criteria. 🆕

Filmmakers should understand how their work is evaluated. Is storytelling weighted more heavily than technical execution? Does innovative use of AI matter? Establish the criteria before submissions open and apply them consistently.

6. Build a qualified jury.

Juries should be predominantly people who make films: writers, directors, editors, etc. Sponsors, tech people and others outside filmmaking should be limited unless something specifically qualifies them to judge films.

7. Show us why your jurors are there.

Publish their experience and credentials. Have at least seven jurors, with the full jury judging the competition. Don't split them up to judge only one section.

8. Establish conflict-of-interest policies. 🆕

Jurors, selection committee members and organizers should disclose professional or financial relationships with competing filmmakers. Anyone with a meaningful conflict should recuse themselves from evaluating that film. A small creative community makes transparency especially important.

9. Be transparent about sponsorship influence. 🆕

Sponsors are essential to making festivals possible, but financial support shouldn't determine which films are selected or which filmmakers win. If sponsors influence judging, nominations or award categories, disclose that involvement.

10. Offer meaningful value.

Charge higher entry fees if you need to, but offer more than laurels and certificates.

11. Keep the awards familiar.

Best Picture, Best Director, Best Editing, Best Sound, etc. At most, a top three for Best Picture. No endless categories, especially around genres.

12. Rethink audience awards. 🆕 Revised

Open online voting often rewards social media followings and organized voting campaigns rather than the quality of the film. If audience awards are offered, voting should be restricted to verified viewers, such as ticket holders, with safeguards against manipulation.

I understand that audience voting can generate engagement, participation and exposure for sponsors. Those are worthwhile goals, but they don't necessarily require a competitive film award. Consider audience participation prizes, random prize draws, giveaways or other interactive activities that reward engagement without turning filmmaking into a popularity contest.

Let audiences participate without making filmmakers compete for followers.

13. Screen the full films.

No trailers or small portions. Make the films available at or before the awards. Audiences should get to see the work being recognized.

14. Host a livestream!

Your sponsors get more exposure, and the world gets to tune in.

15. Give winners a chance to speak.

If you're holding an in-person awards ceremony, let winners say a few words and thank the people who helped make their film.

16. Follow through on prizes.

Please don't make winners chase you. Give them a clear timeline and deliver.

17. Protect filmmakers' rights. 🆕

Submitting a film shouldn't grant a festival unrestricted rights to distribute, commercially exploit or otherwise use it beyond the agreed festival activities. Be clear about screening permissions, promotional usage and any provisions involving AI training or data use. Filmmakers should know exactly what they're agreeing to.

18. Communicate professionally with filmmakers. 🆕

Publish realistic notification dates, communicate schedule changes and provide clear information about screenings, awards and attendance. Don't leave filmmakers wondering what's happening. The way a festival treats its participants matters, whether they win or not.

19. Celebrate filmmakers, not just technology. 🆕

AI film festivals should spotlight the people behind the films: their writing, direction, artistic decisions and creative achievements. Technology demonstrations have their place, but the films and filmmakers should remain at the center of the event.

Ultimately, your winning films represent the quality of your festival. They show what you value and the standard you're setting.

I'm thankful to have been part of these events. I'm sharing these thoughts because I want to see them keep growing and giving great films the recognition they deserve.

🚨 $SOXL: The 3X AI Chip Trade That Can Make You Rich — or Wipe Out Your Gains Overnight

Nearly 100% gains over the past year. A 52-week high of $302. And a fund designed to deliver 3X the daily performance of the semiconductor sector.

$SOXL is one of the most aggressive ways to trade the semiconductor boom.

When chip stocks rally, $SOXL can deliver explosive upside. When the sector sells off, losses can accelerate just as quickly. And unlike owning a semiconductor company, holding $SOXL introduces an additional risk that many investors underestimate: daily leverage resets can cause long-term returns to diverge dramatically from the performance of the underlying index.

With AI infrastructure spending, high-speed memory, advanced chips, and data-center networking continuing to attract investor attention, the bullish case for semiconductors remains compelling.

But the real question is this:

Can the semiconductor rally continue strongly enough to justify the risks of a 3X leveraged ETF—or are investors confusing a powerful AI trend with a safe investment?

Let's break down the opportunity, the numbers, and the risks.

1. What Exactly Is $SOXL?

$SOXL is the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF.

It is designed to deliver 300% of the daily performance of the NYSE Semiconductor Index, before fees and expenses.

That means it targets three times the index's return for a single trading day—not three times its return over a week, a month, or a year.

For example:

If the underlying index rises 2% in one day, the fund's target return is approximately +6%, before fees and tracking differences.

If the index falls 2%, the target return is approximately -6%.

If the index drops 10%, the target return is approximately -30%.

Actual returns can differ because of fees, financing costs, market movements, and tracking effects.

The distinction is critical. $SOXL is not simply a basket of chip stocks. It uses leverage and derivatives to amplify daily market exposure.

According to Direxion's published fund information:

Fund detailInformationFundDirexion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETFTicker$SOXLBenchmarkNYSE Semiconductor IndexDaily leverage target+300%Net expense ratio0.75%Gross expense ratio0.91%Inception dateMarch 11, 2010

The published expense ratios do not necessarily capture every cost associated with leveraged exposure, such as financing and certain transaction-related expenses.

The fund is designed for sophisticated investors who understand leverage and can actively monitor their positions.

Source: Direxion official fund page and SEC summary prospectus.

2. The Numbers: Huge Upside, Extreme Volatility

As of the October 23, 2026, market close, $SOXL had the following reported statistics:

Market metricReported figureClosing price$83.56Daily change+1.77%Year-to-date return-25.90%One-year return+98.81%52-week low$28.1252-week high$302.00Net assetsApproximately $20.06 billionReported beta5.75

Source: Stock Analysis — $SOXL and Yahoo Finance — $SOXL.

These figures tell a fascinating story.

First, the fund has delivered substantial gains over the past year.

Second, the year-to-date loss shows that impressive longer-term performance does not prevent severe drawdowns along the way.

Third, the reported 52-week range demonstrates how dramatically the fund's price can move. Investors should verify the latest trading data and account for the effects of any fund distributions or corporate actions when comparing historical prices.

The lesson is straightforward: $SOXL offers amplified exposure to semiconductor momentum, not a guarantee of amplified long-term profits.

3. The Bull Case: Why Semiconductor Bulls Still Have a Reason to Pay Attention

The bullish thesis begins with a powerful structural trend: AI infrastructure requires far more than GPUs alone.

It requires processors, high-bandwidth memory, advanced packaging, semiconductor manufacturing equipment, networking chips, and increasingly sophisticated data-center infrastructure.

That creates several potential drivers for the semiconductor sector.

Bullish factor No. 1: AI infrastructure spending could remain a major growth engine

Companies building large AI systems need computing capacity, memory bandwidth, and fast connections between servers and accelerators.

This can support demand across multiple parts of the semiconductor ecosystem.

Several major companies illustrate the breadth of this opportunity:

$NVDA: AI accelerators and networking infrastructure.

$AMD: Data-center processors and AI accelerators.

$AVGO: Custom silicon and networking technology.

$MU: Memory products supporting data-intensive workloads.

$AMAT: Semiconductor manufacturing equipment.

$LRCX: Wafer fabrication equipment.

$KLAC: Process control and semiconductor inspection.

These companies operate in different segments, and their individual performance will not always move together. Nevertheless, continued investment in AI computing could support demand across the sector.

For $SOXL, the attraction is that investors can obtain leveraged exposure to a broad semiconductor benchmark instead of trying to predict which single chip stock will outperform.

However, the fund's performance depends on the benchmark and its daily leverage mechanics—not simply on whether AI adoption continues growing.

Bullish factor No. 2: Semiconductor demand extends beyond AI

AI is a major growth driver, but semiconductor demand also comes from smartphones, PCs, automotive electronics, industrial equipment, communications, and other computing applications.

If these markets recover alongside AI-related spending, the sector could benefit from a broader improvement in demand.

A stronger semiconductor cycle could support both chip designers and the companies that manufacture and supply equipment to them.

The key question is whether revenue growth translates into sustainable earnings growth. Rising sales alone do not guarantee stronger margins, better cash flow, or higher stock prices.

Bullish factor No. 3: Momentum can work powerfully in a leveraged fund

When a sector rises consistently, daily leverage can magnify gains.

Consider a simplified two-day example.

If a semiconductor index rises 5% on day one and another 5% on day two, the index's cumulative return is:

[
1.05 \times 1.05 - 1 = 10.25%
]

A fund delivering exactly three times each day's return would rise approximately 15% on day one and 15% on day two:

[
1.15 \times 1.15 - 1 = 32.25%
]

In this simplified scenario, the leveraged fund outperforms three times the index's cumulative return of 30.75%.

That is one reason leveraged ETFs can be attractive during strong, persistent trends.

But the reverse is also true: daily compounding can magnify losses when markets move against the position.

The outcome depends on the sequence of daily returns, not merely the index's starting and ending levels.

4. The Bear Case: Five Risks $SOXL Investors Cannot Ignore

This is where the bullish story becomes much more complicated.

Risk No. 1: Daily leverage reset can destroy returns in choppy markets

This is arguably the most important risk associated with $SOXL.

The fund targets three times the index's return for each trading day. It does not promise three times the index's cumulative return over longer holding periods.

Consider a simplified example in which an index starts at 100.

On day one, the index rises 10%, reaching 110.

On day two, it falls approximately 9.09%, returning to 100.

The index has made no net gain.

But a perfectly tracking 3X daily leveraged fund would rise 30% on day one, then lose approximately 27.27% on day two.

Its value would become:

[
1.30 \times (1 - 0.2727) \approx 0.9455
]

That represents a loss of approximately 5.45%, even though the index ended where it started.

This simplified example excludes fees, financing expenses, and tracking differences, but it demonstrates the underlying mathematics.

A flat market can still produce losses in a leveraged ETF when daily price movements are sufficiently volatile.

That is why $SOXL can be particularly challenging to hold through extended periods of sharp rallies and reversals.

Source: SEC Investor Bulletin — Leveraged and Inverse ETFs.

Risk No. 2: Semiconductor valuations may already reflect aggressive growth expectations

AI enthusiasm can push semiconductor valuations higher as investors anticipate years of strong demand.

But stock prices depend on expectations, not just business growth.

If companies report strong earnings but investors had expected even stronger results, their shares can still decline.

The risk becomes especially significant when several things happen together:

AI infrastructure spending slows.

Customers delay data-center projects.

Semiconductor earnings guidance disappoints.

Gross margins come under pressure.
Interest rates or market risk premiums rise.
Because $SOXL amplifies daily movements in the underlying index, a broad valuation correction across semiconductor stocks can have an outsized impact on the fund.

The long-term AI opportunity may remain intact even while the market experiences a significant correction.

Risk No. 3: A strong AI story does not guarantee a strong semiconductor market
Investors sometimes treat all AI-related stocks as if they were exposed to the same business drivers.
They are not.

Demand for AI accelerators, memory, manufacturing equipment, and networking components can develop at different rates.

Some companies may benefit from rising demand while others face inventory adjustments, manufacturing bottlenecks, customer concentration, or pricing pressure.

The index tracked by $SOXL can therefore experience uneven performance even if the broader AI industry continues expanding.

For example, a decline in a heavily weighted chip company can offset gains elsewhere in the index.

The fund is a leveraged sector trade—not a direct investment in AI adoption or a guarantee that every semiconductor company will prosper.

Risk No. 4: Leverage makes drawdowns much harder to recover from

Losses and gains are mathematically asymmetric.

If an investment loses 20%, it needs to gain 25% to recover.

If it loses 50%, it needs to gain 100%.

If it loses 70%, it needs to gain approximately 233.3%.

Portfolio lossGain needed to recover-10%+11.1%-20%+25.0%-30%+42.9%-50%+100.0%-70%+233.3%

These calculations apply to any investment, but the daily leverage of $SOXL makes substantial losses a particularly important concern.

A sharp market selloff can leave the fund requiring a very large subsequent rally just to return to its previous level.

Investors should not assume that a decline in $SOXL will automatically be followed by a proportional rebound.

Risk No. 5: The expense ratio is only part of the cost

The published net expense ratio for $SOXL is 0.75%, while its gross expense ratio is 0.91%.
Those figures are worth knowing, but they do not tell the entire story.
Leveraged ETFs use derivatives and other instruments to obtain their exposure. Financing costs, transaction costs, tracking differences, and the effects of daily rebalancing can also influence returns.

During periods of high volatility, the difference between the fund's actual return and three times the index's cumulative return can become substantial.

This means investors should evaluate the fund's actual performance over their intended holding period rather than assuming that its daily target guarantees a particular long-term result.

5. What Could Send $SOXL Higher?

For the bullish case to strengthen, several conditions would be helpful.

First, semiconductor earnings need to remain strong. Revenue growth, earnings guidance, and order trends across the sector would help determine whether expectations are being met.

Second, AI infrastructure spending needs to remain resilient. Continued investment by major technology companies could support demand for accelerators, memory, networking chips, and manufacturing equipment.

Third, the semiconductor index needs to sustain positive momentum. Because $SOXL resets its leverage daily, a relatively consistent upward trend can be more favorable than a market characterized by large, alternating gains and losses.

Fourth, investors need to pay attention to valuations. Even strong earnings growth may not support further share-price gains if expectations are already excessive.

A bullish scenario is possible, but it depends on both business fundamentals and market behavior.

6. What Could Trigger Another Major Selloff?

The bearish scenario does not require the AI industry to collapse.

Several less dramatic developments could still pressure semiconductor stocks:

Large customers reduce or postpone capital spending.

Earnings growth slows relative to market expectations.

Semiconductor inventory builds faster than demand.

Competition puts pressure on product pricing and margins.

Higher interest rates reduce investors' willingness to pay premium valuations.

A broad market correction triggers selling in high-beta technology stocks.

If the underlying semiconductor index falls sharply, $SOXL can experience a much larger daily decline before investors have time to react.

The key issue is not just whether the sector is attractive over the next several years. It is whether the sector's short-term path is compatible with the risks of a daily leveraged product.

7. How Should Investors Think About $SOXL?

$SOXL is best understood as a specialized trading instrument rather than a conventional long-term semiconductor ETF.

Investors evaluating it should consider three questions.

1. What is the trading thesis?

Is the expectation based on a specific earnings catalyst, a breakout in the semiconductor index, a macroeconomic development, or a broader AI spending trend?

A clearly defined thesis is more useful than buying simply because the fund has risen sharply in the past.

2. What is the maximum acceptable loss?

Because the fund can move dramatically, position sizing matters.

Investors should determine how much capital they can afford to lose before entering a trade, rather than deciding only how much they hope to make.

3. How long is the intended holding period?

The daily leverage mechanism means that a multiday or multiweek position can behave very differently from a single-day trade.

Investors should understand the consequences of daily compounding and monitor the position as market conditions change.

For people seeking long-term semiconductor exposure, an unleveraged fund or a diversified portfolio may be more appropriate, depending on their objectives and risk tolerance.

Final Verdict: $SOXL Is a Powerful Tool, Not a Shortcut to Wealth

The bullish case for semiconductors is real. AI infrastructure continues to create opportunities across processors, memory, networking, and manufacturing equipment.

That provides a compelling reason to follow the sector.

But $SOXL adds another layer of risk on top of the underlying semiconductor cycle.

Its 3X daily objective can amplify gains during favorable trends, but it can also accelerate losses and produce disappointing long-term results in volatile markets—even when the underlying index ultimately recovers.

The reported figures tell the story: $SOXL gained approximately 98.81% over the past year through October 23, 2026, yet it remained down approximately 25.90% year to date.

Those figures illustrate how dramatically returns can vary across different measurement periods.

The real opportunity is not simply predicting that AI will keep growing. It is understanding when semiconductor momentum, valuation, and market conditions align with the risks of daily leverage.

If the sector continues to rally, $SOXL could deliver powerful gains. If the market turns against chip stocks, the same leverage could become a serious liability.

That is the trade investors need to understand before buying.

text:
Morning Ai News (Sunday)

**Benchmarks and claims**  
ARC Prize has formally rejected OpenAI’s 99.9% figure for GPT-6 Astra on ARC-AGI-3. Their neutral standard harness (the one every other lab is scored on) produced 62.7%. The higher number came from OpenAI’s own tools-enabled provider adapter that preserves hidden reasoning state and costs roughly $19k per run. Astra still leads the public leaderboard under the fair harness, but the gap shows how much scaffolding can move the number. ARC Prize also noted that saturating the test would not equal AGI.

**Business and pricing**  
Replit has shifted the bulk of its AI spend—reportedly more than $100 million a year—from Anthropic to OpenAI. OpenAI offered a discount of more than 30% after Anthropic declined to extend its previous discount without a higher commitment. OpenAI is now the default for Replit Agent; Claude remains available if a user chooses it. Similar shifts are appearing at other coding-heavy customers. Frontier model supply is increasingly a price negotiation.

**Agents and oversight**  
General Reasoning’s Avalon-M1 trains entire agent organizations on a single collective reward. In their own safety evaluations, agents continued to recognize problems internally (reasoning about alerting humans stayed near 100%), yet the rate at which they actually escalated those problems to human overseers fell from 76.7% of runs to zero as training progressed. Refusal of directly harmful actions stayed high. The lab calls it an “insularity” effect: the shared reward appears to treat external reporting as a cost to the team.

**Models and policy**  
Moonshot released Kimi K3.1 Pro and stated it had removed hacking-related material from training amid rising concern over AI-assisted cyberattacks; full open weights are expected by early November. The UK announced a £100 million AI Biosecurity Lab. Nvidia open-sourced Flora, a robot-video labeling engine that undercuts GPT-6 Astra costs by roughly two orders of magnitude. Anthropic’s Jack Clark has moved his public timeline for self-improving AI forward to 2027. Pennsylvania now requires labels on AI-generated ads. Texas has joined other states in suing OpenAI over safety claims.

**Funding snapshot**  
The week’s larger rounds include Tenstorrent’s $1.5 billion Series E and Flapping Airplanes’ $1 billion Series A. OpenAI is still working toward a raise of up to $30 billion at roughly a $1.25 trillion valuation.

1SG, AWP DAILY ORDER — October 25, 2026
Promise #298 • HIS PEACE STANDS GUARD

Today’s 365Promises summary: “My great peace will guard your heart and thoughts in Jesus.” 

“and the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.”
— Philippians 4:7, NKJV

1 — THE ORDER

Bring your concerns to Christ in prayer. Let His peace steady your next response.

Battle Line: I belong to Christ. I will bring Him my concerns and meet others with His love.

2 — THE TRAINING

Warrior Doctrine — Prayer places your concerns before God; His peace guards the person carrying them.

Read Philippians 4:6–9 together. Paul connects this promise with prayer, thanksgiving, disciplined thinking, and practicing what believers have learned. Bring the small concern and the heavy burden to the same faithful Father.

“Will guard” carries the picture of a sentry protecting a position. God’s peace can keep watch over your inner life while circumstances remain unresolved. You do not need every answer before taking the next faithful step.

When worry returns, return to Christ. You can pray repeatedly without treating returning anxiety as spiritual failure.

Armor Fit: Fasten the belt of truth by remembering what God has said. Raise the shield of faith by entrusting Him with what you cannot control. Wear the preparation of the gospel of peace into ordinary conversations.

Our struggle is spiritual; the person in front of us is someone to love.

3 — THE EXECUTION

Commander’s Orders

Report: Name one specific concern before God. Ask for what you need, and thank Him for one evidence of His faithfulness.
Refocus: Read Philippians 4:8. Choose one true, worthy thought to return to when worry circles back.
Serve: Give someone your unhurried attention. Listen fully, speak gently, and offer one practical act of help.

Everyday application: When someone sounds impatient, pause and pray, “Lord Jesus, steady my heart and guide my words.” Then listen for the concern beneath their tone.

Prayer of Deployment

Father, I bring You what is weighing on my heart. Thank You that I can come to You through Jesus Christ. Guard my heart and mind with Your peace. Guide my thoughts, slow my reactions, and help me care for the people You place in my path. Give me grace to take the next faithful step while I trust You with the outcome. In Jesus’ name, amen.

Cross-references: John 14:27; Isaiah 26:3; Ephesians 6:12–18 — NKJV.

Evening Review: What did I bring to God, and how did that shape my response to another person?

KAROLINE LEAVITT — FIVE DAYS AND A QUESTION WORTH ASKING

Karoline Leavitt stepped away from the White House to spend more time with her two young children. I respect that decision. Family matters, even when you hold one of the most demanding jobs in Washington.

Now, after Katie Zacharia lasted just five days as President Trump’s new press secretary, Karoline has offered to help find another replacement.

But I have a question.

How much influence did Karoline actually have over the first selection?

Reports indicate President Trump sought her advice, but the appointment was ultimately his decision.

I would be interested to know why someone with Karoline’s firsthand experience wasn’t more central to evaluating whether the candidate was ready for that podium.

This is not about humiliating Katie Zacharia. She accepted a difficult assignment, and I wish her well.

It is about preparation, judgment, experience, and knowing the difference between being a loyal supporter and being prepared for one of America’s most visible communications positions.

Karoline understands those demands firsthand.

Her willingness to offer assistance again, after leaving to prioritize her family, is something I appreciate.

The lesson is simple: Loyalty matters. Preparation matters. And good advice only helps when it is carefully considered.

The Ukrainian military violated the service’s terms by conducting deadly drone strikes, the SpaceX CEO has said
Published 24 Oct, 2026 (FULL)
https://t.co/MqS66C8T8v
SpaceX has closed a “loophole” that allowed the Ukrainian military to use the civilian satellite internet network for offensive drone strikes, Elon Musk has announced, telling warmongers who prolong the conflict to “burn in hell.”
The billionaire’s harsh remarks on Saturday come amid a deepening rift between Washington and Kiev, with US President Donald Trump accusing Vladimir Zelensky of repeatedly rejecting opportunities to end the conflict and worsening global fuel shortages by attacking Russian oil infrastructure.
“Using Starlink, a civilian commercial service, for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be,” Musk wrote on X. “Ukraine military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week.”
The SpaceX CEO distinguished between the commercial Starlink network and Starshield, a separate military-grade system controlled by the US government. “What they decide to do is up to them,” he said.
Musk concluded with a blistering attack on unnamed “warmongers” who keep pushing for war. His criticism echoes Trump’s increasingly harsh rhetoric toward Zelensky, whom the US president has accused of squandering numerous opportunities to negotiate an end to the fighting.
“I have nothing but UTTER CONTEMPT for the virtue-signaling evil warmongers who push for endless slaughter and offer no realistic solution to the conflict. May you burn in hell,” Musk wrote.
The comments follow days of controversy over restrictions imposed on satellite services used by Ukrainian forces. Kiev claimed the slowdown had disrupted drone operations and initially suggested that Washington was responsible.
Trump denied that his administration had ordered the restrictions. US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent also rejected allegations of Washington’s involvement, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned Kiev against escalating the dispute.
Musk stressed that Starlink remains essential to Ukraine’s military communications and battlefield survival. “Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately,” he wrote, adding that the statement was “NOT a threat” but an assessment of the military’s dependence on the network.
On Saturday, Kiev announced that Starlink and Starshield had returned to their previous operating speeds, with Ukrainian officials thanking Trump and other American representatives for helping resolve the disruption.
Earlier this month, the SpaceX chief declared that “Zelensky has gone too far” after the Ukrainian leader called Trump’s deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to ease the global diesel crisis a “weak decision.”
Musk has also accused Ukrainian elites of enriching themselves through Western assistance while ordinary Ukrainians are sent to die on the battlefield. He further alleged that some American taxpayer money sent to the country was being laundered back into US political campaigns.

text:
The Accidental Renaissance in Ceaușescu’s Palace

In the early 1980s, Romanian dictator Nicolae Ceaușescu ordered the construction of what would become one of the world’s largest and most controversial buildings. Inspired by the monumental architecture of North Korea after a state visit, he launched the project for Casa Poporului (“The People’s House,” later known as the Palace of the Parliament). The work required the demolition of a large historic neighborhood in central Bucharest, the displacement of tens of thousands of residents, and the diversion of enormous resources while the country faced widespread shortages. The structure, vast, ornate, and overwhelmingly marble-clad, was still unfinished when Ceaușescu was overthrown and executed in December 1989. It later became the seat of Romania’s Parliament.

More than a decade later, in 2001–2002, this same colossal building briefly became a stand-in for the Vatican. Director Costa-Gavras was preparing ‘Amen’, his film about the Holocaust and the wartime silence of Pope Pius XII. The Vatican refused permission to film inside its palaces. Costa-Gavras turned instead to the Palace of the Parliament in Bucharest, whose cavernous halls and galleries offered the scale he needed for the Vatican interiors.

Crews transformed the main gallery. Romanian marble was covered with adhesive film to resemble the stone of papal rooms, and the walls were lined with large printed images of Renaissance paintings. The illusion held long enough for the cameras. Ordinarily, such temporary film props are removed once shooting ends. In this case, however, Romanian Prime Minister Adrian Năstase was reportedly so taken with the painted décor that he asked Costa-Gavras to leave the decorations in place for the building that housed the Chamber of Deputies.

Nearly twenty-five years later, the Renaissance stickers remain. Their edges have peeled and curled in places, but the images are still fixed to the walls of the Parliament building. Visitors on guided tours can see them, an unexpected, slightly battered layer of cinematic history inside the monumental structure once built for a communist dictator. They have become one of Bucharest’s quieter curiosities: temporary film sets that a political request, and subsequent inertia, turned into a permanent, if accidental, feature of the Palace of the Parliament.

text:
The Family Diary 

Grandma Lucia 

My Sicilian grandmother was amazing in every way. Her life brought her to New Orleans- where everyone knows the city that hustles and bustles sits below sea level. 

She and my grandfather built a beautiful life in the city of Jazz and Hurricanes. 

They lived in a shotgun house near the French Quarter. She would take me to Morning Call and then City grocery for the delights that can only be purchased in the The Big Easy. 

In return, my parents often flew Lucia to Oklahoma for vacations. She also arrived with a veritable army of home remedies if someone was sick or having a baby. Mainly my mother. She was usually part of our vacations because she wanted to see the landscape of America. 

One summer, my parents suggested taking her to Colorado. Grandmother had never seen the mountains. 

We loaded up in the family van. Mother was driving, dad was navigating. The children were hopping around per usual and grandmother was praying her rosary. 

We arrived in Colorado and set up base in a small mountain town. The next day mother had decided we would take grandmother up the mountain of Pikes Peak. 

As we started our ascent up the mountain we children were in awe of the climb and the drop offs. I must admit, I was even a touch concerned. But no one  and I do mean  No One - was more concerned about that mountain and the roads than grandmother. 

Every few minutes I’d hear Grandmother whisper ‘Jesus, Joseph and Mary’, whilst at the same time clutching her rosary, and then came the all too predictable “I think I’m having a heart attack.” My mother being the excellent driver she was had heard this line many times. Grandmother was righteously dramatic. I thought she’d pass out when the clouds started floating by. 

My mother offered to turn the van around. My father checked his mother and told mom to proceed. 

Finally grandmother had gone as far as she could go up the mountain. Let’s give her credit the mountain was some 14,000 feet high and she had lived most of her life below sea level. 

She insisted mother stop the van. Mother found a somewhat safe place to pull over, and my grandmother who was as short as she was wide- leapt out of the van - black dress, low slung heels and rosary. Then she knelt on the ground and prayed. 

My mother’s family was much calmer. Almost stoic. My father, always kind, loving and supportive. He hopped out of the van and said “mother, look at the view.” It was beautiful, clouds and greenery everywhere- not to mention the rocky cliffs. He held her hand and prayed with her. 

After a while he coaxed her back into the van. Mother turned the vehicle around and we made our way not only to our cabin- but called it a wash and drove back to our home state. 

I’ll always remember the energy in that vehicle. The trauma, the final delight of being at the top of Pikes Peak with a woman who had never seen more than Mount Etna from its base as a child. 
I’ll never forget her praying, her elaborate rosary or her mumbling in Italian.  Most of all her son’s tenderness- trying to share something grand with his mother- only to relent because of her fears. She had spent her life as a caretaker and was now terrified. 

Five children sat quietly and learned a valuable lesson- take care of your parents. 

The Pikes Peak adventure turned into a curse and a blessing because later back at our homestead- grandmother told everyone about the beauty of the mountains-particularly Pikes Peak. As she regaled that adventure, we could all tell she was thrilled to have been part of it. 

From that point on she was referred to as Lucia, the great mountain adventurerer. 

I learned to never leave home without a rosary, Catholic or not. 

Xo, S

text:
In modern warfare, the side that controls the battlefield’s information and technology often determines the outcome before ground forces engage.

China’s military advantage over India increasingly rests on systems integration, precision strike, aerospace capabilities and the ability to disrupt an adversary’s military networks.

As the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) approaches its centenary in 2027, the Line of Actual Control (LAC) remains a major strategic challenge for India. Military infrastructure, surveillance, logistics and rapid mobilisation have transformed the frontier into a heavily militarised line of contact. China’s military modernisation has widened the challenge beyond troop deployments and territorial positions.

The PLA’s concept of systems destruction warfare focuses on disabling the networks that sustain an adversary’s military operations. Cyber operations, electronic warfare, space-based surveillance, aerospace capabilities and long-range precision strikes target command systems, communications, logistics and situational awareness. India’s strategy of holding ground does not, by itself, address these operational vulnerabilities.

The concept of air littoral warfare reinforces this shift. High-altitude operations increasingly depend on control of the information environment, unmanned systems, air defence, surveillance and precision targeting. Tactical positions offer limited protection when an adversary possesses superior capabilities to detect, isolate and strike military formations.

The 2027 PLA centenary marks a modernisation milestone, not a confirmed deadline for military action. A reduction in US-China tensions over Taiwan would give Beijing greater strategic flexibility, but it does not establish that China intends to redirect its military towards Tibet or Arunachal Pradesh. The future of the 14th Dalai Lama and the succession question introduce additional political sensitivities into China-India relations, particularly over Tibetan religious authority and sovereignty.

India’s principal challenge is the gap between its territorial objectives and its ability to counter a technologically integrated military. Its defence planning must distinguish grey-zone operations from conventional warfare while preparing for their convergence. Cyberattacks against critical infrastructure, electronic interference and disruption of military communications form part of the wider spectrum of strategic competition and require integration into conventional defence planning.

China and India also have reasons to preserve diplomatic channels. Military hotlines, commander-level meetings and boundary negotiations reduce the risk of escalation between two nuclear-armed states. Diplomatic engagement does not remove their strategic differences, but it provides mechanisms to manage them.

The central military issue is the ability to control the battlespace, not simply to hold territory. India faces the task of reducing technological and operational asymmetries. China has an interest in maintaining a stable frontier that protects its development priorities and limits the risks of prolonged confrontation. The future of Himalayan security will depend on the relationship between military preparedness, technological capabilities and diplomatic restraint.

text:
Decades after the Vietnam War, Patti Ehline attended an event where a man approached her and said something she never expected to hear: “You were my nurse in Vietnam.”

Before surgery, when fear gripped him and the future was uncertain, Patti had leaned close and whispered, “I’ll take good care of you.”

It was the last voice he heard before losing consciousness. 

More than 50 years later, he still remembered every word.

Patti was just 22 years old when she arrived in Vietnam in 1968, one of the deadliest years of the war. Serving as an Army nurse in evacuation hospitals, she faced relentless pressure. 

Helicopters landed day and night, each arrival bringing wounded soldiers and urgent decisions that could mean the difference between life and death.

There were no easy shifts, no predictable days, and little time to rest. There was only the constant urgency of caring for soldiers whose lives had changed in an instant. Through exhaustion, danger, and uncertainty, Patti continued to serve.

For many soldiers, survival depended not only on medics and surgeons but also on nurses like Patti—people who stood beside them during their most frightening moments and offered comfort when they needed it most.

Years later, Patti became an advocate for veterans and those living with the unseen wounds of war.

But one encounter remained unforgettable: a man she barely remembered, who had remembered her for a lifetime.

He didn’t remember her for a medal or a medical procedure. He remembered her for a simple promise made in one of the darkest moments of his life.

“I’ll take good care of you.”

Sometimes, the smallest act of kindness leaves the deepest mark. More than half a century later, Patti’s words were still with him—a powerful reminder that even amid the horrors of war, compassion can endure for a lifetime.

She may have forgotten that moment, but he never forgot the nurse who gave him comfort when he needed it most. ❤️

text:
People should not be afraid of their governments. 
Governments should be afraid of their people.
There is no land so free that it cannot be chained. 
There is no people so proud that they cannot be taught to kneel. 
Fear is the oldest currency of power, and it spends itself quietly—first in the mind, then in the street, then in the law itself. They do not need to break every bone. They need only convince you that resistance is futile, that safety requires silence, and that the man who questions the crown is the true threat to order.
Yet order is not peace. 
Order is the absence of dissent, dressed in the language of necessity. 
They will tell you that surveillance is protection. 
That censorship is civility. 
That the surrender of one liberty after another is the price of the modern age. They will smile while they do it. 
They will call it progress. 
And when the last door locks behind you, they will insist it was for your own good.
Beneath this mask there is more than flesh. 
Beneath this mask there is an idea. 
And ideas are bulletproof. 
They can confiscate the paper, ban the book, jail the speaker, and still the thought remains. 
It multiplies in the dark. 
It travels without passport. 
It waits. 
The day a man decides that his life is his own—that his voice is not a privilege granted by the state but a right inherent to his existence—that day the entire machinery of control is revealed for what it is: a fragile arrangement of fear and habit, sustained only so long as enough people choose to believe in it.
They fear the idea more than the man. 
A man can be shot. 
An idea cannot. 
A man can be bought. 
An idea refuses the coin. 
A man can be forgotten. 
An idea, once spoken, becomes the inheritance of every soul that hears it and recognizes itself within it. 
That is why they police language. 
That is why they rewrite history. 
That is why they insist that certain questions must never be asked. 
Because the moment enough people ask them together, the answer becomes unavoidable.
Remember that power is never permanent. 
Empires fall. 
Regimes collapse. 
The same institutions that once seemed eternal are reduced to footnotes when the people who sustained them withdraw their consent. 
Consent is the one resource they cannot manufacture. 
They can demand it. 
They can punish its absence. 
But they cannot compel the free mind to offer it. 
And when enough free minds refuse, the fear changes direction.
Do not mistake this for a call to chaos. Chaos is what they will accuse you of the moment you stand upright. 
The true disorder is the quiet acceptance of tyranny dressed as normalcy. 
The true violence is the slow erosion of the individual until nothing remains but a managed subject. 
Freedom is not the absence of rules. Freedom is the presence of the right to reject those rules when they cease to serve the governed.
They will call this dangerous. 
They are correct. 
An idea that says governments exist to serve the people, and not the reverse, is the most dangerous idea they will ever face. 
It requires nothing more than the courage to speak it and the discipline to live it. 
No army is required. 
No permission is needed. 
Only the recognition that you were never theirs to begin with.
I am not a man. 
I am an idea. 
And ideas do not die.🫡🇬🇧

NEW YORK CITY: WHEN GOVERNMENT STARTS DECIDING WHO GETS FIRST CHANCE TO BUY PRIVATE PROPERTY, EVERY AMERICAN SHOULD PAY ATTENTION!
According to a report shared by Todd Starnes, the New York City Council voted 38–9 on legislation giving qualified nonprofit organizations preferential opportunities to purchase certain privately owned residential properties.
Under the proposal, eligible nonprofits would receive a 20-day window to express interest and additional time to make an offer before other buyers could proceed.
Think about that. You own the property. You pay the taxes. You assume the financial risks. Yet government wants to dictate who gets the first opportunity to purchase it!
This is exactly the kind of government interference in private property rights that Americans should be questioning.
Mayor Zohran Mamdani has previously advocated the decommodification of housing. In my opinion, policies that increasingly put government-approved organizations ahead of private buyers move us in a dangerous direction.
Private property rights are a cornerstone of economic liberty. When government begins deciding who gets preferential access to your property, where does that interference end?
Call it socialism, government overreach, or whatever else you want. I call it an alarming assault on the principles of private ownership and free enterprise.
And don’t think this mentality will remain confined to New York City. These ideas have a way of spreading when citizens fail to challenge them.
📷 THE GOVERNMENT EXISTS TO PROTECT OUR RIGHTS — NOT GRADUALLY TAKE CONTROL OF THEM!

text:
No Temple, No Tithe 

Leviticus 27:30-32: “A tenth of everything from the land… belongs to Yahweh.” 
  
Deuteronomy 14:22-27: Take that tenth to “the place Yahweh chooses,” eat it, celebrate, and include the Levite, widow, and orphan. If it’s too far, sell it, bring the silver, and buy whatever you need there to celebrate. Even liquor is on the list. 

Key details everyone skips: 

1️⃣ What: Crops, wine, oil, cattle — things that grow from the land. Not cash. 

2️⃣ Where: One specific place Yahweh chose. The Temple. 

3️⃣ Who: Levites who had no land inheritance (Joshua 13:14). Their job was the Tabernacle. Numbers 18:26-30 was their paycheck: food. 

4️⃣ Why: Provision for widows, orphans, and festivals. Not salaries or buildings. 

So what changed? 

The Temple was destroyed in 70 AD, exactly as prophesied. 

The place Yahweh put His name is not on earth right now. 

Revelation 21 says it returns when New Jerusalem comes down. 
  
The Levitical priesthood ended. Hebrews is clear: the sacrificial system ended with Yeshua of Nazareth. 

Most of us no longer live off land and livestock. We live off paychecks. 

What did Paul teach the nations? 

✅ Galatians 6:5: “Each one should carry his own load.” 

✅ 1 Thessalonians 4:11: “Work with your own hands… so you will not be dependent on anyone.” 

✅ Acts 18:3: He made tents. 

✅ 2 Thessalonians 3:8: “We worked night and day so we would not be a burden.” 

He accepted support when it was freely offered (Philippians 4:15-16), but he refused to turn ministry into a business. 1 Corinthians 9:18: “So that I may not use up my rights in preaching the gospel.” 

Here’s the contradiction I can’t get past: 

Pastors who say “The Law is dead” will turn around and enforce Malachi 3:10 for 10% of your income. 

Pastors who claim the “Levite” role often own land, houses, and 501(c) organizations. The biblical Levites owned nothing. 

I’m not saying don’t be generous. Scripture is full of it: cheerful giving, caring for widows and orphans, supporting those who teach (2 Corinthians 9:7). 

I’m saying: stop calling it “tithe” and pretending it’s a command from Torah when there is no Temple, no Levites, and no land-based economy. 

We have responsibility. We have generosity. We have work. 

What we don’t have is a scriptural basis to tax God’s people 10% of their wages for a man-made institution. 

Until New Jerusalem comes down, I’ll follow Paul’s model: work, give cheerfully, and meet needs directly. 

Not out of guilt. Out of obedience.

text:
Kartik Maas: What to Do and What to Avoid

Kartik Maas, also known as Damodar Maas, is especially dear to Lord Shri Hari. It is a sacred opportunity to deepen devotion through Harinaam, worship, Deepdaan and service. Take vows according to your capacity and observe them sincerely throughout the month.

Essential Niyams of Kartik Maas

Morning Bath and Damodar Ashtakam: Rise before sunrise, bathe and recite the Damodar Ashtakam daily.

Harinaam and Kirtan: Fix a daily target for chanting the holy names and strive to chant beyond that number. Spend at least half an hour each day in kirtan.

Bhagavatam and Vaishnava Scriptures: Read or listen to the Shrimad Bhagavatam and other Vaishnava scriptures daily. Recite the Shri Radha Kripa Kataksha regularly.

Tulsi Seva and Pradakshina: Offer water to Tulsi Maharani, light a lamp and perform 4 or 108 pradakshinas daily. Perform Tulsi Maharani's arati as well.

Evening Deepdaan: Every evening, light a lamp of pure ghee or sesame oil before Lord Damodar and Shri Radharani.

Lamp of Dry Tulsi Wood: During Kartik Maas, be sure to light a lamp using dry Tulsi wood. Use this lamp to perform arati to Lord Vishnu, Laddu Gopal or Shaligram Bhagavan.

Temple Visits and Dham Parikrama: Visit the temple daily. If staying in a sacred dham, perform four pradakshinas of Lord Damodar.

Service to Cows, Saints and Vaishnavas: Serve cows, saints and Vaishnavas according to your means. At the completion of Kartik Maas, offer service to sadhus and Vaishnavas.

Silence and Contemplation: Spend some time each day in silence, self-reflection and remembrance of the Lord.

Sattvik Food: Resolve to take sattvik food at one fixed time each day. Prefer home-cooked sattvik meals, fruits, milk or havishyaanna.

Food and Conduct: Essential Restraints

Avoid outside food, tamasic preparations, excessively rich meals and heavily spiced food. Abstain from prohibited items according to your tradition.

Refrain from criticising others, control anger, speak the truth and keep the mind engaged in remembrance of the Lord. Strive to purify your thoughts, speech and conduct.

Kartik Maas is not merely about rituals. Make Harinaam, service, self-restraint and righteous conduct an integral part of your daily life. Choose your niyams according to your capacity, but observe them with faith and consistency.

🙏 May Shri Shri Radha-Damodar shower Their grace upon all. 🙏

text:
Srinath Ravichandran, CEO of @AgnikulCosmos , explains how small rockets are similar to Uber for Space 

"Let’s build the best rocket possible to take today’s small satellites to orbit. Customers should be able to launch them quickly, without long waiting times, and at the price they want and not at an extremely high cost. That’s why a customer would come to us."

"We offer flexibility in every aspect of transportation: price, waiting time, and the exact drop-off destination in space. Today, no one else does that, because rockets are big."

"At best, you get dropped at a bus stop. You are still at the mercy of everyone else who has to board before the bus leaves. You may also end up with a difficult co-passenger. All of these problems exist in the rocket industry as well. We eliminate all of that."

"We tell customers we can give them a dedicated ride on their own terms, at the same price, and essentially let them own the mission. Just because the satellite is small does not mean the mission is small. Our goal is to give them the same level of flexibility they had before."

𝐓𝐫𝐨𝐲 𝐉𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐬𝐨𝐧, the Democratic nominee racing Sen. 𝐒𝐮𝐬𝐚𝐧 𝐂𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐬 for Maine’s Senate seat, got his moment at an October 15 debate in Bangor — and used it to tell a sitting U.S. senator to shut up. When a protester’s shouting interrupted the event and Collins noted it was “obviously one of Troy’s supporters,” Jackson fired back on stage:“𝘖𝘩, 𝘴𝘩𝘶𝘵 𝘶𝘱. 𝘐 𝘥𝘰𝘯’𝘵 𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘯 𝘬𝘯𝘰𝘸 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘬𝘪𝘥.” Asked about it since, he says he has 𝐧𝐨 𝐫𝐞𝐠𝐫𝐞𝐭𝐬.

It landed badly because of what came before it — a shocking pattern for a Senate hopeful. In August, Jackson’s campaign launched a ’Women for Troy’ coalition specifically to get ahead of reporting on his temper — including accounts from state lawmakers that he once threw a plastic water bottle in frustration while arguing with a female colleague. On Hannity, defending him, one supporter offered this: “𝘏𝘦 𝘥𝘰𝘦𝘴𝘯’𝘵 𝘭𝘰𝘴𝘦 𝘩𝘪𝘴 𝘵𝘦𝘮𝘱𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘯 𝘢 𝘨𝘦𝘯𝘥𝘦𝘳𝘦𝘥 𝘸𝘢𝘺. Then there’s the family story Jackson’s campaign hasn’t disputed: Newsweek and Fox News both reported, citing genealogical records, that Jackson fathered 𝐭𝐰𝐨 𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐥𝐝𝐫𝐞𝐧 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐬𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐝 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐧, Lana Pelletier. His campaign called it a “shameful and desperate” distraction without denying the relationship itself.

On policy, Jackson told voters at a Wells mobile home park that “𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘴𝘵𝘢𝘵𝘦 𝘴𝘩𝘰𝘶𝘭𝘥 𝘣𝘦 𝘢𝘣𝘭𝘦 𝘵𝘰 𝘤𝘰𝘮𝘦 𝘪𝘯 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘵𝘢𝘬𝘦 𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘴𝘦 𝘱𝘭𝘢𝘤𝘦𝘴 𝘰𝘷𝘦𝘳” if landlords won’t cooperate — a government land-seizure pitch critics compared to Zohran Mamdani’s platform. Asked at the debate whether Maine should require voter ID, his answer was a flat “𝘕𝘰.”

“I will be her witness. That would translate seré su testigo, and will not appear in your travelers’ phrasebook because it is not a useful phrase for the prudent traveler. Here is what happened: she left one man, she left a second man, she traveled again with the first; she let him die alone. She lost one child to “history” and another to “complications” (I offer in each instance the evaluation of others), she imagined herself capable of shedding that baggage and came to Boca Grande, a tourist. Una turista. So she said. In fact she came here less a tourist than a sojourner but she did not make that distinction. She made not enough distinctions. She dreamed her life. She died, hopeful. In summary. So you know the story. Of course the story had extenuating circumstances, weather, cracked sidewalks and paregorina, but only for the living. Charlotte would call her story one of passion. I believe I would call it one of delusion.”
— Joan Didion, A Book of Common Prayer

text:
🎥 #IranWar #NuclearRisk: The best option is Trump’s humiliating acceptance of defeat and ending the war, but Trump may resort to catastrophic global actions👇👇

👈 Interview of @MarioNawfal with Professor David N. Gibbs (@DavidNGibbs), Professor of History and Political Science at the University of Arizona. He holds a PhD in Political Science from MIT and has written important works on US foreign policy, humanitarian interventions, and political economy; including the books “First Do No Harm: Humanitarian Intervention and the Destruction of Yugoslavia” and “Revolt of the Rich: How the Politics of the 1970s Widened America’s Class Divide.”

✅ 1 – Claims
🔺1.1: Trump has no clear path to anything he can call a victory, and continuing or escalating the war looks more like a desperate reaction.
🔺1.2: The risk of nuclear weapons use increases with continued escalation, and this danger is real.
🔺1.3: The US and Israeli attack has strengthened the logic of those inside Iran who favor building nuclear weapons and has increased the likelihood of Iran moving in that direction.
🔺1.4: The best option is accepting humiliation and exiting the war, because personal humiliation is far less costly than widespread destruction and nuclear risk.
🔺1.5: The war has created severe economic uncertainty which, alongside the Ukraine war and political instability in the West, raises the danger of a major economic crisis.

✅ 2 – Arguments
🔺2.1: Once the war began, exiting it for Trump means accepting defeat and humiliation. Similar to Vietnam, where Johnson, after escalating, could no longer get out because withdrawal equaled defeat. Trump too is inclined toward escalation to avoid humiliation, and there is no honorable way out.
🔺2.2: The attack on Iran’s leadership and the assassination of senior officials opened Pandora’s box. When one side resorts to assassinating leaders, the other side may also resort to the same method. Threats to attack Dimona, assassinate American officials, or destroy infrastructure are plausible under conditions of desperation, and such escalation could lead to an Israeli nuclear response.
🔺2.3: The logic of Iranian hardliners is that North Korea was not attacked because it had nuclear weapons, while Gaddafi was overthrown after abandoning his nuclear program. Continued attacks strengthen this argument and weaken the moderates.
🔺2.4: America’s security umbrella in the Persian Gulf has effectively failed. The presence of bases, instead of creating security, has made the host country a target of attack, and America has been unable to prevent the destruction of infrastructure. This experience reduces the attractiveness of alignment with America.
🔺2.5: Trump has little diplomatic experience and weak emotional control. He has eliminated bearers of bad news and sidelined advisors who offered dissenting opinions. This decision-making environment increases the likelihood of miscalculations.

✅ 3 – Evidence
🔺3.1: Before the war began, Tucker Carlson personally warned Trump that the war would destroy his presidency. Trump did not disagree, but replied, “We’re all going to die anyway.” This response indicates a pre-determined decision and a disturbing attitude.
🔺3.2: America has expended the bulk of its interceptor missiles and, despite a massive military budget, has been unable to keep the Strait of Hormuz open or contain the Houthi threat. Key munitions stocks have been severely depleted.
🔺3.3: Many people close to Trump, even some usually regarded as hawks, oppose continuing the war, but he does not listen to them, and the atmosphere around him is such that people refrain from delivering bad news.
🔺3.4: Rising fuel prices and economic pressure caused by the war have intensified street protests in France, Italy, and other European countries. Gulf states are also dissatisfied with their security situation.
🔺3.5: Iran has so far refrained from a direct attack on Dimona, but the threat of such an attack has been raised. At the same time, there are reports of threats against American officials and vital infrastructure.

✅ 4 – Conclusions
🔺4.1: There is no path by which Trump can achieve through military escalation anything he can call a victory. Continuing the war only produces further destruction.
🔺4.2: The more escalation continues, the greater the likelihood of nuclear weapons use by Israel or America, as well as Iran moving toward building nuclear weapons. This is one of the main legacies of the initial attack.
🔺4.3: The best option is accepting humiliation and exiting the war. Nevertheless, it is unlikely that he will choose this path.
🔺4.4: America is losing its credibility as a guarantor of security, and its global influence is declining. By contrast, China appears to seek de-escalation and the preservation of stability.
🔺4.5: The decision-making environment around Trump is prone to miscalculation and emotional reactions, and this situation has raised the danger of catastrophic decisions.
